title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
皇上嗣大寶之十有九年乃成化
癸卯當天下大比廵按山東
監察御史宋〔經〕預協謀於藩
臬重臣以事在招延簡拔而
去取焉者不可不慎爰闗貢
院嚴小試選文學於衆望杜
===
蹊徑於先幾百物脩明有光
典故于時適真守太監韋〔焕〕雅
重儒術樂相厥成〔恕〕以菲才
與教諭羅〔玄〕錫偕司主試而
分考則教諭袁〔魯〕蔡〔澤〕楊〔頊〕
姜鳳訓導徐〔哲〕張守〔和〕蕭昇
提調監試則左布政使戴〔珙〕
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

皇上嗣大寶之十有九年，乃成化癸卯，當天下大比。廵按山東監察御史宋〔經〕預協謀於藩臬重臣，以事在招延簡拔，而去取焉者不可不慎。爰闗貢院，嚴小試，選文學於衆望，杜蹊徑於先幾，百物脩明，有光典故。于時適真守太監韋〔焕〕雅重儒術，樂相厥成。〔恕〕以菲才，與教諭羅〔玄〕錫偕司主試，而分考則教諭袁〔魯〕、蔡〔澤〕、楊〔頊〕、姜鳳，訓導徐〔哲〕、張守〔和〕、蕭昇。提調監試則左布政使戴〔珙〕、
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

The nineteenth year since His Majesty succeeded to the imperial throne was the guimao year of the Chenghua reign, when the triennial examinations were held throughout the empire. Song Jing, Regional Inspector of Shandong and Investigating Censor, consulted in advance with the senior officials of the provincial administration and surveillance commissions. Since the undertaking involved inviting and selecting worthy men, he considered that the decisions to reject or accept candidates required the utmost care. Accordingly, instructions were sent to the examination compound, preliminary tests were made rigorous, men of literary learning were selected on the basis of public esteem, and avenues of improper access were blocked before they could develop. Every arrangement was put in good order, bringing distinction to established practice. At this time, the resident Grand Eunuch [?], Wei Huan, who had long esteemed Confucian learning, gladly helped bring the undertaking to completion.

Despite my meager abilities, I, Shu, served jointly as Examiner with Instructor Luo Xuanxi. The Associate Examiners were Instructors Yuan Lu, Cai Ze, Yang Xu, and Jiang Feng, and Assistant Instructors Xu Zhe, Zhang Shouhe, and Xiao Sheng. Those responsible for managing and supervising the examination were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Dai Gong, …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
按察使端宏左叅政李昂副
使許進賛襄防範則右布政
使邢表左右叅政張盛劉〔道〕
孫𤩽副使石渠潘〔珏〕夏寅左
右叅議尚絅王道僉事劉璋
羅膺侯恂表端潘禎劉寅至
如内外執事亦皆遴選以充
===
而御史實總莅焉先一日御
史合凡有事矢心以盟且曰
茲弗飭者有如盟僉曰敢不
夙夜以共
天子之休命乃鎖院揭書命題集
頳所選六郡遼陽之士凡一
千二百有奇三試得七十有
punctuated:
按察使端宏、左叅政李昂、副使許進。賛襄防範，則右布政使邢表、左右叅政張盛、劉〔道〕、孫𤩽、副使石渠、潘〔珏〕、夏寅、左右叅議尚絅、王道、僉事劉璋、羅膺、侯恂、表端、潘禎、劉寅。至如内外執事，亦皆遴選以充，而御史實總莅焉。
先一日，御史合凡有事，矢心以盟，且曰：「茲弗飭者，有如盟！」僉曰：「敢不夙夜以共天子之休命！」乃鎖院，揭書命題，集頳所選六郡遼陽之士，凡一千二百有奇，三試得七十有
translation_en:
… Surveillance Commissioner Duan Hong, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Li Ang, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Xu Jin. Assisting with oversight and safeguards were Right Administration Commissioner Xing Biao; Left and Right Administration Vice Commissioners Zhang Sheng, Liu Dao, and Sun Xian [?]; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Shi Qu, Pan Jue, and Xia Yin; Left and Right Administration Assistant Commissioners Shang Jiong and Wang Dao; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Liu Zhang, Luo Ying, Hou Xun, Biao Duan [?], Pan Zhen, and Liu Yin. The personnel serving inside and outside the examination compound were likewise all carefully selected, while the censor exercised overall supervision.
On the preceding day, the censor assembled everyone charged with duties, and they pledged their resolve in an oath. He further declared: “Should anyone fail to observe discipline in this undertaking, let the oath take effect upon him!” They all replied: “How could we dare not labor morning and night to carry out the Son of Heaven’s gracious command!” The examination compound was then locked, and the books were opened to set the questions. The selected scholars from the six prefectures and Liaoyang were assembled [?], numbering more than twelve hundred in all. Through three examination sessions, they selected seventy and …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
五人既錄其氏名與其文之
可類見者將獻諸
天府恕用謹序其端曰化理之術
有二焉曰治道曰治才而已
矣三代以後人君孰不願治
而卒之用人或以誸愽或以
聲望或以詞賦於是有曲學
有虛名有綺縟李毗之習秦
閳有小補焉者哉
===
太祖高皇帝具冠絕神人之見以
天下之化理弗越乎治道治
才而已肆更古科目之制本
之經書以觀其道愽之策論
以盡其才
punctuated:
五人。既錄其氏名與其文之可類見者，將獻諸天府，恕用謹序其端曰：化理之術有二焉，曰治道，曰治才，而已矣。三代以後，人君孰不願治？而卒之用人，或以誸愽，或以聲望，或以詞賦，於是有曲學，有虛名，有綺縟李毗之習，秦閳有小補焉者哉？
太祖高皇帝具冠絕神人之見，以天下之化理弗越乎治道、治才而已，肆更古科目之制，本之經書以觀其道，愽之策論以盡其才。
translation_en:
…five men. Having recorded their names and selected examples of their compositions, we are about to submit these to the imperial repository. I, Shu, therefore respectfully offer these introductory remarks: There are only two means of bringing about moral transformation and good government: the Way of governance and talent for governance. Since the Three Dynasties, what ruler has not desired good government? Yet appointments ultimately came to depend variously on erudition [?], reputation, or skill in verse and rhapsodies. Thus arose distorted learning, empty reputations, and habits of ornate writing [the following characters, 李毗 and 秦閳, are doubtful]. Could these have offered even a little benefit [?]?
Emperor Taizu Gao possessed insight surpassing that of spirits and men. He held that moral transformation and good government throughout the realm depended solely upon the Way of governance and talent for governance. Accordingly, he reformed the old system of examination categories, grounding it in the classics to assess candidates’ understanding of the Way and broadening it through policy essays and discourses to give full scope to their talents.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承率由滋慎百餘年閒□
才輩出於盛矣哉夫諸士子
學聖人之道者也聖人之道
載在六經孔子刪述之以開
詔萬世大賢偉儒相繼發明
微辭奥義皆與經表裏識天
地之心生民之紀萬化萬福
===
之原不可一日委焉者也置
心於此而心正置身於此而
身脩置家於此而家齊舉而
措之於國於天下謂之治道
能舉其國與天下而置之於
此謂之治才外此道而別以
求治則管商之功利申韓□
punctuated:
列聖相承，率由滋慎，百餘年閒，□才輩出，於盛矣哉！夫諸士子，學聖人之道者也。聖人之道，載在六經，孔子刪述之，以開詔萬世。大賢偉儒，相繼發明，微辭奥義，皆與經表裏。識天地之心、生民之紀、萬化萬福之原，不可一日委焉者也。
置心於此而心正，置身於此而身脩，置家於此而家齊，舉而措之於國、於天下，謂之治道。能舉其國與天下而置之於此，謂之治才。外此道而別以求治，則管商之功利、申韓□
translation_en:
…Successive sage emperors have followed one another, adhering to this practice with ever greater care. Over more than a hundred years, talented men [preceding character illegible] have emerged in succession. How flourishing indeed [?]! These examination candidates are men who study the Way of the sages. The Way of the sages is recorded in the Six Classics, which Confucius edited and expounded to enlighten and instruct all future ages. Great worthies and eminent Confucian scholars have successively elucidated them; their subtle expressions and profound meanings complement the Classics. To understand the heart of Heaven and Earth, the ordering principles of human life, and the source of all transformations and blessings is something that must not be set aside for even a single day.
Set the mind upon this, and the mind becomes upright; ground oneself in this, and one’s person becomes cultivated; ground the family in this, and the family becomes well ordered. To extend and apply this to the state and all under Heaven is called the Way of governance. The ability to take one’s state and all under Heaven and establish them upon this is called talent for governance. If one departs from this Way and seeks governance elsewhere, the result is the pursuit of achievement and profit associated with Guan Zhong and Shang Yang, and Shen Buhai and Han Fei [illegible character]…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
刑名漢與唐雜霸雜夷之習
非治也外此才而策之於該
博聲望言語文辭之間則公
孫弘之曲學李元成之虛名
王楊盧駱之浮文非才也故
恐嘗以爲我
國家取士之制曠前古而不可
===
及者此也諸士子遭逢
聖明荷菁莪樂育之化學斯道而
來應賓興而起何其幸也行
用矣所以愛其身重其報當
何如哉其必無內外無崇卑
無險夷終始以如保位靡
道如靡祿恤人言如恤意外
punctuated:
刑名，漢與唐雜霸雜夷之習，非治也。外此才而策之於該博、聲望、言語、文辭之間，則公孫弘之曲學、李元成之虛名、王楊盧駱之浮文，非才也。故恐嘗以爲，我國家取士之制，曠前古而不可及者，此也。
諸士子遭逢聖明，荷菁莪樂育之化，學斯道而來，應賓興而起，何其幸也！行用矣，所以愛其身、重其報，當何如哉？其必無內外，無崇卑，無險夷，終始以如保位，靡道如靡祿，恤人言如恤意外。
translation_en:
…penal administration, and the practices of the Han and Tang, mingling the ways of hegemons and foreign peoples, are not true governance. If one looks beyond this kind of talent and seeks it instead in extensive learning, reputation, speech, and literary composition, then Gongsun Hong’s distorted learning, Li Yuancheng’s empty reputation, and the superficial writings of Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo are not true talent. Thus, I have long thought [?] that this is why our dynasty’s system for selecting officials surpasses all antiquity and cannot be matched.
You candidates have encountered a sage and enlightened ruler and received the transforming influence of his joyful cultivation of talent, celebrated in the Odes’ “Luxuriant Southernwood.” You have come through studying this Way and stepped forward in response to the summons for recommending worthy men as honored guests. How fortunate you are! Soon you will be employed. How, then, should you cherish your persons and take seriously your obligation to repay this favor? Surely, whether serving within the capital or outside it, in high or low office, amid danger or ease, you must from beginning to end … as though safeguarding your position [?], expend the Way as you expend your emoluments [?], and heed what people say as you heed unforeseen events…

Shandong Provincial Examination, Nineteenth Year of Chenghua (1483)

Supervising Official:
Song Jing, Investigating Censor on inspection duty in Shandong, courtesy name Dajing, was a native of Yuzhou, Shanxi, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jichou year.

Proctors:
Dai Gong, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Tingbi, was a native of Biyang County, Henan, and a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.
Li Ang, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Wenju, was a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Examination Inspectors:
Duan Hong, Surveillance Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Zhongren, was a native of Dangtu County, Huguang [?], and a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.
Xu Jin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Jisheng, was a native of Lingbao County, Henan, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Examiners:
Wang Shu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Bingzhong, was a native of Qimen County, Zhili, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the bingzi year.
Luo Xuanxun, Instructor at the Confucian School of Dexing County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Gongxun, was a native of Min County, Fujian, and a tribute student of the jimao year.

Associate Examiners:
Yuan Lu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Qianshan County, Anqing Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Xican, was a native of Jieyang County, Guangdong, and a tribute student of the yiyou year.
Cai Ze, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shanggao County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Juren, was a native of Haiyang County, Guangdong, and a tribute student of the dingyou year.
Yang Fen, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shangcai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Jingzhang, was a native of Yangcheng County, Shanxi, and a tribute student of the dingyou year.
Jiang Feng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shucheng County, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Tingyi, was a native of Tiantai County, Zhejiang, and a tribute student of the dingyou year.
Xu Zhe, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Boxi, was a native of Leping County, Jiangxi, and a tribute student of the xinmao year.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
仰之彌高鑽之彌堅瞻之在前忽焉在後
德爲聖人尊爲天子富有四海之内
可欲之謂善有諸己之謂信充實之謂美
充實而有光輝之謂大大而化之之
謂聖聖而不可知之之謂神
易
中正以觀天下
利貞久於其道也天地之道恒久而不已
也利有攸往終則有始也
===
易簡之善配至德
初率其辭而揆其方既有典常苟非其人
道不虛行
書
帝光天之下至于海隅蒼生萬邦黎獻共
惟帝臣
導弱水至于合黎餘波入于流沙導黑水
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
仰之彌高，鑽之彌堅，瞻之在前，忽焉在後。
德爲聖人，尊爲天子，富有四海之内。
可欲之謂善，有諸己之謂信，充實之謂美，充實而有光輝之謂大，大而化之之謂聖，聖而不可知之之謂神。

易
中正以觀天下。
利貞，久於其道也。天地之道，恒久而不已也。利有攸往，終則有始也。
易簡之善，配至德。
初率其辭而揆其方，既有典常，苟非其人，道不虛行。

書
帝光天之下，至于海隅蒼生，萬邦黎獻，共惟帝臣。
導弱水，至于合黎，餘波入于流沙。導黑水
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
“The more I look up to it, the higher it grows; the more I bore into it, the harder it becomes. I see it before me, and suddenly it is behind me.”
“In virtue he was a sage; in exalted station he was the Son of Heaven; in wealth he possessed all within the Four Seas.”
“What is desirable is called goodness. Possessing it in oneself is called genuineness. Being filled with it is called beauty. Being filled with it and radiating brilliance is called greatness. Being great and transforming others is called sagehood. Being a sage whose workings cannot be fathomed is called spiritual marvel.”

Book of Changes (Yijing)
“Central and correct, he observes all under Heaven.”
“‘It is beneficial to remain steadfast’: this means enduring in one’s way. The way of Heaven and Earth endures forever without ceasing. ‘It is beneficial to have somewhere to go’: an ending is followed by a beginning.”
“The goodness of ease and simplicity matches the highest virtue.”
“At first, follow its words and consider their direction. There are established standards; yet unless there is the right person, the Way does not operate of itself.”

Book of Documents (Shangshu)
“The emperor’s radiance illuminated all beneath Heaven, reaching the common people at the shores of the seas. The many worthy men of the myriad states were all the emperor’s subjects.”
“He channeled the Ruoshui as far as Heli; its remaining waters flowed into the shifting sands. He channeled the Heishui …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
至于三危入于南海
公不敢不敬天之休來相宅其作周匹休
惟敬五刑以成三德一人有慶兆民賴之
詩
以爲酒食以饗以祀以妥以侑以介景福
王公伊濯維豐之垣四方攸同王后維翰
王后烝哉豐水東注維禹之績四方
攸同皇王維辟皇王烝哉
旣明且哲以保其身夙夜匪解以事一人
===
念兹戎功繼序其皇之
春秋
公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕齊侯伐衛
遂伐晉〔襄公二十三年〕
齊人侵我西鄙公追齊師至酅弗及〔僖公二十六年〕
楚師鄭師侵衛〔成公二年〕公會晉侯宋公衛
侯曹伯伐鄭〔□□□□〕□□□□
punctuated:
至于三危，入于南海。

公不敢不敬天之休，來相宅，其作周匹休。

惟敬五刑，以成三德。一人有慶，兆民賴之。

詩

以爲酒食，以饗以祀，以妥以侑，以介景福。

王公伊濯，維豐之垣。四方攸同，王后維翰。王后烝哉！豐水東注，維禹之績。四方攸同，皇王維辟。皇王烝哉！

旣明且哲，以保其身。夙夜匪解，以事一人。

念兹戎功，繼序其皇之。

春秋

公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚。〔僖公四年〕齊侯伐衛，遂伐晉。〔襄公二十三年〕

齊人侵我西鄙，公追齊師至酅，弗及。〔僖公二十六年〕

楚師、鄭師侵衛。〔成公二年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭。〔□□□□〕□□□□
translation_en:
…to Sanwei, entering the Southern Sea.

The Duke dared not fail to honor Heaven’s favor. He came to inspect the site for the capital, that it might bring Zhou blessings matching those of earlier dynasties.

Reverently administer the five punishments so as to perfect the three virtues. When the One Man enjoys blessings, the myriad people benefit from them.

Book of Odes

With these they prepare wine and food, to offer at feasts and sacrifices, to settle the spirits and urge them to partake, and to obtain great blessings.

Illustrious was the king’s achievement: the walls of Feng! The four quarters gathered there; the king was their supporting pillar. How great was the king! The Feng River flows eastward—this was Yu’s achievement. The four quarters gathered there; the august king was their sovereign. How great was the august king!

Both discerning and wise, he preserved his person. From dawn to night he was never remiss in serving the One Man.

Remember these great achievements; carry them on in due succession and magnify them.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The Duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed, and they then attacked Chu. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 The Marquis of Qi attacked Wei and then attacked Jin. 〔Twenty-third year of Duke Xiang.〕

Men of Qi invaded our western borderlands. The Duke pursued the army of Qi as far as Xi but failed to catch it. 〔Twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi.〕

The armies of Chu and Zheng invaded Wei. 〔Second year of Duke Cheng.〕 The Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng. 〔Four illegible characters.〕 [Four illegible characters] …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
許鄭伐許〔并成公三年〕楚子鄭伯伐
宋楚人鄭人侵宋〔并成公十八年〕鄭
師伐宋遂城虎牢〔并襄公二年〕
公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕
禮記
故人者天地之心也五行之端也食味別
聲被色而生者也
日五盥沐稷而靧粱櫛用樿櫛髮晞用象
櫛進禨進羞工乃升歌浴用二巾上
絺下綌出杅履蒯席連用湯履蒲席
===
衣布晞身乃屨進飲
樂則安安則久久則天天則神
閒歌三終合樂三終
第貳場
論
萬世道德宗主
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢章帝詔百官各貢忠誠詔
punctuated:
許，鄭伐許〔并成公三年〕；楚子、鄭伯伐宋，楚人、鄭人侵宋〔并成公十八年〕；鄭師伐宋，遂城虎牢〔并襄公二年〕。
公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕。
禮記
故人者，天地之心也，五行之端也，食味、別聲、被色而生者也。
日五盥，沐稷而靧粱，櫛用樿櫛，髮晞用象櫛，進禨，進羞，工乃升歌。浴用二巾，上絺下綌。出杅，履蒯席，連用湯，履蒲席，衣布晞身，乃屨，進飲。
樂則安，安則久，久則天，天則神。
閒歌三終，合樂三終。
第貳場
論
萬世道德宗主。
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢章帝詔百官各貢忠誠詔。
translation_en:
…Xu; Zheng attacked Xu [?].〔Both in the third year of Duke Cheng.〕 The Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng attacked Song; men of Chu and men of Zheng invaded Song.〔Both in the eighteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 The army of Zheng attacked Song; subsequently, Hulao was fortified.〔Both in the second year of Duke Xiang.〕
The duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu.〔The tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Record of Rites
Thus the human being is the heart of Heaven and Earth, the culmination of the Five Phases: a being who lives by consuming flavors, distinguishing sounds, and being clothed in colors.
Wash the hands five times a day. Wash the hair with millet water and the face with fine millet water. For combing, use a comb of white hardwood; once the hair is dry, use an ivory comb. Serve the drink taken after washing the hair, and serve delicacies; the musicians then ascend and sing. For bathing, use two cloths: fine kudzu cloth for the upper body and coarse kudzu cloth for the lower body. On leaving the tub, step onto a mat of rushes; then use hot water [?], and step onto a mat of cattails. Cover the body with cloth to dry it, then put on shoes and serve a drink.
Joy brings repose; repose brings endurance; endurance brings accord with Heaven; accord with Heaven brings spiritual efficacy.
Perform three complete pieces with singing and instruments alternating, and three complete pieces with singing and instruments together.
Second Session
Discourse
The supreme exemplar of the Way and virtue for all ages.
Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials〔One question from among these categories [?].〕
Compose, in the voice of Emperor Zhang of the Han, an edict commanding all officials to offer their loyalty and sincerity.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以姚元之爲兵部尚書同中書門下
三品誥
擬
賀大有年表
判語五條
增減官文書
私借官車船
僧道拜父母
官員赴調習
斷罪引律令
===
第叁場
策五道
問自古帝王之興必有經世之典以風化
天下垂鑒萬世如典謨訓誥之書是
已洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝條成大誥三編
太宗文皇帝御製孝順事實爲善陰隲二書
punctuated:
擬唐以姚元之爲兵部尚書、同中書門下三品誥。
擬賀大有年表。
判語五條：增減官文書；私借官車船；僧道拜父母；官員赴調習；斷罪引律令。
第叁場
策五道
問：自古帝王之興，必有經世之典，以風化天下，垂鑒萬世，如典謨訓誥之書是已。洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝條成《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝御製《孝順事實》《爲善陰隲》二書，
translation_en:
Draft an investiture proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Yao Yuanzhi as Minister of War and Grand Councilor (tong Zhongshu Menxia sanpin).
Draft a memorial congratulating the emperor on an abundant harvest.
Five legal judgments: adding to or deleting from official documents; privately borrowing government carts or boats; Buddhist monks and Daoist priests bowing to their parents; officials proceeding to reassignment or training [?]; citing statutes and ordinances when adjudicating crimes.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: Whenever emperors and kings have arisen since antiquity, they have invariably possessed canonical writings for ordering the world, through which to transform all under Heaven by moral influence and provide a mirror for myriad generations. Such are the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements in the Book of Documents. We reverently reflect that Emperor Taizu Gao of our dynasty compiled the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) in three collections, and Emperor Taizong Wen personally composed the two books Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi) and Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Weishan Yinzhi), …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
宣宗章皇帝釆輯經傳纂爲五倫一書皆欲天
下後世曉然知大經所在真古
帝王以善養人之盛心也其間大旨果有同歟
抑與典謨訓誥相表裏歟大經所在
莫重於人倫也請以五倫之一二質
之除秦苛害而約法三章慮民溝壑
而議貸賑貸授之君道何如知效君
命而喪首不顧恪守忠義而斷舌不
恤律之臣道何如集家誡書於屏風
===
以儉約率其子弟受之而能勞矣貸
錢以葬父傭身以養母貧不可爲孝
乎處田野相敬如賓翁十年不娶媵
媵德何盛也入帷剔目以明無貳引
斧斷臂以示不辱節何壯也以至處
兄弟或友愛甚篤或並敦義讓待朋
友或同席而食或分屋而居是皆能
篤乎倫理者也其人其事可一一而
指陳歟其人之行爲之
punctuated: 宣宗章皇帝釆輯經傳，纂爲《五倫》一書，皆欲天下後世曉然知大經所在，真古帝王以善養人之盛心也。其間大旨果有同歟？抑與典謨訓誥相表裏歟？大經所在，莫重於人倫也。請以五倫之一二質之：除秦苛害而約法三章，慮民溝壑而議貸賑貸，授之君道何如？知效君命而喪首不顧，恪守忠義而斷舌不恤，律之臣道何如？集家誡書於屏風，以儉約率其子弟，受之而能勞矣；貸錢以葬父，傭身以養母，貧不可爲孝乎？處田野，相敬如賓，翁十年不娶媵，媵德何盛也！入帷剔目以明無貳，引斧斷臂以示不辱，節何壯也！以至處兄弟，或友愛甚篤，或並敦義讓；待朋友，或同席而食，或分屋而居。是皆能篤乎倫理者也。其人其事，可一一而指陳歟？其人之行爲之
translation_en:
… Emperor Xuanzong Zhang selected material from the classics and their commentaries and compiled it into a book, The Five Human Relationships (Wulun). All sought to enable everyone under Heaven and in later generations to understand clearly where the great guiding principles lay. This truly embodied the generous intention of the ancient sage rulers to nurture people through goodness. Were the principal intentions of these works indeed the same? Or did they complement the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements? Among the matters governed by the great guiding principles, none is weightier than human relationships. Let us examine one or two examples from The Five Human Relationships.

One abolished Qin’s harsh and harmful measures and reduced the laws to three articles; another, fearing that the people would perish in ditches and ravines, proposed loans and relief [?]. How do these measure up to the way of a ruler [?]? One knew to carry out his ruler’s commands, heedless of losing his head; another steadfastly upheld loyalty and righteousness, undeterred by having his tongue cut out. How do these measure up to the way of a minister?

One collected family admonitions and inscribed them on a screen, leading his sons and younger kinsmen by an example of frugality; receiving this instruction, they were able to undertake toil [?]. One borrowed money to bury his father; another hired himself out to support his mother. Does poverty make filial conduct impossible? Living in the countryside, a couple treated each other with the respect accorded to guests; an old man went ten years without taking a concubine [?]. How abundant was the concubine’s virtue [?]! One entered the bedchamber and gouged out her eye to demonstrate undivided fidelity; another took an axe and severed her arm to show that she would not suffer dishonor. How heroic was their integrity!

As for relations among brothers, some showed exceptionally deep affection, while others alike cultivated righteousness and deference. In their treatment of friends, some ate together on the same mat, while others shared their dwelling. All these were people who faithfully upheld the proper human relationships. Can you identify these people and recount their deeds one by one? As for these people’s conduct and their practice of it [?] …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
三詁二書中有可比倫者歟願著於篇以觀博
通之學
閩地誌之有名宦人物也尚矣昔所以紀
一時之人才而因以見世道之隆汙
非細故也山東古重地也其名宦人
物固不可以僂數然姑問一二用啓
諸士子尚友之心可乎其名宦有仁
惠澤人而去為老幼所留有恩信綏
盜而政為天下第一者果何人歟有
===
分導水勢而民賴以安有請弛鹽禁
而歲豐乃復者抑何人歟秩滿代去
而絕橋以留去官十年而立碑以頌
德何深也閉閣自責而吏不忍欺內
嚴備禦而寇尋引去政何善也他若
不貴刑罰而為仲淹所薦惟尚寬厚
而為夷簡所賢者可指歟嘗斷究獄
而郡中稱為神明事至即決而姓名
書於殿柱者可詳歟其人物有負薪
punctuated:
三詁二書中有可比倫者歟？願著於篇，以觀博通之學。

閩地誌之有名宦人物也，尚矣。昔所以紀一時之人才，而因以見世道之隆汙，非細故也。山東古重地也，其名宦人物固不可以僂數。然姑問一二，用啓諸士子尚友之心，可乎？其名宦，有仁惠澤人而去為老幼所留，有恩信綏盜而政為天下第一者，果何人歟？有分導水勢而民賴以安，有請弛鹽禁而歲豐乃復者，抑何人歟？秩滿代去而絕橋以留，去官十年而立碑以頌，德何深也！閉閣自責而吏不忍欺，內嚴備禦而寇尋引去，政何善也！他若不貴刑罰而為仲淹所薦，惟尚寬厚而為夷簡所賢者，可指歟？嘗斷究獄而郡中稱為神明，事至即決而姓名書於殿柱者，可詳歟？其人物，有負薪
translation_en:
…are there comparable examples in the “three exegeses and two books” [?]? Set them forth in your essay, so that we may see the breadth and depth of your learning.

The inclusion of distinguished officials and notable persons in the geographical records of Min [?] is a longstanding practice. In the past, this served to record the talented men of an age and thereby reveal the flourishing or decline of the moral order. This was no minor matter. Shandong has been an important region since antiquity; its distinguished officials and notable persons are assuredly too numerous to count. Yet may we ask about one or two, to awaken in you candidates the desire to befriend the worthy of the past?

Among its distinguished officials, one benefited the people through benevolence and kindness, and young and old sought to detain him when he departed; another pacified bandits through favor and good faith, and his administration was ranked first in the empire. Who indeed were they? One divided and channeled the flow of water, securing the people’s safety; another requested the relaxation of the salt prohibition and restored it only when the harvest was plentiful. Who were they?

When one completed his term and was leaving upon replacement, the people cut off the bridge to keep him there; ten years after another left office, they erected a stele to praise him. How profound was their virtue! One shut himself in his chamber and reproached himself, so that his subordinate officials could not bear to deceive him; another strengthened internal defenses, and the raiders soon withdrew. How excellent was their administration!

Can you identify the others, such as the man who placed little value on punishments and was recommended by Zhongyan, and the man who esteemed only leniency and generosity and was judged worthy by Yijian? Can you give detailed accounts of the man who investigated and adjudicated legal cases and was acclaimed throughout the commandery as divinely perceptive, and the man who decided matters as soon as they arose and whose name was inscribed on a palace pillar? Among its notable persons, there was one who carried firewood…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
讀誦而以儒行見稱有躬耕徂徠而
以易經教授者誰歟有父子同時謝
事而時有二踈之比有兄弟同日拜
官而世有兩鳳之稱者又誰歟九歲
能文文章獨步于當時才何高也八
十二登第姓名獨冠于天下志何堅
也他若有人呼爲皂鵰者稱自號爲
垂崖者有稱爲謝顏子者有號爲韓
夫子者其故何由或名爲墮淚碑或
號爲棠棣碑或圖形麒麟閣或繪像
凌煙閣其功安在諸士子生長是邦
聞之稔矣然而所願學者在是歟抑
別有其人歟幸明以告我毋謙之曰
未能
===
問安上治民莫善於禮禮固君子所當講
也有虞命伯夷典三禮周官大宗伯
以五禮經邦國王制司徒脩六禮以
節民性曰三禮五禮六禮其制可得
punctuated:
讀誦而以儒行見稱，有躬耕徂徠而以易經教授者，誰歟？有父子同時謝事而時有二踈之比，有兄弟同日拜官而世有兩鳳之稱者，又誰歟？九歲能文，文章獨步于當時，才何高也！八十二登第，姓名獨冠于天下，志何堅也！他若有人呼爲皂鵰者，稱自號爲垂崖者，有稱爲謝顏子者，有號爲韓夫子者，其故何由？或名爲墮淚碑，或號爲棠棣碑，或圖形麒麟閣，或繪像凌煙閣，其功安在？諸士子生長是邦，聞之稔矣。然而所願學者在是歟？抑別有其人歟？幸明以告我，毋謙之曰未能。

問：安上治民，莫善於禮。禮固君子所當講也。有虞命伯夷典三禮，《周官》大宗伯以五禮經邦國，《王制》司徒脩六禮以節民性。曰三禮、五禮、六禮，其制可得
translation_en:
…who read and recited and was renowned for his Confucian conduct; and there was one who farmed at Culai and taught the Book of Changes. Who were they? There were a father and son who retired from office together and were compared in their day to the two Shus; there were also brothers appointed to office on the same day whom the world called the “two phoenixes.” Who were they? One could compose literary works at nine, and his writing was unrivaled in his time—how great his talent! Another passed the examination at eighty-two, his name ranking first throughout the realm—how steadfast his resolve! As for the one people called the “Black Eagle,” the one said to have styled himself “Chuǐyá” (“Hanging Cliff”) [?], the one called “Xie’s Master Yan,” and the one known as “Master Han,” how did these names arise? Some were commemorated by what was named the “Stele of Falling Tears” or called the “Stele of the Cherry Trees”; others had their likenesses depicted in the Qilin Pavilion or their portraits painted in the Lingyan Pavilion. What meritorious deeds had they performed? You examination candidates grew up in this region and have heard these accounts well and often. Yet are those whom you wish to emulate among these men, or are there others? Kindly tell me clearly; do not modestly say that you cannot.

Question: For securing those above and governing the people, nothing surpasses ritual. Ritual is certainly something the gentleman should study. The ruler of Youyu commanded Bo Yi to oversee the Three Rites. In the Offices of Zhou, the Minister of Rites orders the states through the Five Rites; in “Royal Regulations,” the Minister of Education cultivates the Six Rites to regulate the people’s dispositions. As for what are called the Three Rites, Five Rites, and Six Rites, can their institutions be…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
而言歟禮器謂經禮三百曲禮三千
其三百之目三千之條可槩舉其一二歟
歟漢初叔孫通制禮其效至於羣臣
震恐無敢諠譁者視古禮同歟異歟
唐有開元顯慶二禮宋有開寶及政
和五禮其視叔孫通之制何者爲近
古歟禮制莫善於古而人之議者往
往謂古禮不宜行於後世何歟晦庵
朱子盖嘗論之矣豈無歸一之說歟
===
皇明以禮治天下有
令有
制有職掌孝慈諸書皆萬世不刊之典而又
敕天下臣民冠昏喪祭得用朱子家禮禮制
可謂備矣天下守之如一國國守之
如一家家守之如一人漢唐以下何
足彷彿其萬一哉諸士子服習有年
試舉其一二以見
今日之盛焉
punctuated:
而言歟？《禮器》謂經禮三百，曲禮三千，其三百之目、三千之條，可槩舉其一二歟？歟？漢初叔孫通制禮，其效至於羣臣震恐，無敢諠譁者，視古禮同歟異歟？唐有開元、顯慶二禮，宋有開寶及政和五禮，其視叔孫通之制，何者爲近古歟？禮制莫善於古，而人之議者往往謂古禮不宜行於後世，何歟？晦庵朱子盖嘗論之矣，豈無歸一之說歟？
皇明以禮治天下，有《令》，有《制》，有《職掌》《孝慈》諸書，皆萬世不刊之典。而又敕天下臣民冠昏喪祭得用《朱子家禮》，禮制可謂備矣。天下守之如一國，國守之如一家，家守之如一人，漢唐以下何足彷彿其萬一哉！諸士子服習有年，試舉其一二，以見今日之盛焉。
translation_en:
…and be explained? The chapter “Ritual Vessels” (Liqi) speaks of three hundred fundamental rites and three thousand detailed observances. Can you briefly cite one or two of these three hundred categories and three thousand provisions? [The transcription repeats the interrogative particle here: 歟歟.] In the early Han, Shusun Tong established rituals whose effect was such that all the assembled officials trembled in fear, and none dared make a commotion. Were these the same as ancient rites, or different? The Tang had the two ritual codes of the Kaiyuan and Xianqing eras, and the Song had those of the Kaibao era and the Five Rites of the Zhenghe Era. Compared with Shusun Tong’s institutions, which came closer to antiquity? No ritual institutions surpass those of antiquity; yet those who discuss the matter frequently say that ancient rites are unsuitable for practice in later ages. Why is this? Master Zhu, known as Hui’an, once discussed this. Is there no explanation that reconciles these views?
Our august Ming governs All under Heaven through ritual. There are the Ordinances, the Regulations, and such books as Duties of Offices and Filial Piety and Compassion, all authoritative codes that shall remain unaltered for ten thousand generations. Furthermore, an imperial command permits officials and commoners throughout the realm to use Master Zhu’s Family Rituals for capping ceremonies, weddings, funerals, and sacrifices. The ritual institutions may indeed be called complete. All under Heaven observes them as though it were a single state; a state observes them as though it were a single household; and a household observes them as though it were a single person. How could the Han, Tang, or subsequent dynasties approximate even a ten-thousandth of this achievement? You scholars have practiced and studied these rites for years. Cite one or two examples to demonstrate the flourishing accomplishments of the present age.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
問自古列國皆有史春秋亦魯史也筆削
於聖人而成經不可尚已後世之爲
史者舍春秋將何法乎自漢而下若
司馬遷之史記或稱其有良史才或
稱其爲實錄其果有合於春秋之旨
歟或又譏其是非頗謬於聖人然歟
否歟班固范曄陳壽之徒相繼而作
說者謂其皆依倣遷法而爲之者也
其果然歟抑有出於遷之外歟歐陽
===
脩作五代史每篇必以嗚呼發之其
有意歟其傳八篇名義亦各有所指
歟脩學孔子者其書法有得於春秋
之遺意歟論者謂其功不在司馬遷
下抑果然歟既以爲不在遷下又謂
其紀例精密非遷所及何言之戾歟
朱子作通鑑綱目識者以爲深得春
秋之法固無庸議矣然其義果安在
歟請詳言之以觀諸士子考古之學
punctuated: 問：自古列國皆有史，《春秋》亦魯史也。筆削於聖人而成經，不可尚已。後世之爲史者，舍《春秋》將何法乎？自漢而下，若司馬遷之《史記》，或稱其有良史才，或稱其爲實錄，其果有合於《春秋》之旨歟？或又譏其是非頗謬於聖人，然歟？否歟？班固、范曄、陳壽之徒相繼而作，說者謂其皆依倣遷法而爲之者也。其果然歟？抑有出於遷之外歟？歐陽脩作《五代史》，每篇必以「嗚呼」發之，其有意歟？其傳八篇，名義亦各有所指歟？脩學孔子者，其書法有得於《春秋》之遺意歟？論者謂其功不在司馬遷下，抑果然歟？既以爲不在遷下，又謂其紀例精密，非遷所及，何言之戾歟？朱子作《通鑑綱目》，識者以爲深得《春秋》之法，固無庸議矣。然其義果安在歟？請詳言之，以觀諸士子考古之學。
translation_en:
Question: From antiquity, the various states all had historical records; the Spring and Autumn Annals, too, was a history of Lu. Through the Sage’s revisions and deletions, it became a classic that cannot be surpassed. What, then, should later writers of history take as their model if they abandon the Spring and Autumn Annals? From the Han onward, consider Sima Qian’s Records of the Historian: some praise him for possessing the talents of a fine historian, while others praise his work as a truthful record. Does it indeed accord with the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals? Others criticize his judgments of right and wrong as diverging considerably from those of the Sage. Is this so, or not? Ban Gu, Fan Ye, Chen Shou, and others produced their works in succession. Commentators say that they all wrote by following Sima Qian’s methods. Is this really so? Or did they go beyond him in some respects?

When Ouyang Xiu wrote the History of the Five Dynasties, he invariably introduced each piece with “Alas!” Did he have a particular intention in doing so? Do the titles of its eight biographical sections likewise each carry a particular significance? As Xiu was a student of Confucius, did his manner of writing capture something of the meaning bequeathed by the Spring and Autumn Annals? Critics say that his achievement was no less than Sima Qian’s. Is this indeed so? Having judged him no less accomplished than Sima Qian, they also say that the precision and rigor of his annalistic conventions were beyond Sima Qian’s reach. Why are their statements at odds?

Master Zhu composed the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror. Discerning readers consider it to have profoundly grasped the methods of the Spring and Autumn Annals; this surely requires no debate. But where, precisely, does its significance lie? Please explain in detail, so that we may assess your learning in the study of antiquity.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
問自古無不弊之法非法弊也行之不善
斯弊矣君子起而救之法固在也方今
朝廷清明法無不善奚容以私議然其中亦
有所當講者請商之夫理國莫急於
財用今租稅之入未嘗有盈縮也而
用或不足何歟豈所出者過所入歟
當承平而人物夥矣兵甲盛矣用果
得已歟伊欲不加賦而用足其術何
===
繇平政莫先於賦役今有司之法未
嘗無差等也而民多逋負何歟豈所
取者過所有歟居中國而有人倫也
有國用也事果得已歟伊欲不變法
而政平其道何自盜非不治也而攘
奪之風尚未能息欲里不閧桴鼓不
何法而可荒非不救也而水旱之災
卒不能禦欲道不見流殍行何政而
得學校本以明教化然攻異端者尚
punctuated: 問：自古無不弊之法，非法弊也，行之不善，斯弊矣。君子起而救之，法固在也。方今朝廷清明，法無不善，奚容以私議？然其中亦有所當講者，請商之。夫理國莫急於財用，今租稅之入未嘗有盈縮也，而用或不足，何歟？豈所出者過所入歟？當承平而人物夥矣，兵甲盛矣，用果得已歟？伊欲不加賦而用足，其術何繇？平政莫先於賦役，今有司之法未嘗無差等也，而民多逋負，何歟？豈所取者過所有歟？居中國而有人倫也，有國用也，事果得已歟？伊欲不變法而政平，其道何自？盜非不治也，而攘奪之風尚未能息，欲里不閧，桴鼓不，何法而可？荒非不救也，而水旱之災卒不能禦，欲道不見流殍，行何政而得？學校本以明教化，然攻異端者尚
translation_en:
Question: Since antiquity, no law has been free from abuses. It is not the law itself that is defective: abuses arise when it is poorly administered. A gentleman steps forward to remedy them, while the law itself remains intact. Today the court is enlightened, and all its laws are good. How could there be room for private criticism? Nevertheless, there are matters within them that warrant discussion; let us consider these.

In governing a state, nothing is more urgent than its finances. Revenue from rents and taxes has not fluctuated, yet funds sometimes fall short. Why is this? Could expenditure exceed income? In a time of enduring peace, people and goods are abundant, and troops and armaments are plentiful. Can such expenditure really be dispensed with? If we wish to make funds sufficient without increasing taxes, by what means can this be achieved?

In making government equitable, nothing takes precedence over taxes and labor services. The regulations administered by the responsible officials have always provided for graded assessments, yet many commoners fall into arrears. Why is this? Could what is exacted exceed what they possess? Living in the Central Kingdom, we have the obligations of human relationships and the expenses of the state. Can these matters really be dispensed with? If we wish to make government equitable without changing the laws, what course should we follow?

It is not that robbery goes unpunished, yet the practice of plunder and seizure has still not been suppressed. What measures could ensure that villages suffer no disturbances and that the watch drums do not [sound the alarm?] [?]? It is not that famine goes unrelieved, yet disasters of flood and drought ultimately cannot be warded off. What policies could ensure that no displaced people who have died of starvation are seen along the roads? Schools were established to make moral instruction clear, yet those who pursue heterodox teachings still…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
有若何而使士皆崇德重行純然道
義之正歟鄉飲本以敦和睦然習流
頹者不無若何而使民知禮向義翕
然淳厚之風歟諸士子負有用之才
應簡興而至於是數者必講之熟矣
幸爲我陳之用將採擇而獻於
上
punctuated: 有。若何而使士皆崇德重行，純然道義之正歟？鄉飲本以敦和睦，然習流頹者不無，若何而使民知禮向義，翕然淳厚之風歟？諸士子負有用之才，應簡興而至，於是數者必講之熟矣。幸爲我陳之，用將採擇而獻於上。
translation_en: …still exist. How can scholars all be brought to esteem virtue and value conduct, adhering wholly to what is correct in the Way and righteousness? The village drinking ceremony was originally intended to foster harmony and concord, yet there are still those whose habits have become debased. How can the people be brought to understand ritual propriety and turn toward righteousness, united in an ethos of sincerity and generosity? You examination candidates possess talents suited to practical service and have come here in response to selection and recommendation. You must surely have studied these several matters thoroughly. Kindly set forth your views for me, so that I may select from them and present them to His Majesty.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
或可及也然而高不可階仰之愈見其高莫得
而及焉嘗致力以鑽之意其或可入也然而堅
不可磷鑽之愈見其堅莫得而入焉高焉莫及
堅焉莫入其無窮盡也如此是豈可以人力至
耶又嘗即而瞻之恍然若見其參於吾前似以
爲不及矣非不及也弗得其真而不及耳忽焉
又見其在於吾後似有所過也非過也弗得其
妙而過耳前焉莫據後焉莫依其無方體也如
此又豈可以形象求耶噫非顏子深有所得安
===
能述其先難之故而嘆之親切若是哉雖然聖
人之道果終不可至耶博文約禮則聖人之所
以教而顏子所以得至乎聖人之域者也學者
果由是而學焉卓爾之地可馴至矣故曰聖人
可學而至
德爲聖人尊爲天子富有四海之內
胡鰲
同考試官訓導張　批　是作本大孝立說詞
不浮而理自到表而出之允當
punctuated:
或可及也，然而高不可階，仰之愈見其高，莫得而及焉。嘗致力以鑽之，意其或可入也，然而堅不可磷，鑽之愈見其堅，莫得而入焉。高焉莫及，堅焉莫入，其無窮盡也如此，是豈可以人力至耶？又嘗即而瞻之，恍然若見其參於吾前，似以爲不及矣。非不及也，弗得其真而不及耳。忽焉又見其在於吾後，似有所過也。非過也，弗得其妙而過耳。前焉莫據，後焉莫依，其無方體也如此，又豈可以形象求耶？噫！非顏子深有所得，安能述其先難之故，而嘆之親切若是哉？雖然，聖人之道果終不可至耶？博文約禮，則聖人之所以教，而顏子所以得至乎聖人之域者也。學者果由是而學焉，卓爾之地可馴至矣。故曰：「聖人可學而至。」

德爲聖人，尊爲天子，富有四海之內。
胡鰲。
同考試官訓導張，批：是作本大孝立說，詞不浮而理自到，表而出之允當。
translation_en:
…perhaps it could be reached. Yet its height admits of no ascending by steps: the more I look up to it, the higher it appears, beyond all reach. I once applied myself to boring into it, thinking that perhaps I could penetrate it. Yet its hardness cannot be worn away: the more I bore into it, the harder it appears, beyond all penetration. So high that it cannot be reached, so hard that it cannot be penetrated—such is its inexhaustibility. How could it be attained by human effort? I also once approached and gazed upon it, dimly seeming to see it standing before me, as though I had fallen short of it. It is not truly a matter of falling short: I merely fail to grasp its reality and thus fall short. Suddenly I see it behind me again, as though I had gone beyond it. It is not truly a matter of surpassing it: I merely fail to grasp its subtlety and thus overshoot it. Before me, it affords no foothold; behind me, it offers no support. Such is its lack of fixed location or form. How, then, could it be sought through images and shapes? Ah! Had Master Yan not gained a profound understanding, how could he have described the reasons for his earlier difficulties and expressed his wonder so intimately? Nevertheless, is the Way of the sage ultimately unattainable? Broadening learning through cultural refinement and restraining conduct through ritual propriety were the means by which the sage taught and Master Yan attained the sage’s realm. If learners truly follow this course of study, they may gradually reach that lofty eminence. Thus it is said: “One can become a sage through learning.”

“In virtue he was a sage; in dignity, the Son of Heaven; in wealth, he possessed all within the Four Seas.”
By Hu Ao.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: This essay grounds its argument in supreme filial piety. Its language is not superficial, and its reasoning naturally reaches the point. It is entirely fitting to single it out for publication.

德盛位尊而尊有天下此聖人之大孝也蓋孝
莫大乎有德有位有天下也大舜無而有之非
大孝而何哉中庸引孔子稱舜之孝以明斯道
之實如此吾想其意以為凡有德者皆可以顯
親也舜之德濬哲文明首出乎庶物溫恭允塞
===
卓冠乎羣倫其德則聖人之德也德而至於聖
人德之至也以聖人為之子顯其親為聖人之
親其顯之也至矣凡有位者皆可以尊親也舜
之位恭己南面臨御乎萬方曆數在躬宰制乎
羣動其位則天子之位也位而至於天子尊之
極也以天子為之子尊其親為天子之親其尊

同考試官教諭袁批〔順不平易場中作者類〕多陳腐，殊無討人意，看理明詞順，僅見此篇。

德盛位尊，而尊有天下，此聖人之大孝也。蓋孝莫大乎有德、有位、有天下也。大舜無而有之，非大孝而何哉？《中庸》引孔子稱舜之孝，以明斯道之實如此。吾想其意，以為凡有德者皆可以顯親也。舜之德，濬哲文明，首出乎庶物；溫恭允塞，卓冠乎羣倫。其德則聖人之德也。德而至於聖人，德之至也。以聖人為之子，顯其親為聖人之親，其顯之也至矣。凡有位者皆可以尊親也。舜之位，恭己南面，臨御乎萬方；曆數在躬，宰制乎羣動。其位則天子之位也。位而至於天子，尊之極也。以天子為之子，尊其親為天子之親，其尊之也極矣。以至凡有祿者，況亦可以養其親，而舜之富，尺地莫非其有，惟正之供；率土之民莫非其臣，方物之畢獻。其富□□□□之□□□□至

Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔“Fluent but not plain [?]. Among those writing in the examination hall, most…”〕 “…are stale and conventional, with scarcely anything to engage the reader [?]. For clear reasoning and fluent expression, I have seen only this piece.”

Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔“It brings out the substance of great filial piety and merits selection.”〕

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔“Not misled by divergent interpretations. Select it.”〕

Abundant virtue, exalted rank, and the dignity of possessing all under Heaven: these constitute the sage’s great filial piety. For no filial piety is greater than possessing virtue, holding rank, and possessing all under Heaven. The great Shun came to possess these from having none. If this is not great filial piety, what is? The Doctrine of the Mean quotes Confucius’s praise of Shun’s filial piety to show that the substance of this Way is thus. As I consider its meaning, I take it that all who possess virtue can bring distinction to their parents. Shun’s virtue was profound in wisdom and brilliant in cultivation, placing him foremost among all beings; he was gentle, reverent, sincere, and fully accomplished, standing preeminent among his fellows. His virtue was the virtue of a sage. When virtue reaches sagehood, it has reached its utmost. Having a sage as their son brings distinction to his parents as the parents of a sage: the distinction he brings them is supreme.

All who hold rank can bring honor to their parents. In his station, Shun maintained a reverent bearing and faced south, ruling over the myriad regions; Heaven’s appointed succession rested upon his person, and he governed all living beings. His station was that of the Son of Heaven. To attain the station of Son of Heaven is to reach the pinnacle of honor. Having the Son of Heaven as their son honors his parents as the parents of the Son of Heaven: the honor he brings them is supreme.

Furthermore, all who receive an official stipend can also support their parents. As for Shun’s wealth, not a foot of land lay outside his possession, providing the regular dues; none of the people throughout the realm were other than his subjects, presenting all their local products. title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
於四海富之極也養其親以四海之養其養之
也無以加矣視彼以一家一國而養者何如哉
德則聖人尊則天子富則四海舜之孝茲其所
以為大也歟不特此耳下文有曰宗廟饗之子
孫保之則舜之大孝又上格于宗祖下延及于
子孫矣舜惟矣求其有德有位享有天下而繼
舜之大孝者今有
聖天子在上
可欲之謂善有諸己之謂信充實之謂美
充實而有光輝之謂大大而化之之
謂聖聖而不可知之之謂神
同考試官教諭蔡　批　場中作此者多矣〔昧善信庶分截殊失本旨獨此篇一理貫講不涉陳腐可愛可愛〕
高達
===
考試官教諭羅　批　融會傳註成文佳作也
考試官教諭汪　批　一意貫說合旨
由一理而馴致其極隨所至而歷著其名蓋自
善信以至於聖神其理一而已矣大賢歷著其
punctuated:
於四海，富之極也。養其親以四海之養，其養之也無以加矣。視彼以一家一國而養者，何如哉？德則聖人，尊則天子，富則四海，舜之孝，茲其所以為大也歟！不特此耳，下文有曰：「宗廟饗之，子孫保之。」則舜之大孝，又上格于宗祖，下延及于子孫矣。舜惟矣。求其有德有位、享有天下而繼舜之大孝者，今有聖天子在上。

可欲之謂善，有諸己之謂信，充實之謂美，充實而有光輝之謂大，大而化之之謂聖，聖而不可知之之謂神。

translation_en:
…extending to all within the Four Seas: this is the utmost wealth. Supporting his parents with the resources of the Four Seas, he could add nothing further to their support. How does this compare with those who support their parents with the resources of a single household or state? In virtue, a sage; in exalted position, the Son of Heaven; in wealth, possessing the Four Seas—was this not what made Shun’s filial piety great? Nor was this all. The text below says: “The ancestral temples received his offerings, and his descendants preserved them.” Thus Shun’s great filial piety reached upward to his ancestors and extended downward to his descendants. Shun indeed [?]. If we seek one who possesses virtue and rank, holds all under Heaven, and succeeds to Shun’s great filial piety, today we have the sagely Son of Heaven above us.

“What is desirable is called good; possessing it within oneself is called genuine; being fully endowed with it is called beautiful; being fully endowed with it and radiating brilliance is called great; being great and transforming others is called sagely; being sagely and beyond comprehension is called divine.”

This essay alone explains the passage through one unifying principle, without lapsing into stale formulations. Admirable, admirable!〕

Gao Da

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
名義以告時人得非欲因之以曉門人也歟昔
孟子因浩生不害未喻樂正子善信之意於是
告之若曰天下之理善者必可欲惡者必可惡
其為人也可欲而不可惡此所謂善人也天下
之人好善未必實惡惡未必誠其於善也皆實
有之如惡惡臭如好好色此所謂信人也力行
其善至於充滿而積實清和而純懿則美在其
中而無待於外矣不謂之美乎充積其善至於
和順積中而英華發外暢於四肢而發於事業
===
則德業至盛而不可加矣不謂之大乎大而能
化使其大者泯然無迹則不思不勉從容中道
而非人力所能為矣非聖而何聖不可知則出
之至妙無聲無臭有非耳目所能盡心思所能
測不可得而名矣非神而何吁孟子因論善信
而歷言及此其所以著明造道之義無餘蘊矣
雖然理一也善非粗淺神非高虛由善而神顧
擴充之何如耳使樂正子因孟子之言而加擴
充之功則由善信而美而大而聖神也不難矣
punctuated: 名義，以告時人，得非欲因之以曉門人也歟？昔孟子因浩生不害未喻樂正子善信之意，於是告之若曰：「天下之理，善者必可欲，惡者必可惡。其為人也，可欲而不可惡，此所謂善人也。天下之人，好善未必實，惡惡未必誠。其於善也，皆實有之，如惡惡臭，如好好色，此所謂信人也。力行其善，至於充滿而積實，清和而純懿，則美在其中而無待於外矣，不謂之美乎？充積其善，至於和順積中而英華發外，暢於四肢而發於事業，則德業至盛而不可加矣，不謂之大乎？大而能化，使其大者泯然無迹，則不思不勉，從容中道，而非人力所能為矣，非聖而何？聖不可知，則出之至妙，無聲無臭，有非耳目所能盡、心思所能測，不可得而名矣，非神而何？」吁！孟子因論善信而歷言及此，其所以著明造道之義，無餘蘊矣。雖然，理一也，善非粗淺，神非高虛，由善而神，顧擴充之何如耳。使樂正子因孟子之言而加擴充之功，則由善信而美而大而聖神也，不難矣。
translation_en:
…the meanings of these designations, to instruct the people of his time—might he not have wished thereby to enlighten his disciples? Formerly, because Haosheng Buhai did not understand what it meant to call Yuezhengzi good and genuine, Mengzi instructed him, as if saying: “According to the principles of the world, what is good must be desirable, and what is evil must be detestable. Someone whose character is desirable and not detestable is what we call a good person. Among the people of the world, a fondness for goodness is not necessarily substantial, nor is hatred of evil necessarily sincere. Someone who truly possesses goodness within himself, as naturally as he hates a foul smell or loves a beautiful sight, is what we call a genuine person. When he earnestly practices this goodness until it fills him and accumulates in substance, becoming clear and harmonious, pure and excellent, beauty then resides within him and depends on nothing external. Do we not call this beautiful? When he fills himself with goodness and accumulates it until harmony and accord gather within and their splendid flowering appears without, suffusing his four limbs and manifesting itself in his undertakings, his virtue and achievements reach their utmost flourishing, beyond which nothing can be added. Do we not call this great? When, having become great, he can undergo transformation, so that his greatness leaves no discernible trace, he accords effortlessly with the Way, without deliberation or exertion. This is beyond what human effort can accomplish. What could this be but sagehood? When his sagehood cannot be fathomed, what issues from him is supremely subtle, without sound or smell. There is something here that ears and eyes cannot fully apprehend and thought cannot measure; it cannot be named. What could this be but spiritual?”

Ah! Starting with a discussion of goodness and genuineness, Mengzi proceeded through these successive stages. In elucidating the meaning of advancing in the Way, he left nothing unexplained. Nevertheless, the principle is one: goodness is neither crude nor shallow, and the spiritual is neither remote nor empty. Progressing from goodness to the spiritual depends only on how one extends and develops that goodness. If Yuezhengzi were to take Mengzi’s words as his guide and further exert himself in extending and developing it, then advancing from goodness and genuineness to beauty, greatness, sagehood, and the spiritual would not be difficult.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
慣乎樂正子猶在善信之間即其從乎敎一事
觀之則其有諸己者尚未實也噫
易
中正以觀天下
高晝達
同考試官敎諭蔡　批〔題本平易作者率多牽合不通此篇說理詳盡措詞簡當宜取以冠本房〕
考試官敎諭羅　批〔詞語清新優於衆作〕
考試官敎諭汪　批〔發明中正爲觀之義最爲親切〕
===
以至德而表儀乎天下此彖傳釋觀之名義也
蓋德以中正爲至也九五以是德而表儀於天
下觀之道大矣哉昔伏羲畫下坤上巽之卦名
之曰觀吾夫子擧而傳之謂夫〔陽本乎上陰本乎下〕〔陰陽〕之
上爲大觀之主其德則聖人之德其位則聖人
之位其所以爲觀於天下一本於中正焉夫以
九居五是其中也中則無過不及而爲天下之
大中以陽居陽是其正也正則不偏不倚而爲
天下之至正以是中正而恭己南面一神道設
punctuated:
慣乎！樂正子猶在善信之間，即其從乎敎一事觀之，則其有諸己者尚未實也。噫！

易
中正以觀天下
高晝達
同考試官敎諭蔡　批〔題本平易，作者率多牽合不通。此篇說理詳盡，措詞簡當，宜取以冠本房。〕
考試官敎諭羅　批〔詞語清新，優於衆作。〕
考試官敎諭汪　批〔發明中正爲觀之義，最爲親切。〕

以至德而表儀乎天下，此彖傳釋觀之名義也。蓋德以中正爲至也，九五以是德而表儀於天下，觀之道大矣哉！昔伏羲畫下坤上巽之卦，名之曰觀。吾夫子擧而傳之，謂夫〔陽本乎上，陰本乎下〕〔陰陽〕之上，爲大觀之主。其德則聖人之德，其位則聖人之位，其所以爲觀於天下，一本於中正焉。夫以九居五，是其中也；中則無過不及，而爲天下之大中。以陽居陽，是其正也；正則不偏不倚，而爲天下之至正。以是中正而恭己南面，一神道設
translation_en:
…“Accustomed?” [?] Yuezheng Zi was still between goodness and sincerity. Judging just from his following the teaching [?], what he possessed within himself was not yet fully realized. Alas!

Book of Changes
“Through Centrality and Correctness, He Displays Himself to All under Heaven”
Gao Zhouda

Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is straightforward, yet most writers force connections and fail to make sense. This essay explains the principles thoroughly, and its wording is concise and apt. It should be selected to head the essays in this examining room.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔The language is fresh and lucid, superior to the other compositions.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Its elucidation of how centrality and correctness constitute a model for others is especially pertinent.〕

To serve as a model for all under Heaven through consummate virtue: this is how the Commentary on the Judgments explains the name and meaning of Guan, “Contemplation.” For virtue reaches its utmost in centrality and correctness. With this virtue, the nine in the fifth place serves as a model for all under Heaven. Great indeed is the Way of Guan! In antiquity, Fuxi drew the hexagram with Kun below and Xun above, naming it Guan. Our Master took it up and composed his commentary, saying that the one 〔yang is rooted above; yin is rooted below〕 above 〔yin and yang〕 [?] is the ruler who provides the great spectacle. His virtue is the virtue of a sage; his position is the position of a sage. His serving as a model for all under Heaven is rooted entirely in centrality and correctness.

A nine occupying the fifth place constitutes his centrality. Being central, he neither exceeds nor falls short, and thus embodies the great mean for all under Heaven. A yang line occupying a yang place constitutes his correctness. Being correct, he neither deviates nor inclines to either side, and thus embodies the utmost correctness for all under Heaven. With this centrality and correctness, he holds himself reverently and faces south as ruler, wholly employing the numinous Way to establish…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
敎也豈假脩為乎以是中正而凝命九重一神
化宜民也奚容智力乎是以營東郊西地里雖
有遠近也而中正之敷布不以遠近而有閒越
南冀北疆域雖有彼此也而中正之流行不以
彼此而或殊中則有以示天下之不中使不中
者取法於此而咸歸於無過不及之域所謂建
中于民者是已正則有以示天下之不正俾不
正者取則於斯而悉底於不偏不倚之鄉所謂
表正萬邦者是已吁為觀之道何以加於此哉
===
吾夫子舉之以釋觀之名義宜矣抑考九五之
文曰觀我生君子无咎象曰觀我生觀民也其
義蓋與此互相發耳夫五有是中正之德固為
人所瞻仰又當驗之於民以自省察也不然何
以知民德之善否而驗吾所行之得失哉然則
觀民設教者當以中正為本
易簡之善配至德
張纁
同考試官教諭蔡　批　說易簡至德處真切
punctuated:
敎也，豈假脩為乎？以是中正而凝命九重，一神化宜民也，奚容智力乎？是以營東郊西，地里雖有遠近也，而中正之敷布不以遠近而有閒；越南冀北，疆域雖有彼此也，而中正之流行不以彼此而或殊。中則有以示天下之不中，使不中者取法於此，而咸歸於無過不及之域，所謂建中于民者是已。正則有以示天下之不正，俾不正者取則於斯，而悉底於不偏不倚之鄉，所謂表正萬邦者是已。吁！為觀之道，何以加於此哉？吾夫子舉之以釋觀之名義，宜矣。抑考九五之文曰：「觀我生，君子无咎。」象曰：「觀我生，觀民也。」其義蓋與此互相發耳。夫五有是中正之德，固為人所瞻仰，又當驗之於民，以自省察也。不然，何以知民德之善否，而驗吾所行之得失哉？然則觀民設教者，當以中正為本。

易簡之善配至德
張纁
同考試官教諭蔡　批：說易簡至德處真切
translation_en:
…teaching: how could this depend upon deliberate cultivation and action? Through this centrality and correctness, he secures the Mandate within the ninefold palace; this is entirely a matter of benefiting the people through numinous transformation. What place is there for cleverness or force? Thus, whether east of Ying or west of Jiao [?], although places differ in their distance, the diffusion of centrality and correctness suffers no interruption on account of distance. Whether south in Yue or north in Ji, although territories lie in different regions, the circulation of centrality and correctness does not vary from one to another. Through centrality, he provides guidance to those under Heaven who lack it, causing them to take this as their model and all return to a condition of neither excess nor deficiency. This is what is meant by “establishing the mean among the people.” Through correctness, he provides guidance to those under Heaven who are not correct, causing them to take this as their standard and all reach a state of neither partiality nor deviation. This is what is meant by “setting a correct example for the myriad states.” Ah! How could the way of serving as an object of contemplation surpass this? It was fitting that our Master invoked this to explain the name and meaning of the hexagram Contemplation (Guan). Yet consider the text for the nine in the fifth place: “Contemplating my life: the gentleman is without blame.” The Image Commentary says: “‘Contemplating my life’ means contemplating the people.” Its meaning and the foregoing explanation illuminate one another. Possessing this virtue of centrality and correctness, the ruler in the fifth place is indeed looked up to by others; yet he must also test it against the condition of the people in order to examine himself. Otherwise, how could he know whether the people’s virtue is good or bad, and thereby assess what is right or wrong in his own conduct? Thus, one who observes the people and establishes teaching must take centrality and correctness as his foundation.

The Goodness of Ease and Simplicity Matches Supreme Virtue
Zhang Xun 張纁
Associate Examiner Cai 蔡, Instructor, comments: The discussion of ease and simplicity and of supreme virtue is authentic and apt…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
有味其敷演條暢蓋用心於易者一薦何疑
考試官教諭羅　批　至德不外乎易簡發
明可觀
考試官教諭汪　批　體認易簡詳盡
論在易所言當行之理猶在人所得當然之理
夫易與人心相爲流通者也然則易書所言當
行之理豈不與人所得當然之理而相似哉昔
吾夫子大傳論易之廣大及此謂夫易書之理
不但配之天道而人事亦與之配焉是故易之
===
所有陰陽而已凡陽皆乾而乾之德則易觀夫
三十有二之陽卦百九十二之陽爻其辭之所
命者雖有不一然無一而非此易之善焉凡陰
皆坤而坤之德則簡觀夫三十有二之陰卦百
九十二之陰爻其辭之所指者雖有不同然無
一而非此簡之善焉夫易書所言易簡之善如
此果若何而配於至德乎蓋人之所行坦然明
白而不艱不深者易之至德也是至德也物莫
之似易乃顯微無間故凡言易之善者實相似
punctuated:
有味，其敷演條暢，蓋用心於易者，一薦何疑？
考試官教諭羅批：至德不外乎易簡，發明可觀。
考試官教諭汪批：體認易簡詳盡。
論在易所言當行之理，猶在人所得當然之理。
夫易與人心相爲流通者也。然則易書所言當行之理，豈不與人所得當然之理而相似哉？昔吾夫子大傳論易之廣大，及此謂夫易書之理，不但配之天道，而人事亦與之配焉。是故易之所有，陰陽而已。凡陽皆乾，而乾之德則易。觀夫三十有二之陽卦、百九十二之陽爻，其辭之所命者雖有不一，然無一而非此易之善焉。凡陰皆坤，而坤之德則簡。觀夫三十有二之陰卦、百九十二之陰爻，其辭之所指者雖有不同，然無一而非此簡之善焉。夫易書所言易簡之善如此，果若何而配於至德乎？蓋人之所行，坦然明白而不艱不深者，易之至德也。是至德也，物莫之似，易乃顯微無間，故凡言易之善者，實相似
translation_en:
…rich in meaning. Its exposition is orderly and fluent: this is surely someone who has devoted thought to the Changes. What doubt can there be about recommending him?

Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “Consummate virtue lies wholly within ease and simplicity. The elucidation is worthy of attention.”

Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “His understanding of ease and simplicity is detailed and thorough.”

The argument is that the principles of proper conduct articulated in the Changes resemble the principles of what ought to be that human beings possess.

The Changes and the human mind communicate with one another. How, then, could the principles of proper conduct articulated in the Book of Changes fail to resemble the principles of what ought to be that human beings possess? Long ago, when our Master discussed the breadth and greatness of the Changes in the Great Commentary, he reached this point: the principles of the Book of Changes correspond not only to the Way of Heaven; human affairs also correspond to them. Thus, what the Changes contains is simply yin and yang. All yang belongs to Qian, and Qian’s virtue is ease. Consider the thirty-two yang hexagrams and the hundred and ninety-two yang lines: although the injunctions of their statements vary, none fails to embody this goodness of ease. All yin belongs to Kun, and Kun’s virtue is simplicity. Consider the thirty-two yin hexagrams and the hundred and ninety-two yin lines: although the matters indicated by their statements differ, none fails to embody this goodness of simplicity.

Such is the goodness of ease and simplicity articulated in the Book of Changes. How, then, does it correspond to consummate virtue? Human conduct that is open and clear, neither difficult nor obscure, constitutes the consummate virtue of ease. Nothing among other things resembles this consummate virtue; yet the Changes encompasses the manifest and the subtle without a gap. Thus, wherever it speaks of the goodness of ease, this indeed resembles…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
焉其相似者非牽合也蓋易有此易而人亦有
此易耳人之所行截然要約而不煩不擾者簡
之至德也是至德也物莫之配易乃廣大悉備
故凡言簡之善者實相配也其相配者非附會
也蓋易有此簡而人亦有此簡耳吁易書具乎
易簡而易簡配乎至德易之所以廣大者如
是夫抑通考之此章首言易之廣大上文既以
乾坤廣大實之矣至此又曰廣大配天地變通
配四時陰陽之義配日月而終之以易簡之善
配至德由是觀之則知易書之理不徒在於造
化而又在於吾心矣
===
書
帝光天之下至于海隅蒼生萬邦黎獻共
惟帝臣
胡鰲
同考試官訓導張　批
發揮明德化頑處宛然
虞廷告君氣象且詞理俱到文采燁然故録之以式多學
同考試官教諭袁　批
此題淺近易見學者率
punctuated:
焉。其相似者，非牽合也，蓋易有此易，而人亦有此易耳。人之所行截然要約而不煩不擾者，簡之至德也。是至德也，物莫之配，易乃廣大悉備，故凡言簡之善者，實相配也。其相配者，非附會也，蓋易有此簡，而人亦有此簡耳。吁！易書具乎易簡，而易簡配乎至德，易之所以廣大者如是夫！抑通考之，此章首言易之廣大，上文既以乾坤廣大實之矣。至此，又曰：「廣大配天地，變通配四時，陰陽之義配日月。」而終之以「易簡之善配至德」。由是觀之，則知易書之理不徒在於造化，而又在於吾心矣。

書
帝光天之下，至于海隅蒼生，萬邦黎獻，共惟帝臣。
胡鰲

同考試官訓導張　批：
發揮明德化頑處，宛然虞廷告君氣象，且詞理俱到，文采燁然，故録之以式多學。

同考試官教諭袁　批：
此題淺近易見，學者率
translation_en:
…with it. This resemblance is no forced connection: the Book of Changes possesses this ease, and human beings likewise possess it. When a person's conduct is clearly defined and concise, without complication or disturbance, this is the consummate virtue of simplicity. Nothing among things can match this consummate virtue; yet the Book of Changes is vast and comprehensive, encompassing everything. Thus all that it says about the goodness of simplicity truly corresponds to this virtue. This correspondence is no strained interpretation: the Book of Changes possesses this simplicity, and human beings likewise possess it. Ah! The Book of Changes embodies ease and simplicity, and ease and simplicity correspond to consummate virtue. Such is what makes the Changes vast and great!
Considering this chapter as a whole, its opening speaks of the vastness and greatness of the Changes, and the preceding passage has already substantiated this through the vastness and greatness of Qian and Kun. Here it further says, “Its vastness and greatness correspond to Heaven and Earth; its change and continuity correspond to the four seasons; the significance of yin and yang corresponds to the sun and moon.” It concludes with “The goodness of ease and simplicity corresponds to consummate virtue.” Viewed in this light, we know that the principles of the Book of Changes reside not only in the workings of creation but also in our own hearts.

Book of Documents
“The Emperor's radiance illuminated all beneath Heaven, reaching the common people at the farthest shores. The worthy men of the myriad states all acknowledged themselves as the Emperor's subjects.”
Hu Ao 胡鰲

Moreover, both expression and reasoning are fully realized, and its literary brilliance shines forth. We have therefore selected it to serve as a model for the many students.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
能道其所欲言者之偏枯則涉於陳腐惟意若少是篇詞不繁而意已
□殆盡經之旨矣筆者獻宜表而出之
考試官教諭羅　批
深得大臣告君之旨佳作也
考試官教諭汪　批
詞理俱到
惟君德之著極其遠則天下之賢樂於用夫德
乃感化人心之本也君德之著旣極其遠則天
下之賢皆樂於用矣尚何頑讒之足慮哉昔禹
因舜慮庶頑讒說而告之以此謂夫頑讒不足
固所當威也孰若明之以德使帝德之光輝達
===
于普天之下遠而至于海隅蒼生之地一皆是
德之昭灼而無遠弗届焉頑讒不直固所當懲
也孰若化之以德俾帝德之光華被于覆幬之
間極而至於海表蒼生之域一皆是德之宣著
而無遠弗至焉德之遠著如此由是萬邦黎民
之衆有懷忠而晦迹者昔雖永矢弗諼也今則
感德輝之昭灼而爲之興起皆有帝臣之願矣
天下庶民之廣有秉直而韜光者向雖永矢弗
告也今則慕德輝之宣著而爲之奮發咸有獻
punctuated:
能道其所欲言者之偏枯，則涉於陳腐，惟意若少。是篇詞不繁而意已□，殆盡經之旨矣。筆者獻，宜表而出之。
考試官教諭羅批：深得大臣告君之旨，佳作也。
考試官教諭汪批：詞理俱到。
惟君德之著極其遠，則天下之賢樂於用。
夫德乃感化人心之本也。君德之著旣極其遠，則天下之賢皆樂於用矣，尚何頑讒之足慮哉？昔禹因舜慮庶頑讒說而告之以此，謂夫頑讒不足，固所當威也。孰若明之以德，使帝德之光輝達于普天之下，遠而至于海隅蒼生之地，一皆是德之昭灼，而無遠弗届焉。頑讒不直，固所當懲也。孰若化之以德，俾帝德之光華被于覆幬之間，極而至於海表蒼生之域，一皆是德之宣著，而無遠弗至焉。德之遠著如此，由是萬邦黎民之衆，有懷忠而晦迹者，昔雖永矢弗諼也，今則感德輝之昭灼而爲之興起，皆有帝臣之願矣。天下庶民之廣，有秉直而韜光者，向雖永矢弗告也，今則慕德輝之宣著而爲之奮發，咸有獻
translation_en:
…can express what they wish to say, but their one-sided treatment lapses into stale convention, with little apparent substance [?]. This essay is not verbose, yet its meaning is already [illegible]; it nearly exhausts the purport of the Classic. The writer’s offering [?] deserves to be singled out and published.
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “It profoundly captures the intent of a great minister addressing his ruler. An excellent composition.”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”
Only when the manifestation of the ruler’s virtue reaches the remotest places do the worthy throughout the realm delight in entering his service.
Virtue is the foundation for moving and transforming people’s hearts. Once the manifestation of the ruler’s virtue reaches the remotest places, all the worthy throughout the realm delight in entering his service. What reason remains to fear the obstinate and slanderous? Long ago, because Shun was concerned about the many obstinate people and their slanderous talk, Yu addressed him with these words. His meaning was that the obstinate and slanderous were deficient [?] and certainly ought to be overawed. Yet how could that compare with enlightening them through virtue, causing the radiance of the emperor’s virtue to reach everywhere beneath Heaven, extending as far as the lands inhabited by the people at the sea’s edge? Everywhere this virtue would shine brilliantly, with no place too distant for it to reach. The obstinate and slanderous are not upright and certainly ought to be punished. Yet how could that compare with transforming them through virtue, causing the splendor of the emperor’s virtue to spread throughout all that Heaven covers, extending even to the regions inhabited by people beyond the seas? Everywhere this virtue would be manifest, with no place too distant for it to reach.
With virtue manifested so far afield, among the multitudes of common people in the myriad states, those who harbor loyalty while concealing their whereabouts—even though formerly they had sworn never to forget—would now be stirred to action by the brilliant radiance of virtue, all wishing to become the emperor’s servants. Among the vast numbers of ordinary people throughout the realm, those who uphold rectitude while hiding their brilliance—even though formerly they had sworn never to make it known—would now admire the manifest radiance of virtue and be roused to exert themselves, all possessing the desire to offer…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
臣之心矣吁此以德感彼以德應賢智奮庸蹙
于至治庶頑讒說豈足慮哉大抵德者爲治之
本刑者輔治之具有其本而無其具是謂徒善
有其具而無其本是謂徒法禹之意雖欲舜弛
其鞭朴之威而益廣其文教之及至舜之意則
又稱禹之功叙而尤不廢士師之刑噫德刑並
施恩威兼著此有虞所以恭己無爲而卓乎不
可及也歟
惟敬五刑以成三德一人有慶兆民賴之
邢瓘

〔〔此處左行〕無絲毫宜錄以爲式〕

punctuated:
臣之心矣。吁！此以德感，彼以德應，賢智奮庸，蹙于至治，庶頑讒說豈足慮哉？大抵德者，爲治之本；刑者，輔治之具。有其本而無其具，是謂徒善；有其具而無其本，是謂徒法。禹之意，雖欲舜弛其鞭朴之威，而益廣其文教之及；至舜之意，則又稱禹之功叙，而尤不廢士師之刑。噫！德刑並施，恩威兼著，此有虞所以恭己無爲而卓乎不可及也歟？

惟敬五刑，以成三德。一人有慶，兆民賴之。

translation_en:
…the desire to offer themselves as ministers. Ah! When the ruler moves others through virtue, they respond through virtue; the worthy and wise rise to service, hastening toward perfect government [?]. What cause for concern could the multitude of obstinate people and slanderers present? Generally speaking, virtue is the foundation of government, and punishments are instruments that assist government. To possess the foundation without the instruments is called mere goodness; to possess the instruments without the foundation is called mere law. Yu's intention was that Shun should relax the coercive force of his whips and rods and further extend the reach of his civilizing instruction. Shun, for his part, praised Yu's achievements in bringing order, yet above all did not dispense with the punishments administered by the Judge. Ah! Virtue and punishment were applied together, and benevolence and authority were both manifest. Was this not why the ruler of Youyu could reverently comport himself and govern without action, standing so far above others that none could equal him?

“Only by reverently administering the five punishments can you perfect the three virtues. When the One Man enjoys felicity, the myriad people benefit thereby.”
Xing Guan

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The essay shows that the ruler's felicity and the people's benefit arise from ‘cultivating punishments’ [?] and perfecting virtue. Its language is vigorous and mature, its reasoning clear and fluent. Placing it among the leading essays accords with the collective judgment.〕
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔Among the essays addressing this topic, many confuse the five punishments with the three virtues and fail to distinguish them clearly; they also lack a definite understanding of the ruler's felicity and the people's benefit. This essay brings out King Mu's intention in his instructions on punishments.〕 〔〔Here, the left-hand column〕There is not the slightest … [?]. It should be recorded as a model.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps the essential meaning.〕

A worthy king invariably exhorts the feudal lords of his own surname in the proper way to employ punishments, expecting their beneficial effects …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
焉夫敬刑成德用刑之道也能勉乎此則君庶
民賴之效自有不期然而然者矣昔穆王訓刑
而告同姓諸侯及此意豈不曰爲治固不廢乎
刑而用刑必先本乎敬是刑也有所謂墨劓者
焉有所謂剕宮大辟者焉誠能敬乎五刑之用
君雖以爲辟也兢兢戒謹不敢以狥君而或辟
謹乎五刑之施君雖以爲宥也業業危懼不敢
以從君而或宥當重而重當輕而輕于以成夫
三德之剛柔夫何有於太苛而太縱宜辟而辟
===
宜宥而宥于以成夫三德之正直未嘗至於或
邪而或曲夫敬刑成德如此由是刑期無刑而
得以優游乎天位之尊辟以止辟而得以從容
乎九重之上則君受其福而慶於上矣四方風
動而自不犯于有司萬邦咸寧而罔或干于刑
憲則民蒙其惠而賴於下矣吁以一敬用刑而
君慶民賴如此汝同姓諸侯可不知所務耶雖
然敬以用刑穆王豈無所本乎舜之欽恤文王
之敬忌一此心之用也故其訓刑不曰敬忌罔
punctuated: 焉。夫敬刑成德，用刑之道也。能勉乎此，則君庶民賴之效，自有不期然而然者矣。昔穆王訓刑，而告同姓諸侯及此，意豈不曰：「爲治固不廢乎刑，而用刑必先本乎敬。是刑也，有所謂墨劓者焉，有所謂剕宮大辟者焉。誠能敬乎五刑之用，君雖以爲辟也，兢兢戒謹，不敢以狥君而或辟；謹乎五刑之施，君雖以爲宥也，業業危懼，不敢以從君而或宥。當重而重，當輕而輕，于以成夫三德之剛柔，夫何有於太苛而太縱？宜辟而辟，宜宥而宥，于以成夫三德之正直，未嘗至於或邪而或曲。夫敬刑成德如此，由是刑期無刑，而得以優游乎天位之尊；辟以止辟，而得以從容乎九重之上。則君受其福而慶於上矣。四方風動，而自不犯于有司；萬邦咸寧，而罔或干于刑憲。則民蒙其惠而賴於下矣。吁！以一敬用刑，而君慶民賴如此，汝同姓諸侯可不知所務耶？」雖然，敬以用刑，穆王豈無所本乎？舜之欽恤，文王之敬忌，一此心之用也。故其訓刑，不曰「敬忌罔
translation_en:
…therein. Reverently administering punishments to perfect the virtues is the proper way to employ punishment. If one can strive at this, the benefits to ruler and common people [?] will follow naturally, without being sought. When King Mu instructed the feudal lords of his own surname about punishments and addressed this matter, was his meaning not as follows?

“In governing, punishment certainly cannot be dispensed with; yet its use must first be grounded in reverence. These punishments include tattooing and cutting off the nose, as well as amputation of the foot, castration, and death. If you are truly reverent in employing the Five Punishments, then even when the ruler considers someone deserving of execution, you will remain vigilant and cautious, not daring to execute merely to indulge him. If you are circumspect in administering the Five Punishments, then even when the ruler considers someone deserving of pardon, you will remain apprehensive and fearful, not daring to pardon merely to comply with him. Impose severity where severity is due, and leniency where leniency is due: thereby perfect firmness and gentleness among the Three Virtues. How could there then be excessive harshness or excessive indulgence? Execute where execution is appropriate, and pardon where pardon is appropriate: thereby perfect uprightness among the Three Virtues, never descending into perversity or crookedness.

“When reverent administration of punishments perfects the virtues in this way, punishment aims at eliminating the need for punishment, and the ruler can enjoy ease in the dignity of his Heaven-appointed position. Penalties serve to end penalties, and he can dwell at leisure within the ninefold palace. Thus the ruler receives these blessings and enjoys felicity above. The four quarters respond as if moved by the wind, and naturally commit no offenses against the authorities; the myriad states are all at peace, and none transgresses the penal statutes. Thus the people receive these benefits and find support below. Ah! When reverence alone guides punishment, the ruler enjoys felicity and the people find support in this way. Can you feudal lords of the same surname fail to know what you must strive for?”

Yet did King Mu have no precedent for employing punishment with reverence? Shun’s reverent compassion and King Wen’s reverent caution were alike expressions of this same disposition. Thus, in his instructions concerning punishment, if he did not say, “Be reverent and cautious; do not…”

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
有擇言在身則曰何敬非刑不曰哀敬折獄則
曰朕敬于刑敬之之言凡三四致意焉吁穆王
於訓刑之際而不忽乎敬之之心此夫子所以
筆之於書也歟
詩
王公伊濯維豐之垣四方攸同王后維翰
王后烝哉豐水東注維禹之績四方
攸同皇王維辟皇王烝哉
朱應昌
===
同考試官訓導蕭　批〔雅題正大以王后皇王之號觀之文王遷豐天下有二至武王居豐而天下一統矣作者往〕〔往易而忽之間有得焉又不親切惟此作詞理俱到真奇才也故〕
錄之
同考試官教諭姜　批〔大雅一題場中多以漸都舊都立說甚有以遷鎬爲武王克君者深戾厥旨披沙揀金僅得〕
此篇宜錄以爲經義式
同考試官教諭楊　批〔場中作此題者多不知文〕〔王作豐始遷王業武王繼之統一天下之意此作得之必用心於本領之學〕
punctuated:
有擇言在身」，則曰「何敬非刑」；不曰「哀敬折獄」，則曰「朕敬于刑」。敬之之言，凡三四致意焉。吁！穆王於訓刑之際，而不忽乎敬之之心，此夫子所以筆之於書也歟？

詩
王公伊濯，維豐之垣。四方攸同，王后維翰。王后烝哉！豐水東注，維禹之績。四方攸同，皇王維辟。皇王烝哉！
朱應昌

同考試官訓導蕭，批〔雅題正大，以王后皇王之號觀之，文王遷豐，天下有二；至武王居豐，而天下一統矣。作者往〕〔往易而忽之，間有得焉，又不親切。惟此作詞理俱到，真奇才也，故〕錄之。

同考試官教諭姜，批〔大雅一題，場中多以漸都舊都立說，甚有以遷鎬爲武王克君者，深戾厥旨。披沙揀金，僅得〕此篇，宜錄以爲經義式。

同考試官教諭楊，批〔場中作此題者，多不知文〕〔王作豐，始遷王業，武王繼之，統一天下之意。此作得之，必用心於本領之學〕
translation_en:
…that there should be words open to criticism in one's conduct,” he says, “What exercise of reverence is not concerned with punishments?” If he does not say, “With compassion and reverence decide lawsuits,” he says, “I am reverent in administering punishments.” Three or four times he gives earnest emphasis to reverence. Ah! King Mu, when issuing instructions on punishments, did not neglect a reverent heart. Is this why the Master recorded these words in the Book of Documents?

Book of Odes
The king's achievement was glorious: such were the walls of Feng. The four quarters came together; the king was their pillar. How exalted was the king! The Feng River flowed eastward: this was the achievement of Yu. The four quarters came together; the august king was their sovereign. How exalted was the august king!
Zhu Yingchang

Associate Examiner Xiao, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This topic from the Court Hymns is grand and upright. Judging by the designations ‘king’ and ‘august king,’ when King Wen moved to Feng, he possessed two [parts of the realm?]; when King Wu resided at Feng, all under Heaven became united. Writers frequently treat this lightly and overlook it. Occasionally some grasp the point, but their treatment is still insufficiently precise. This composition alone fully succeeds in both expression and reasoning. Its author is truly an exceptional talent; therefore I have selected it for inclusion.”

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “On this topic from the Greater Court Hymns, many candidates in the examination hall based their arguments on a ‘gradual capital’ [?] and an ‘old capital.’ Some even took the move to Hao as demonstrating King Wu's ability to act as ruler, profoundly contradicting the passage's meaning. Sifting sand to pick out gold, I have found only this essay. It should be included as a model of interpretation of the Classics.”

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Most candidates who wrote on this topic did not understand its meaning: King Wen established Feng and first transferred the royal enterprise there, and King Wu succeeded him and united all under Heaven. This composition grasps that meaning. Its author must have devoted himself to learning concerned with the foundations…”

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
有聲之以冠本房
考試官教諭羅　批　詞順理明作詩義當如此
考試官教諭汪　批　說文武盡君道處無餘
前王作豐而得人心也既見其克君後王居豐
而一人心也亦見其克君蓋君道未易盡也文
王作豐於前武王繼之於後而人心之歸如此
非克盡君道能然哉此詩言文王遷豐武王遷
鎬之事至此謂夫遹求厥寧遹觀厥成王公尚
未著也今而濯濯然芳勲顯著偉績昭彰者豈
===
無自歟蓋以文王既伐于崇作邑于豐而成此
垣故耳是以此疆爾界四方何廣也皆於是來
歸來附而以文王爲之貞榦是臣是僕而以文
王爲之依歸豐邑一作人心翕從由是焉三分
有二一代之王業振矣則文王克盡君道也何
如文王造矣武王繼之豐邑翼翼豐水湯湯人
但見豐之美也而不知湯湯然東入於渭而注
於河者誰之績歟蓋由神禹疏鑿之功濬導之
力而底于成故耳是以普天率土四方何大也
punctuated:
有聲之以冠本房。
考試官教諭羅批：詞順理明，作詩義當如此。
考試官教諭汪批：說文武盡君道處無餘。
前王作豐而得人心也，既見其克君；後王居豐而一人心也，亦見其克君。蓋君道未易盡也，文王作豐於前，武王繼之於後，而人心之歸如此，非克盡君道能然哉？此詩言文王遷豐、武王遷鎬之事，至此謂夫「遹求厥寧，遹觀厥成」，王公尚未著也。今而濯濯然芳勲顯著、偉績昭彰者，豈無自歟？蓋以文王既伐于崇，作邑于豐，而成此垣故耳。是以此疆爾界，四方何廣也！皆於是來歸來附，而以文王爲之貞榦；是臣是僕，而以文王爲之依歸。豐邑一作，人心翕從，由是焉三分有二，一代之王業振矣。則文王克盡君道也何如？文王造矣，武王繼之。豐邑翼翼，豐水湯湯，人但見豐之美也，而不知湯湯然東入於渭而注於河者，誰之績歟？蓋由神禹疏鑿之功、濬導之力，而底于成故耳。是以普天率土，四方何大也！
translation_en:
…and acclaim it by ranking it first in this examining division [?].
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “The language flows smoothly and the reasoning is clear. An exposition of the Odes should be written like this.”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Its account of how Kings Wen and Wu fulfilled the way of the ruler leaves nothing unsaid.”
The former king founded Feng and won the people’s hearts: this already showed his ability to act as ruler. The later king resided at Feng and united the people’s hearts: this likewise showed his ability to act as ruler. For the way of the ruler is not easily fulfilled. King Wen founded Feng first, and King Wu succeeded him afterward; the people’s hearts turned to them in this manner. Could this have happened had they not fully fulfilled the way of the ruler? This ode recounts King Wen’s removal to Feng and King Wu’s removal to Hao. At this point it means that, when he “sought its peace” and “examined its completion,” the king’s achievements [?] were not yet manifest. Now his illustrious merits stand brilliantly revealed and his great accomplishments shine forth: could these have come about without a cause? It was simply because King Wen had attacked Chong, established his city at Feng, and completed these walls. Thus, within these boundaries and borders—how extensive were the lands in every direction!—all came to submit and attach themselves to him, taking King Wen as their steadfast support. They became his subjects and servants, taking King Wen as the one on whom they depended and to whom they owed allegiance. Once the city of Feng was founded, the people’s hearts followed him in concord. Thus he possessed two of the realm’s three parts, and the royal enterprise of a dynasty flourished. How fully, then, did King Wen fulfill the way of the ruler!
King Wen founded it, and King Wu succeeded him. The city of Feng was stately and well ordered; the Feng River flowed in mighty streams. People saw only the beauty of Feng, without knowing whose achievement it was that these mighty waters flowed east into the Wei and poured into the Yellow River. It was simply through the divine Yu’s work of cutting channels and his efforts in dredging and directing the waters that this was brought to completion. Thus, throughout all beneath Heaven and to the furthest bounds of the land—how vast were the regions in every direction! …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
豈得以循豐水而來歸戴武王以爲元后仰豐
邑而來同媚武王以爲天子豐都如故歸附維
新由是爲天下一統一代之王業成矣則武王
克盡君道也何如詩人各以箴哉贊之宜矣嗟
夫莫爲之前雖美弗彰莫爲之後雖盛弗傳文
王伐崇作豐而造王業於始武王續之而成王
業於終父子一心文武一道有周王業之成豈
偶然哉千載而下讀是詩者猶可想見當時之
盛
===
爲茲戎功繼序其皇之
徐崇德
同考試官訓導蕭　批〔得厥繼而嘗成功之音聖之〕
同考試官教諭吳　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
〔王報臣之意筆勁理明字數自別宜録〕
同考試官教諭楊　批〔作此題者於繼序皇之〕
〔句多體認不真是篇說出王者報功使諸侯子孫繼序而益大勛〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔采擇□□之可〕
〔祭錫福之功之意誠葩經中之傑士也〕
punctuated:
豈得以循豐水而來歸，戴武王以爲元后；仰豐邑而來同，媚武王以爲天子。豐都如故，歸附維新，由是爲天下一統，一代之王業成矣。則武王克盡君道也何如？詩人各以箴哉贊之，宜矣。嗟夫！莫爲之前，雖美弗彰；莫爲之後，雖盛弗傳。文王伐崇作豐，而造王業於始；武王續之，而成王業於終。父子一心，文武一道，有周王業之成，豈偶然哉？千載而下，讀是詩者，猶可想見當時之盛。
爲茲戎功，繼序其皇之。
徐崇德
同考試官訓導蕭，批〔得厥繼而嘗成功之音聖之〕
同考試官教諭吳，批〔□□□□□□□□□□□□〕〔王報臣之意，筆勁理明，字數自別，宜録。〕
同考試官教諭楊，批〔作此題者，於繼序皇之〕〔句多體認不真，是篇說出王者報功，使諸侯子孫繼序而益大勛〕
考試官教諭羅，批〔采擇□□之可〕〔祭錫福之功之意，誠葩經中之傑士也。〕
translation_en:
…How could they follow the Feng River to come and give their allegiance, honoring King Wu as their sovereign; look toward the settlement of Feng and come together, loving King Wu as the Son of Heaven? [?] The capital at Feng remained as before, but the allegiance it received was renewed. Through this, all under Heaven became united, and the dynasty’s royal enterprise was accomplished. How fully, then, did King Wu discharge the duties of a ruler! It was fitting that the poet praised each king with the words, “A warning indeed!” Alas! Without someone to begin it, even excellence would remain unmanifested; without someone to follow it, even greatness would not be transmitted. King Wen attacked Chong and established Feng, thus initiating the royal enterprise; King Wu continued his work and brought it to completion. Father and son shared one heart; Wen and Wu followed one Way. Could the accomplishment of the Zhou royal enterprise have been accidental? A thousand years later, readers of this poem can still imagine the splendor of that age.

“You have performed this great service; may your successors carry it on and magnify it.”

Xu Chongde

Associate Examiner Xiao, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Obtaining successors and tasting the sound of accomplished achievement … sage …” [?]

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “[Twelve illegible characters.] The meaning of the king’s rewarding his ministers: the writing is vigorous and the reasoning clear; the word count is distinctive [?]. It merits selection.”

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Those who write on this topic frequently fail to grasp correctly the phrase ‘may your successors carry it on and magnify it.’ This essay explains how the king rewards service, allowing the descendants of the regional lords to succeed in turn and further magnify their achievements …”

Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “Selection … [two illegible characters] … acceptable [?].” “The meaning of service in sacrifice and the conferring of blessings [?]: truly an outstanding scholar of the Classic of Poetry.”

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭汪　批〔講當時周王報臣之意極爲明順〕
念其功之大報其後之隆此王者於助祭諸侯
然也盖功之大者報必隆也今諸侯旣有助祭
錫福之大功王者得不隆其報於後哉此祭於
宗廟而獻助祭諸侯之樂歌其意謂夫助祭用
脩臣職之常報功寔我王朝之典維爾辟公於
予肆祀錫茲祉福而惠我以無疆之休功莫大
矣念茲大功獨不有以報之乎助我祭事今以
繁祉而延及於後世之遠勲莫隆矣顧茲隆渥
===
獨不思以報之乎將圭爵是予以爲汝報耶汝
所已有也匪報也惟使爾子而又子繼斯土而
而益大其助祭錫福之功不但今日然也將享
土是錫以爲汝報耶汝所固有也非報也惟俾
汝孫而又孫纘斯茅土而益大其助祭錫福之
勲不特一世然也夫如是庶乎他日汝子孫助
祭錫福無異乎汝今日之福我我子孫獲福報
功不殊乎我今日之報汝君臣先後相爲輝映
不爲有周之盛乎雖然周王之待諸侯豈特報
punctuated:
考試官教諭汪，批〔講當時周王報臣之意極爲明順〕。

念其功之大，報其後之隆，此王者於助祭諸侯然也。盖功之大者，報必隆也。今諸侯旣有助祭錫福之大功，王者得不隆其報於後哉？此祭於宗廟而獻助祭諸侯之樂歌，其意謂：夫助祭用脩，臣職之常；報功，寔我王朝之典。維爾辟公，於予肆祀，錫茲祉福，而惠我以無疆之休，功莫大矣。念茲大功，獨不有以報之乎？助我祭事，今以繁祉而延及於後世之遠，勲莫隆矣。顧茲隆渥，獨不思以報之乎？將圭爵是予，以爲汝報耶？汝所已有也，匪報也。惟使爾子而又子，繼斯土而而益大其助祭錫福之功，不但今日然也。將享土是錫，以爲汝報耶？汝所固有也，非報也。惟俾汝孫而又孫，纘斯茅土而益大其助祭錫福之勲，不特一世然也。夫如是，庶乎他日汝子孫助祭錫福，無異乎汝今日之福我；我子孫獲福報功，不殊乎我今日之報汝。君臣先後，相爲輝映，不爲有周之盛乎？雖然，周王之待諸侯，豈特報
translation_en:
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation of the Zhou king’s intention in rewarding his subjects at that time is exceptionally clear and coherent.〕

Mindful of the greatness of their merit, he richly rewarded their descendants: such was the king’s treatment of the feudal lords who assisted at the sacrifices. For great merit must receive generous recompense. Since the lords had rendered the great service of assisting at sacrifices and bringing blessings, could the king fail to reward their descendants generously? This is a ritual song performed at the ancestral temple and presented to the lords who assisted at the sacrifices. Its meaning is as follows:

Assisting in the proper performance of sacrifices is a regular duty of a subject; rewarding merit is indeed an established practice of our royal court. You, my lords, have brought these blessings to my great sacrifice, bestowing boundless favor upon me. No merit could be greater. Mindful of this great merit, could I fail to provide recompense? By assisting at my sacrifices, you have now caused abundant blessings to extend to generations far into the future. No achievement could be more exalted. Considering such ample bounty, could I fail to think of repaying it?

Shall I give you jade tablets and noble ranks as your reward? These you already possess; they would be no recompense. Rather, I shall ensure that your sons, generation after generation, inherit this territory and further magnify their meritorious service in assisting at sacrifices and bringing blessings, so that it will not be confined to the present day. Shall I grant you lands to enjoy as your reward? These are already yours; they would be no recompense. Rather, I shall ensure that your grandsons, generation after generation, succeed to these enfeoffed lands and further magnify their achievements in assisting at sacrifices and bringing blessings, so that these will not be confined to a single generation.

In this way, one may hope that in days to come your descendants will assist at sacrifices and bring blessings just as you bless me today, and that my descendants will receive blessings and reward merit just as I reward you today. Rulers and subjects, in successive generations, will lend splendor to one another. Would this not constitute the flourishing glory of Zhou? Yet, in his treatment of the feudal lords, did the Zhou king merely reward…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
其功而已哉下文又舉道德以戒勉之歎先王
以感動之蓋以不能勉乎道德法乎先王則今
日之序且不能保况能衍之於無窮乎崇報之
中不忘勸戒之意此所以爲盛時之樂歌也歟
春秋
楚師鄭師侵衛〔成公二年〕公會晉侯宋公
衛侯曹伯伐鄭〔成公〕鄭公子去疾帥師
伐許〔成公〕鄭伐許〔並成公三年〕楚子鄭
伯伐宋〔並成公十〕楚人鄭人侵宋〔並成公十〕
八年〕鄭師伐宋〔並襄公〕遂城虎牢〔並襄公〕
二年〕
===
考試官教諭羅 批〔尋究狄鄭削鄭之由可謂善〕
用傳者也
考試官教諭汪 批〔作者體認未真唯是篇合旨〕
他卷莫能或之先也
王景運
戴國行同於外夷春秋黜爵以示貶志附於外
夷春秋削地以示譏此可見鄭之附楚以亟病
punctuated:
其功而已哉？下文又舉道德以戒勉之，歎先王以感動之。蓋以不能勉乎道德、法乎先王，則今日之序且不能保，况能衍之於無窮乎？崇報之中，不忘勸戒之意，此所以爲盛時之樂歌也歟！

春秋

楚師、鄭師侵衛〔成公二年〕。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭〔成公〕。鄭公子去疾帥師伐許〔成公〕。鄭伐許〔並成公三年〕。楚子、鄭伯伐宋〔並成公十〕。楚人、鄭人侵宋〔並成公十〕八年〕。鄭師伐宋〔並襄公〕。遂城虎牢〔並襄公〕二年〕。

考試官教諭羅批〔尋究狄鄭、削鄭之由，可謂善〕用傳者也。

考試官教諭汪批〔作者體認未真，唯是篇合旨〕他卷莫能或之先也。

王景運

戴國行同於外夷，春秋黜爵以示貶；志附於外夷，春秋削地以示譏。此可見鄭之附楚以亟病
translation_en:
…their service alone? The following passage also invokes the Way and virtue to admonish and encourage them, and praises the former kings to move their hearts.
