For if they cannot strive to cultivate the Way and virtue and take the former kings as their models, they cannot even preserve their present order, much less perpetuate it without end. Amid lavish rewards, the intention to encourage and admonish is never forgotten. Is this not what makes it a ceremonial song of a flourishing age?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The armies of Chu and Zheng invaded Wei.” [Second year of Duke Cheng.] “The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng.” [Duke Cheng.] “Prince Quji of Zheng led an army to attack Xu.” [Duke Cheng.] “Zheng attacked Xu.” [All in the third year of Duke Cheng.] “The Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng attacked Song.” [All in Duke Cheng’s ‘tenth…’ year [?].] “Men of Chu and Zheng invaded Song.” [All in Duke Cheng’s ‘tenth…’ year; ‘eighth year’ follows outside the annotation [?].] “The army of Zheng attacked Song.” [All under Duke Xiang.] “They then fortified Hulao.” [All under Duke Xiang; ‘second year’ follows outside the annotation [?].]

Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: “By investigating why Zheng is treated as barbarian and why its name is omitted, he may be called adept at using the commentaries.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The writer’s understanding is not yet fully sound; only this essay accords with the intended meaning. None of the other papers can surpass it.”

Wang Jingyun

When a state [?] behaves like the outer barbarians, the Spring and Autumn Annals suppresses its ruler’s rank to express censure; when its intentions incline toward the outer barbarians, the Spring and Autumn Annals omits its territorial name to express criticism. Here we can see how Zheng’s adherence to Chu repeatedly brought suffering upon…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
中國春秋得不嚴詞以深責之哉思昔鄭之爵
位受之天子子孫世繼率有舊職春秋何爲黜
爵以貶之耶蓋鄭自取郊以來不懲先世之失
決意戎楚之從今年因楚救齊遂合兵以伐衛
後明年因晉往討即在興以覆晉師未幾怒許
不從而君臣相繼以伐許焉導楚以憑陵上國
而伐喪背晉不之顧動衆以暴虐鄰邦而憑弱
犯寡不之恤夫鄭以王室懿親唯利所在而不
擇義之可否以爲去就其所以異於夷者幾希
===
矣故春秋特於鄭襄之伐許黜其本爵比之夷
狄例以荊吳而止書國者非黜爵以示貶乎鄭
之王迹傳之先祖子孫世守罔敢失墜春秋何
爲削地以譏之耶蓋鄭自鄢陵以後不改先君
之惡唯馳南向之轅今日因楚助魚石之叛兩
黨楚以虐宋明日因楚憤彭城之復遂奉命以
伐宋已而負固不服晉合諸侯以城虎牢焉棄
親暱而從豺狼不思戢扈之臣不可助背諸夏
而黨荊楚不惜地險之設不能守夫鄭以天子
punctuated: 中國，春秋得不嚴詞以深責之哉？思昔鄭之爵位，受之天子，子孫世繼，率有舊職，春秋何爲黜爵以貶之耶？蓋鄭自取郊以來，不懲先世之失，決意戎楚之從。今年因楚救齊，遂合兵以伐衛；後明年因晉往討，即在興以覆晉師；未幾，怒許不從，而君臣相繼以伐許焉。導楚以憑陵上國，而伐喪背晉不之顧；動衆以暴虐鄰邦，而憑弱犯寡不之恤。夫鄭以王室懿親，唯利所在，而不擇義之可否以爲去就，其所以異於夷者幾希矣。故春秋特於鄭襄之伐許，黜其本爵，比之夷狄，例以荊吳，而止書國者，非黜爵以示貶乎？鄭之王迹，傳之先祖，子孫世守，罔敢失墜，春秋何爲削地以譏之耶？蓋鄭自鄢陵以後，不改先君之惡，唯馳南向之轅。今日因楚助魚石之叛，兩黨楚以虐宋；明日因楚憤彭城之復，遂奉命以伐宋。已而負固不服，晉合諸侯以城虎牢焉。棄親暱而從豺狼，不思戢扈之臣不可助；背諸夏而黨荊楚，不惜地險之設不能守。夫鄭以天子
translation_en:
…the central states—how could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to employ stern language to rebuke Zheng severely? Consider how Zheng’s rank was originally received from the Son of Heaven: its descendants inherited it generation after generation, each continuing to discharge the established duties. Why, then, do the Spring and Autumn Annals strip away its rank to express condemnation? Since taking Jiao [?], Zheng had failed to learn from its predecessors’ errors and had resolved to follow the Rong and Chu. In this year, when Chu came to Qi’s rescue, Zheng joined forces with it to attack Wei. The year after next, when Jin went to chastise Zheng, Zheng thereupon overturned Jin’s army at Xing [?]. Before long, angered by Xu’s refusal to follow it, Zheng’s ruler and ministers attacked Xu in succession. Zheng led Chu in assaulting the central states, heedless of attacking a state in mourning and turning its back on Jin. It mobilized troops to brutalize neighboring states, unconcerned about bullying the weak and attacking those with few defenders. Although Zheng was a close kinsman of the royal house, it followed profit alone, choosing its allegiances without considering whether righteousness permitted them. Little indeed distinguished it from the barbarians. Thus, specifically when recording Duke Xiang of Zheng’s attack on Xu, the Spring and Autumn Annals suppress his proper rank, equate Zheng with the barbarians, and apply the precedent of Jing and Wu by recording only the state’s name. Is this not the suppression of rank to express condemnation?

Zheng’s royal legacy had been handed down from its ancestors; their descendants guarded it through the generations, none daring to let it fall away. Why, then, do the Spring and Autumn Annals remove its territory to express censure? After Yanling, Zheng failed to reform the evils of its former ruler and drove its chariot only southward. On one occasion, when Chu supported Yu Shi’s rebellion, Zheng twice [?] sided with Chu to oppress Song. On the next, when Chu was angered by the recovery of Pengcheng, Zheng obeyed its command to attack Song. Subsequently, Zheng relied on its defenses and refused submission, whereupon Jin assembled the regional lords to fortify Hulao. Abandoning its close kin to follow jackals and wolves, Zheng failed to consider that a rebellious minister [?] must not be supported. Turning its back on the Xia states to side with Jing and Chu, it showed no concern that it could not hold the defenses afforded by its terrain. Now Zheng, in its relation to the Son of Heaven…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
侯度惟強是與而不義之以大義以為從違其
辱天子之封守亦甚矣故春秋獨於諸侯之滅
虎牢削之於鄭歸之中國例以下陽不書國而
止書虎牢者非削地以示譏乎吁伯爵鄭之封
號也以行同於夷而黜之虎牢鄭之封疆也以
志附於夷而削之春秋之法其嚴矣哉或者有
曰貶爵削地天子事也仲尼無天子之位而行
天子之事可乎噫不曰春秋天子之事也知我
罪我者其惟春秋乎仲尼有德無位不得行天
===
子之法於當時故假魯史脩春秋垂天子之法
於萬世其事雖殊其理一耳夫奚疑
公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕
張進
考試官教諭羅　批〔說得聖人化齊透徹〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔此題作者雷同而是篇詞〕
獨豐贍故表之
即二國之好會見聖化之大行此齊魯夾谷之
會春秋所以特書之也歟且天下莫大於理而
punctuated:
侯度，惟強是與，而不義之以大義，以為從違，其辱天子之封守亦甚矣。故《春秋》獨於諸侯之滅虎牢，削之於鄭，歸之中國。例以下陽，不書國而止書虎牢者，非削地以示譏乎？吁！伯爵，鄭之封號也，以行同於夷而黜之；虎牢，鄭之封疆也，以志附於夷而削之。《春秋》之法，其嚴矣哉！或者有曰：「貶爵削地，天子事也。仲尼無天子之位而行天子之事，可乎？」噫！不曰「《春秋》，天子之事也」，「知我罪我者，其惟《春秋》乎」？仲尼有德無位，不得行天子之法於當時，故假魯史脩《春秋》，垂天子之法於萬世。其事雖殊，其理一耳，夫奚疑？

公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕
張進
考試官教諭羅，批〔說得聖人化齊透徹〕
考試官教諭汪，批〔此題作者雷同，而是篇詞〕獨豐贍，故表之。

即二國之好會，見聖化之大行，此齊魯夾谷之會，《春秋》所以特書之也歟？且天下莫大於理，而
translation_en:
…the ordinances governing a feudal lord. Zheng allied itself solely with the strong, failing to judge them by higher righteousness as the basis for following or rejecting them [?]. It gravely dishonored the territory entrusted to it by the Son of Heaven. Thus, specifically when the feudal lords destroyed [?] Hulao, the Spring and Autumn Annals stripped it from Zheng and assigned it to the central states. Following the precedent of Xiayang, it names no state but records only Hulao: is this not a stripping away of territory to convey censure? Ah! The rank of earl was Zheng’s enfeoffed title; because its conduct resembled that of the barbarians, the Annals demoted it. Hulao was part of Zheng’s enfeoffed domain; because its allegiance lay with the barbarians, the Annals stripped it away. How stern are the laws of the Spring and Autumn Annals! Someone may ask: “Demoting ranks and stripping away territory are the Son of Heaven’s business. Could Zhongni undertake the Son of Heaven’s business without occupying his position?” Ah! Did he not say, “The Spring and Autumn Annals concerns the Son of Heaven’s business,” and “Those who understand me and those who condemn me will surely do so through the Spring and Autumn Annals”? Zhongni possessed virtue but held no ruling position. Unable to enforce the Son of Heaven’s laws in his own time, he therefore drew upon the historical records of Lu to compile the Spring and Autumn Annals, transmitting the Son of Heaven’s laws to all succeeding ages. Although the undertakings differed, their principle was one. What cause is there for doubt?

“The Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding〕
Zhang Jin
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔“The account of how the sage transformed Qi is penetrating and thorough.”〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔“Those writing on this topic all say much the same thing, but this essay’s language”〕 is exceptionally rich and ample; therefore I single it out.

In a friendly meeting between two states, we see the far-reaching exercise of the sage’s transforming influence. Was this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically recorded this meeting of Qi and Lu at Jiagu? Moreover, nothing under Heaven is greater than principle, and…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
強衆不與焉有如魯定之世齊再伐魯而強於
魯魯再侵齊而弱於齊孰不以爲齊勝於魯魯
弱於齊耶一旦齊魯相平講會夾谷齊惑犂彌
之計欲逞萊夷之兵匿干櫓於好會之間而欲
脅我魯以詐謾伏甲冑於揖讓之際而欲迫我
魯以威力斯時也魯無人乎定公之側豈不岌
岌乎其殆哉幸而魯用宣聖相禮會所以衣冠
爲甲冑以禮義爲干櫓出于盟偪好之詞詞何
嚴也而萊夷之兵自靡發不祥愆義之言言何
===
順也而野享之設自卻齊君愧悔之不遑齊臣
謝過之恐後兵不必交也自足以安我魯於泰
山之安刃不必接也自足以固我魯於磐石之
固以一會俄頃之間成曠古所無之績聖人以
王道而化齊也何其不疾而速之若是耶吁夾
谷未會齊欲駕魯而魯有不測之憂夾谷既會
魯能化齊而齊有服義之美聖人王道大行於
是乎見矣由是而觀魯能終用聖人則文武成
康之治可以復見豈直化齊而已哉惜乎天不
punctuated: 強衆不與焉。有如魯定之世，齊再伐魯而強於魯，魯再侵齊而弱於齊，孰不以爲齊勝於魯，魯弱於齊耶？一旦齊魯相平，講會夾谷，齊惑犂彌之計，欲逞萊夷之兵，匿干櫓於好會之間，而欲脅我魯以詐謾；伏甲冑於揖讓之際，而欲迫我魯以威力。斯時也，魯無人乎？定公之側，豈不岌岌乎其殆哉？幸而魯用宣聖相禮會所，以衣冠爲甲冑，以禮義爲干櫓。出于盟偪好之詞，詞何嚴也，而萊夷之兵自靡；發不祥愆義之言，言何順也，而野享之設自卻。齊君愧悔之不遑，齊臣謝過之恐後。兵不必交也，自足以安我魯於泰山之安；刃不必接也，自足以固我魯於磐石之固。以一會俄頃之間，成曠古所無之績。聖人以王道而化齊也，何其不疾而速之若是耶！吁！夾谷未會，齊欲駕魯，而魯有不測之憂；夾谷既會，魯能化齊，而齊有服義之美。聖人王道大行，於是乎見矣。由是而觀，魯能終用聖人，則文武成康之治可以復見，豈直化齊而已哉？惜乎天不
translation_en: …strength and numbers have no part in it. In the time of Duke Ding of Lu, Qi twice attacked Lu and was stronger than Lu; Lu twice invaded Qi yet remained weaker than Qi. Who did not think that Qi surpassed Lu and that Lu was weaker than Qi? When Qi and Lu made peace and arranged a meeting at Jiagu, Qi was misled by Li Mi’s scheme and sought to unleash the troops of the Lai barbarians. They concealed shields amid a friendly meeting, intending to intimidate our state of Lu through deceit; they stationed armored soldiers in ambush amid the ceremonial bows and courtesies, intending to coerce our Lu by force. At that moment, did Lu have no capable man? Was not Duke Ding’s immediate situation precarious indeed? Fortunately, Lu employed the Illustrious Sage, Confucius, to assist with the rites at the meeting place, taking ceremonial robes and caps as armor and helmets, and ritual and righteousness as shields. He issued words condemning coercion in an alliance of friendship [?]—how stern those words were!—and the Lai troops gave way of themselves. He spoke of inauspicious conduct and offenses against righteousness—how sound those words were!—and the arrangements for a banquet in the open country were withdrawn of themselves. The ruler of Qi was overwhelmed with shame and remorse, and Qi’s ministers hastened to apologize, each fearing to fall behind. Without troops needing to clash, this sufficed to make our Lu as secure as Mount Tai; without blades needing to meet, it sufficed to make our Lu as firm as solid rock. In the brief span of a single meeting, he accomplished a feat unprecedented since antiquity. How swiftly the Sage transformed Qi through the Kingly Way, without haste! Ah! Before the meeting at Jiagu, Qi wished to dominate Lu, and Lu feared unforeseen calamity. After the meeting at Jiagu, Lu had succeeded in transforming Qi, and Qi displayed the virtue of submitting to righteousness. Here we see the Sage’s Kingly Way taking full effect. Viewed in this light, had Lu been able to employ the Sage to the end, the government of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang could have appeared again. Would the achievement have been merely the transformation of Qi? Alas, Heaven did not…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
欲平治我舉而使之不克終用也噫天果無意
於聖人耶殆將欲其刪述六經垂憲後世以開
萬世之太平也歟
禮記
故人者天地之心也五行之端也食味別
聲被色而生者也
李簡
同考試官訓導徐　批〔場中作此題者率指情言殊以性爲氣且分裂破碎殊不可人意是卷剖理明〕
===
〔而文足以發之殆知爲人之道者〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔文冇頓挫〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔善認理者〕
論人具造化理氣之正而資物用之常以有生
焉蓋理氣稟於有生之初物用資於有生之後
也然則人之生也得不有在於是歟記禮君子
謂夫所貴乎人者以其得造化之理氣以爲形
性資造化之功用以爲育養焉耳彼天地之心
以理言也人何以謂天地之心邪曰元曰亨天
punctuated:
欲平治我舉，而使之不克終用也。噫！天果無意於聖人耶？殆將欲其刪述六經，垂憲後世，以開萬世之太平也歟？

禮記
故人者，天地之心也，五行之端也，食味、別聲、被色而生者也。

李簡
同考試官訓導徐批〔場中作此題者，率指情言，殊以性爲氣，且分裂破碎，殊不可人意。是卷剖理明〕〔而文足以發之，殆知爲人之道者。〕
考試官教諭羅批〔文冇頓挫。〕
考試官教諭汪批〔善認理者。〕

論人具造化理氣之正，而資物用之常以有生焉。蓋理氣稟於有生之初，物用資於有生之後也。然則人之生也，得不有在於是歟？記禮君子謂夫所貴乎人者，以其得造化之理氣以爲形性，資造化之功用以爲育養焉耳。彼天地之心，以理言也。人何以謂天地之心邪？曰元，曰亨，天
translation_en:
…did not wish to bring peace and order to our realm [?], and thus prevented him from being employed to the end. Alas! Did Heaven truly have no purpose for the sage? Perhaps it intended him to edit and transmit the Six Classics, bequeathing models to later generations and thereby opening an age of supreme peace lasting ten thousand generations?

Record of Rites
“Thus the human being is the heart of Heaven and Earth, the culmination of the Five Phases, living by tasting flavors, distinguishing sounds, and being clothed in colors.”

Li Jian
Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic generally addressed it in terms of the emotions, wrongly treating human nature as material force (qi). Their treatments were also fragmented and disjointed, thoroughly unsatisfactory. This paper analyzes principle clearly” “and its writing adequately brings that analysis out. Its author seems to understand the Way of being human.”
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “The writing has [?] pauses and turns.”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “One who is skilled at discerning principle.”

The argument is that human beings possess the proper endowment of principle (li) and material force from the transforming processes of creation, and sustain their lives through the regular use of things. Principle and material force are received at the beginning of life; the use of things provides support after life has begun. Must not human life, then, depend upon these? The gentleman who recorded the rites meant that what makes human beings precious is simply that they obtain the principle and material force of creation to constitute their bodily form and nature, and draw upon its workings to grow and be nourished. To call them “the heart of Heaven and Earth” is to speak in terms of principle. Why are human beings called the heart of Heaven and Earth? “Origination” and “flourishing”: Heaven …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
地生物之心也而人得之則爲仁爲利
曰貞天地成物之心也而人得之則爲禮爲
焉此非天地之心而何五行之端以氣言也人
何以謂五行之端邪曰木曰火其端見於春夏
也而人之肝心屬焉曰金曰水曰土其端見於
秋冬與四時也而人之肺腎脾屬焉此非五行
之端而何然五行滋而爲酸苦辛鹹甘之五味
也人則食之以養其口矣五行感而爲宮商角
徵羽之聲也人則別之以養其耳矣五行形
===
而爲青赤黃白黑之五色也人則被之以爲身
之章焉夫既賦之以理氣之正又資之以物用
之常此人所以參立於天地之間涵育於覆載
之內而獨異於萬物也歟大抵得天地之理氣
而有生者人與物皆然也但人得其全而物則
惟得其一偏耳此人之爲人所以生於天地而
參於天地囿於五行而妙於五行養於萬物而
靈於萬物者也學者察此而有得焉則爲人之
道其庶幾乎
punctuated: 地生物之心也，而人得之則爲仁爲利。曰貞，天地成物之心也，而人得之則爲禮爲焉。此非天地之心而何？五行之端，以氣言也。人何以謂五行之端邪？曰木曰火，其端見於春夏也，而人之肝心屬焉；曰金曰水曰土，其端見於秋冬與四時也，而人之肺腎脾屬焉。此非五行之端而何？然五行滋而爲酸苦辛鹹甘之五味也，人則食之以養其口矣；五行感而爲宮商角徵羽之聲也，人則別之以養其耳矣；五行形而爲青赤黃白黑之五色也，人則被之以爲身之章焉。夫既賦之以理氣之正，又資之以物用之常，此人所以參立於天地之間，涵育於覆載之內，而獨異於萬物也歟！大抵得天地之理氣而有生者，人與物皆然也。但人得其全，而物則惟得其一偏耳。此人之爲人所以生於天地而參於天地，囿於五行而妙於五行，養於萬物而靈於萬物者也。學者察此而有得焉，則爲人之道其庶幾乎！
translation_en:
…the heart of Heaven and Earth that generates things; when human beings receive it, it becomes benevolence and benefit [?]. As for steadfastness (zhen), it is the heart of Heaven and Earth that brings things to completion; when human beings receive it, it becomes ritual propriety and … [?]. If this is not the heart of Heaven and Earth, what is it? The expression “the culmination of the Five Phases” refers to vital energy (qi). Why are human beings called the culmination of the Five Phases? Wood and Fire manifest themselves in spring and summer, and the human liver and heart belong to them. Metal, Water, and Earth manifest themselves in autumn, winter, and all four seasons, and the human lungs, kidneys, and spleen belong to them. If this is not the culmination of the Five Phases, what is it?

The Five Phases yield the five flavors—sour, bitter, pungent, salty, and sweet—and people consume them to nourish their mouths. Through mutual stimulation, the Five Phases produce the musical notes gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu, and people distinguish them to nourish their ears. The Five Phases take visible form as the five colors—blue-green, red, yellow, white, and black—and people wear them as adornment for their bodies. Having endowed human beings with the proper principle and vital energy, Heaven and Earth also supply them with the constant resources of material things. Is this not why human beings stand as a third alongside Heaven and Earth, nurtured within what Heaven covers and Earth supports, and uniquely distinguished from the myriad things?

In general, human beings and other things alike receive the principle and vital energy of Heaven and Earth and thereby come to life. But human beings receive them in their entirety, whereas other things receive only one partial aspect. This is what makes human beings human: born of Heaven and Earth, they nevertheless stand alongside them; encompassed by the Five Phases, they nevertheless embody their wondrous workings; nourished by the myriad things, they nevertheless surpass them in spiritual intelligence. If students examine this and attain an understanding of it, will they not come close to the Way of being human?

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
樂則安安則久久則天天則神
劉珝
同考試官訓導徐　批〔此作分别安久天神之意而貫以易直慈良之心字字有體認而節節無間斷〕
宜録爲學禮者式
考試官教諭羅　批〔始終主心說最是〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔說出致樂治心之妙〕
心樂乎善而漸極其妙此致樂之效然也甚矣
樂之感化人心也則夫樂善而漸極其妙得非
===
致樂以治心之所致哉今夫樂由中出心以樂
治故君子致和平中正之樂使易直慈良之心
邪穢蕩滌此心以之怡愉查滓消融是心爲之
悅豫夫既樂矣由是易直慈良之心從容自得
外物莫之撓優游自如非僻莫之干何如其安
也既安矣由是易直慈良之心始終一致不或
作而或輟先後一念不若存而若亡何如其久
也久則一真渾融無事乎勉强衆迹俱泯無待
於矯拂豈非易直慈良之心純於天乎天則神
punctuated:
樂則安，安則久，久則天，天則神。
劉珝
同考試官訓導徐批〔此作分别安久天神之意，而貫以易直慈良之心，字字有體認，而節節無間斷〕宜録爲學禮者式。
考試官教諭羅批〔始終主心說，最是〕
考試官教諭汪批〔說出致樂治心之妙〕
心樂乎善，而漸極其妙，此致樂之效然也。甚矣，樂之感化人心也！則夫樂善而漸極其妙，得非致樂以治心之所致哉？今夫樂由中出，心以樂治，故君子致和平中正之樂，使易直慈良之心，邪穢蕩滌，此心以之怡愉；查滓消融，是心爲之悅豫。夫既樂矣，由是易直慈良之心，從容自得，外物莫之撓；優游自如，非僻莫之干。何如其安也！既安矣，由是易直慈良之心，始終一致，不或作而或輟；先後一念，不若存而若亡。何如其久也！久則一真渾融，無事乎勉强；衆迹俱泯，無待於矯拂。豈非易直慈良之心純於天乎？天則神
translation_en:
“Joy brings repose; repose brings constancy; constancy brings accord with Heaven; accord with Heaven brings spiritual efficacy.”
Liu Xu
Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔This composition distinguishes the meanings of repose, constancy, accord with Heaven, and spiritual efficacy, while threading them together through the accommodating, upright, compassionate, and good heart. Every word shows an understanding grounded in personal reflection, and each successive section follows without interruption.〕 It should be recorded as a model for students of the rites.
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔Keeping the discussion centered on the heart from beginning to end is entirely right.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔It brings out the subtle workings of fully realizing music to govern the heart.〕
The heart delights in goodness and gradually reaches its utmost subtlety: this is the effect of fully realizing music. How profound is music’s power to influence and transform the human heart! Thus, is not delighting in goodness and gradually reaching its utmost subtlety precisely the result of fully realizing music to govern the heart? Now, music issues from within, and the heart is governed through music. Hence the gentleman fully realizes music that is harmonious, peaceful, balanced, and correct, so that wickedness and impurity are washed away from his accommodating, upright, compassionate, and good heart, and the heart thereby becomes joyful; its dregs dissolve, and it becomes glad.
Once there is joy, this accommodating, upright, compassionate, and good heart is composed and content in itself, undisturbed by external things; it is at ease and free, unassailed by perversity or wrongdoing. How great is its repose! Once there is repose, this accommodating, upright, compassionate, and good heart remains consistent from beginning to end, never active at one moment and idle at another. Its intent remains one throughout, never seeming present at one moment and absent at another. How great is its constancy! With constancy, its single genuineness becomes wholly integrated, without any need for forced effort; all traces of contrivance disappear, without any need for corrective restraint. Is this not the accommodating, upright, compassionate, and good heart becoming purely in accord with Heaven? With accord with Heaven comes spiritual …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
妙莫測非耳目所能盡變化無方非心思所能
度豈非易直慈良之心入於神乎吁樂之感化
人心至於如此此樂所以不可斯須去身也歟
大抵內而一心外而一身皆學者所當致力而
不可闕焉者故古之君子旣致樂以治心而使
內無不和又致禮以治躬而使外無不順由是
感人動物舉而錯之天下也無難矣
第貳場
論
===
萬世道德宗主
徐崇德
同考試官訓導蕭　批〔有抑揚有起伏作也高薦何疑〕
同考試官教諭姜　批〔議論精詳考據明白況文法章法燦然可觀令人讀之凜若吾夫子之臨於前也千百人中得士如子誰不珍重也耶〕
同考試官教諭楊　批〔文詞蒼古筆力老健必有學之士也宜然舉首孰曰不宜〕
punctuated:
妙莫測，非耳目所能盡；變化無方，非心思所能度。豈非易直慈良之心入於神乎？吁！樂之感化人心至於如此，此樂所以不可斯須去身也歟！大抵內而一心，外而一身，皆學者所當致力而不可闕焉者。故古之君子旣致樂以治心，而使內無不和；又致禮以治躬，而使外無不順。由是感人動物，舉而錯之天下也，無難矣。

第貳場
論

萬世道德宗主
徐崇德

同考試官訓導蕭，批〔有抑揚，有起伏，作也高薦何疑。〕
同考試官教諭姜，批〔議論精詳，考據明白。況文法章法燦然可觀，令人讀之，凜若吾夫子之臨於前也。千百人中得士如子，誰不珍重也耶？〕
同考試官教諭楊，批〔文詞蒼古，筆力老健，必有學之士也。宜然舉首，孰曰不宜？〕
translation_en:
…wondrous and unfathomable, beyond what ears and eyes can fully apprehend; its transformations follow no fixed pattern and are beyond what thought can measure. Is this not the heart of ease, uprightness, kindness, and goodness entering the realm of the numinous? Ah! Music moves and transforms the human heart to such an extent: is this not why one must never be without music, even for a moment? Broadly speaking, both the heart within and the person without require the learner’s effort; neither may be neglected. Thus the gentlemen of antiquity fully employed music to govern the heart, making everything within harmonious, and fully employed ritual to govern their conduct, making everything without accord with proper order. Thereafter, to influence people and move other beings, extending these practices throughout the world, presented no difficulty.

Second Session
Discourse

The Exemplar of the Way and Virtue for All Ages
Xu Chongde

Associate Examiner Xiao, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔There is restraint and emphasis, rising and falling. The composition merits high recommendation [?]; what doubt can there be?〕

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: 〔The argument is precise and thorough, and the supporting evidence clear. Moreover, the handling of prose and the organization of sections are brilliantly accomplished. Reading it, one feels an awed reverence, as though our Master himself stood before one. To find among hundreds or thousands a scholar such as you—who would not prize him?〕

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: 〔The language has an antique gravity, and the writing is mature and vigorous. This must be a man of learning. It is fitting that he should head the list of successful candidates [?]; who could say otherwise?〕

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭羅　批　〔筆力高古議論卓□〕
塲中之魁是者也
考試官教諭汪　批　〔作者詞浮無援是篇雅明道德宗主鑿鑿乎其實也且文勢滔滔豈稗章所能及耶〕
論曰平水土以奠民萬世之功也然而不
能救人心之陷溺躬稼穡以粒民萬世之
功也然而不能保人心之淪亡蓋可有也
人心不可溺也食可去也人心不可亡也
然則萬世之功其歸於孔子乎孔子删述
===
六經以為萬世道德之宗主所以救人心
之陷溺者在是所以保人心之淪亡者在
是所以參天地贊化育而立人極於千萬
世者在是孔子之功萬世之功也使世無
孔子則六經不備六經不備則道德湮閉
天下後世之人將貿貿焉如聾如瞶戴天
行日而莫之聞見也雖安居於水土之上
飽食於稼穡之餘靈於物而實不異於物
矣如人心何世道何有希曰自生民以來
punctuated:
考試官教諭羅批〔筆力高古，議論卓□。〕塲中之魁，是者也。

考試官教諭汪批〔作者詞浮無援，是篇雅明道德宗主，鑿鑿乎其實也。且文勢滔滔，豈稗章所能及耶？〕

論曰：平水土以奠民，萬世之功也，然而不能救人心之陷溺；躬稼穡以粒民，萬世之功也，然而不能保人心之淪亡。蓋可有也，人心不可溺也；食可去也，人心不可亡也。然則萬世之功，其歸於孔子乎？孔子删述六經，以為萬世道德之宗主，所以救人心之陷溺者在是，所以保人心之淪亡者在是，所以參天地、贊化育而立人極於千萬世者在是。孔子之功，萬世之功也。使世無孔子，則六經不備；六經不備，則道德湮閉。天下後世之人，將貿貿焉，如聾如瞶，戴天行日，而莫之聞見也。雖安居於水土之上，飽食於稼穡之餘，靈於物而實不異於物矣。如人心何？世道何？有希曰：「自生民以來
translation_en:
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔The writing has an elevated, antique vigor, and the argument is outstanding □.〕 This is the foremost composition in the examination.

Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Writers’ language is often superficial and unsupported; this essay lucidly explains the supreme master of the Way and virtue, establishing the substance of that claim with certainty. Moreover, its prose flows in an irresistible torrent. How could lesser compositions match it?〕

The discourse states: Ordering the waters and the land to settle the people was an achievement for all ages, yet it could not rescue human hearts from sinking into corruption. Personally undertaking sowing and reaping to feed the people was an achievement for all ages, yet it could not preserve human hearts from ruin. These may indeed be possessed [?], but human hearts must not be submerged; food may be dispensed with, but human hearts must not be lost. Does not achievement for all ages, then, belong to Confucius? Confucius edited and transmitted the Six Classics, thereby becoming the supreme master of the Way and virtue for all ages. Herein lies the means of rescuing human hearts from sinking into corruption; herein lies the means of preserving human hearts from ruin; herein lies the means of standing alongside Heaven and Earth, assisting their transforming and nurturing activity, and establishing the highest standard of humanity for countless generations. Confucius’s achievement is an achievement for all ages.

Had the world been without Confucius, the Six Classics would not have been complete. Had the Six Classics not been complete, the Way and virtue would have been obscured and shut away. The people of the world in later generations would have been bewildered, like the deaf and blind: beneath Heaven and walking in the sunlight, they would nevertheless have heard and seen nothing of these things. Though dwelling securely upon the land amid its waters and eating their fill from the harvests, they would, despite their spiritual superiority to other creatures, in reality have been no different from them. What would become of human hearts? What would become of the moral order of the world? Someone has said [?]: “Since humankind first came into being …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
未有盛於孔子也信乎窮天地亘古今一
人而已矣果齋李氏之論如此或者聞而
疑焉曰道德之天古今賢愚所同也行之
而爲道有之而爲德萬古此天地則萬古
此人心萬古此人心則萬古此道德也孔
子何以獨爲萬世之宗主乎意不然允執
厥中堯傳舜也惟精惟一舜授禹也堯舜
禹相傳一道而爲當時道德之宗主豈不
能皆堯舜禹也歷四百載而始傳之湯建
===
中于民則湯所以爲有商一代之宗主也
世不能皆湯也歷六百載而始傳之文武
周公懿恭建極思兼三王則文武周公所
以爲有周一代之宗主也世不能皆文武
周公陵夷而至於春秋之時無傳焉衰被
之時何時也諸侯放恣人欲橫流道德或
幾乎熄矣斯時也誰其宗主乎孔子有德
無位不得宗主乎道德於天下將託之書
而傳也則易更三古混於八索矣詩書煩
punctuated: 未有盛於孔子也。」信乎！窮天地，亘古今，一人而已矣。果齋李氏之論如此。或者聞而疑焉，曰：「道德之天，古今賢愚所同也。行之而爲道，有之而爲德。萬古此天地，則萬古此人心；萬古此人心，則萬古此道德也。孔子何以獨爲萬世之宗主乎？」意不然。允執厥中，堯傳舜也；惟精惟一，舜授禹也。堯舜禹相傳一道，而爲當時道德之宗主，豈不能皆堯舜禹也？歷四百載而始傳之湯，建中于民，則湯所以爲有商一代之宗主也。世不能皆湯也。歷六百載而始傳之文武周公，懿恭建極，思兼三王，則文武周公所以爲有周一代之宗主也。世不能皆文武周公。陵夷而至於春秋之時，無傳焉。衰被之時，何時也？諸侯放恣，人欲橫流，道德或幾乎熄矣。斯時也，誰其宗主乎？孔子有德無位，不得宗主乎道德於天下，將託之書而傳也，則《易》更三古，混於八索矣；《詩》《書》煩
translation_en:
…there has never been anyone greater than Kongzi.” How true! Throughout heaven and earth, across antiquity and the present, there has been but this one man. Such is the argument of Master Li, known as Guozhai. Someone who heard it expressed doubt, saying: “The heaven of the Way and virtue [?] is shared by the worthy and the foolish, ancient and modern alike. Practised, it constitutes the Way; possessed, it constitutes virtue. Throughout the ages, heaven and earth remain the same, and so does the human heart; throughout the ages, the human heart remains the same, and so do the Way and virtue. Why should Kongzi alone be the supreme teacher for all generations?”

I think otherwise. “Sincerely hold fast to the Mean” was what Yao transmitted to Shun; “Be discerning and single-minded” was what Shun imparted to Yu. Yao, Shun, and Yu transmitted the same Way to one another and were the supreme teachers of the Way and virtue in their times. Could not all be Yao, Shun, and Yu [?]? Only after four hundred years was it transmitted to Tang. Establishing the Mean among the people was what made Tang the supreme teacher of the Shang dynasty. Not everyone in the world could be Tang. Only after six hundred years was it transmitted to Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou. Through admirable reverence they established the supreme standard, and their aspirations encompassed those of the Three Kings: this was what made Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou the supreme teachers of the Zhou dynasty. Not everyone in the world could be Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou.

With gradual decline, the Spring and Autumn period arrived, and there was no one to carry on the transmission. What sort of age was this time of decay [?]? The feudal lords acted without restraint, human desires ran rampant, and the Way and virtue were almost extinguished. At such a time, who could be their supreme teacher? Kongzi possessed virtue but held no position; unable to serve as the supreme teacher of the Way and virtue throughout the realm, he would entrust them to writings for transmission. Yet the Book of Changes, having passed through the three ancient eras, had become mingled with the Eight Cords; the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents were encumbered…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
亂禮樂散亡而皆莫之正矣於是乎有堯
焉乃刪詩書定禮樂贊周易脩春秋堯舜
禹湯文武周公之道既壞而復完既墜而
復續凡天地之所以高厚日月之所以照
臨山川之所以峙流草木之所以蕃育仁
義禮智之所以為性惻隱羞惡辭讓是非
之所以為情父子君臣夫婦兄弟朋友之
所以為倫理物之為物人之為人君子之
所以為君子聖賢之所以為聖賢何莫不
===
備於斯而為世道德于焉不宗主於堯舜
禹湯文武周公而宗主於六經矣孔子所
以為萬世計者不其至乎自是一變而縱
橫再變而楊墨春秋下而戰國矣縱橫楊
墨能變孔子之六經乎孟子生而闢六經
之道德於子思之門入於是正人心息邪
說距詖行一主乎孔子戰國之人得不陷
於夷狄禽獸者非孔子之功誰之功也洎
焚於秦詖自坑焚甲伏生之口授孔壁安
punctuated: 亂，禮樂散亡，而皆莫之正矣。於是乎有堯焉，乃刪詩書，定禮樂，贊周易，脩春秋。堯舜禹湯文武周公之道，既壞而復完，既墜而復續。凡天地之所以高厚，日月之所以照臨，山川之所以峙流，草木之所以蕃育，仁義禮智之所以為性，惻隱羞惡辭讓是非之所以為情，父子君臣夫婦兄弟朋友之所以為倫理，物之為物，人之為人，君子之所以為君子，聖賢之所以為聖賢，何莫不備於斯？而為世道德，于焉不宗主於堯舜禹湯文武周公，而宗主於六經矣。孔子所以為萬世計者，不其至乎？自是一變而縱橫，再變而楊墨，春秋下而戰國矣。縱橫楊墨，能變孔子之六經乎？孟子生而闢六經之道德於子思之門，入於是正人心，息邪說，距詖行，一主乎孔子。戰國之人得不陷於夷狄禽獸者，非孔子之功，誰之功也？洎焚於秦，詖自坑焚甲，伏生之口授，孔壁安
translation_en:
…in disorder, while rites and music had become scattered and lost, and no one had put any of them right. Then there was Yao [?], who edited the Documents and Odes, established rites and music, elucidated the Changes of Zhou, and revised the Spring and Autumn Annals. The Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou, once damaged, was made whole again; once fallen into abeyance, it was continued again. Why Heaven and Earth are lofty and deep; why the sun and moon shed their light; why mountains stand and rivers flow; why plants flourish; why benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom constitute human nature; why compassion, shame and aversion, deference, and the sense of right and wrong constitute its feelings; why the relationships between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger brother, and friends constitute the ethical order; what makes things things and humans human; what makes exemplary men exemplary and sages and worthies sages and worthies—what among these is not fully contained here? Thus, for the Way and virtue in the world, people came to take as their supreme authority the Six Classics, rather than Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou. Was not Kongzi’s provision for all future ages most complete?

Thereafter, one transformation brought the advocates of vertical and horizontal alliances, and another brought the teachings of Yang Zhu and Mo Di; the Spring and Autumn period gave way to the Warring States. Could these advocates and the teachings of Yang and Mo alter Kongzi’s Six Classics? Mengzi arose and expounded the Way and virtue of the Six Classics in the school of Zisi. Thereupon [?] he rectified people’s hearts, put an end to heterodox doctrines, and opposed perverse conduct, taking Kongzi alone as his authority. That the people of the Warring States avoided sinking to the level of barbarians and beasts—if this was not Kongzi’s achievement, whose was it? When the books were burned under the Qin, [the text concerning the burying and burning is garbled: ?], Fu Sheng’s oral transmission and the wall of Kongzi’s house [?]…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
坑焚之黃老於漢彼自黃老耳董子之明
經孰得而黃老之所以爲秦漢道德之宗
主者孔子也不有孔子則伏生董子何所
傳秦漢之人何所聞而宗主之乎下是而
晉宋教斯佛矣晉宋而隋唐佛斯盛矣人
之去夷狄也其幾何哉昌黎韓子聞道德
於孟子之後原道一篇拳拳乎仁義之說
佛骨一表汲汲乎正邪之辯非有得於六
經之道德能如是耶然則以道德宗主乎
===
南北之間而啓唐者孔子也去是而梁唐
壞且亂矣梁唐而漢周壞亂極矣人之去
禽獸也其幾何哉有宋諸子倡道德於千
載之下濂溪周子繼孟子不傳之緒而兩
程得之兩程夫子發前聖未發之蘊而朱
子足之非本原於六經之旨𨗳能如是耶
然則以道德宗主乎五季之時而啓宋者
孔子也宋之有金腥我中原甚矣然是道
也然猶能於我朱子聞其起居則孔子之
punctuated:
坑焚之，黃老於漢，彼自黃老耳。董子之明經，孰得而黃老之？所以爲秦漢道德之宗主者，孔子也。不有孔子，則伏生、董子何所傳？秦漢之人何所聞而宗主之乎？下是而晉宋，教斯佛矣；晉宋而隋唐，佛斯盛矣。人之去夷狄也，其幾何哉？昌黎韓子聞道德於孟子之後，《原道》一篇，拳拳乎仁義之說；《佛骨》一表，汲汲乎正邪之辯。非有得於六經之道德，能如是耶？然則以道德宗主乎南北之間而啓唐者，孔子也。

去是而梁唐，壞且亂矣；梁唐而漢周，壞亂極矣。人之去禽獸也，其幾何哉？有宋諸子倡道德於千載之下，濂溪周子繼孟子不傳之緒，而兩程得之；兩程夫子發前聖未發之蘊，而朱子足之。非本原於六經之旨，𨗳能如是耶？然則以道德宗主乎五季之時而啓宋者，孔子也。宋之有金，腥我中原甚矣。然是道也，然猶能於我朱子聞其起居，則孔子之
translation_en:
…the burying and burning; Huang-Lao teachings in the Han [?]—those men merely followed Huang-Lao themselves. As for Master Dong’s elucidation of the Classics, who could turn it into Huang-Lao teaching? It was Confucius who served as the supreme authority for the Way and virtue in the Qin and Han. Without Confucius, what would Fu Sheng and Master Dong have transmitted? What would the people of Qin and Han have heard and taken as their supreme authority? Thereafter, in the Jin and Song, the teaching became Buddhist; from the Jin and Song to the Sui and Tang, Buddhism flourished. How little separated people from the barbarians! Master Han of Changli learned of the Way and virtue after Mencius. In his essay “An Inquiry into the Way,” he earnestly expounded benevolence and righteousness; in his “Memorial on the Buddha’s Bone,” he urgently distinguished the orthodox from the heterodox. Could he have done this without grasping the Way and virtue of the Six Classics? Thus it was Confucius who, through the Way and virtue, served as the supreme authority during the Northern and Southern Dynasties and opened the way for the Tang.

After this came the Later Liang and Later Tang, with decay and disorder; from the Later Liang and Later Tang to the Later Han and Later Zhou, decay and disorder reached their utmost extreme. How little separated people from birds and beasts! The masters of the Song proclaimed the Way and virtue a thousand years later. Master Zhou of Lianxi continued the thread of transmission that had been broken since Mencius, and the two Cheng brothers received it. The two masters Cheng brought forth meanings that the earlier sages had not disclosed, and Master Zhu completed their work. Without taking the purport of the Six Classics as their foundation, how could they have accomplished this [?]? Thus it was Confucius who, through the Way and virtue, served as the supreme authority in the age of the Five Dynasties and opened the way for the Song. During the Song, the Jin grievously befouled our Central Plain. Yet as for this Way, they could still inquire after the well-being of our Master Zhu; thus Confucius’s …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
道德行乎夷狄矣元以繼宋訏我衣冠甚
矣何足道哉然猶能用許魯齋教其族類
則孔子之道德變乎夷狄矣孔子刪述六
經以爲萬世道德之宗主詎不信哉雖然
孔子不可尚已自其刪述之後言之則發
明道德者孰有過於有宋諸君子而宋之
諸君子孰有備於朱子者哉惜乎不幸而
誤以僞學見沮求其能躬行於上推行於
下者不可得也孰若我
===
朝
太祖高皇帝主之於先
列聖相傳繼之於後六經之道行之在上六經
之說明之在下上下一心古今一道孔子
固萬世道德之宗主而我
列聖與
今日
聖天子又孔子道德之宗主也愚何幸親逢其
盛
punctuated: 道德行乎夷狄矣。元以繼宋，訏我衣冠甚矣，何足道哉！然猶能用許魯齋教其族類，則孔子之道德變乎夷狄矣。孔子刪述六經，以爲萬世道德之宗主，詎不信哉！雖然，孔子不可尚已。自其刪述之後言之，則發明道德者，孰有過於有宋諸君子？而宋之諸君子，孰有備於朱子者哉？惜乎不幸而誤以僞學見沮，求其能躬行於上、推行於下者，不可得也。孰若我朝太祖高皇帝主之於先，列聖相傳，繼之於後！六經之道，行之在上；六經之說，明之在下。上下一心，古今一道。孔子固萬世道德之宗主，而我列聖與今日聖天子，又孔子道德之宗主也。愚何幸親逢其盛！
translation_en:
…Confucius’s Way and virtue were practiced even among the barbarians. The Yuan succeeded the Song and grievously affronted our civilization of caps and gowns [?]; what merit did they have worth mentioning? Yet they could still employ Xu Luzhai to instruct their own people, so Confucius’s Way and virtue transformed even the barbarians. Confucius edited and transmitted the Six Classics, becoming the authoritative teacher of the Way and virtue for all ages: can this indeed be doubted?

Nevertheless, Confucius cannot be surpassed. Speaking of the time after his editing and transmission of the classics, who elucidated the Way and virtue more fully than the masters of the Song? And among those masters, who was more comprehensive than Master Zhu? Sadly, he suffered the misfortune of having his teachings wrongly condemned and obstructed as “false learning.” One could find no one able to embody them personally in high office and extend their practice among those below.

How could this compare with our dynasty, in which Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, first championed them, and the successive sage emperors transmitted them to one another and carried them forward? The Way of the Six Classics is practiced by those above; the teachings of the Six Classics are elucidated by those below. Above and below are of one mind; past and present follow one Way. Confucius is indeed the authoritative teacher of the Way and virtue for all ages, while our successive sage emperors and the reigning sage Son of Heaven are themselves the chief guardians of Confucius’s Way and virtue. How fortunate I, in my humble ignorance, am to witness this flourishing age in person!

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
表
擬賀大有年表
高士達
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔驊麗可觀〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔得體〕
考試官教諭江　批〔表佳〕
伏以
天開景運萃和氣於兩間
帝握乾符繼豐登於九有萬類戴含宏之化羣
生圖樂育之仁夷夏騰歡臣民胥慶茲盖
伏遇
===
一德格天
重華協帝隆儒重道大恢
列聖之良圖敬神恤民允荷
上天之寵命在璣衡以齊七政調玉燭以撫五
辰三白兆今歲之休徵九垓普及時之厚
punctuated:
表
擬賀大有年表
高士達
同考試官教諭蔡，批〔驊麗可觀〕。
考試官教諭羅，批〔得體〕。
考試官教諭江，批〔表佳〕。
伏以，天開景運，萃和氣於兩間；帝握乾符，繼豐登於九有。萬類戴含宏之化，羣生圖樂育之仁。夷夏騰歡，臣民胥慶。茲盖伏遇，一德格天，重華協帝，隆儒重道，大恢列聖之良圖；敬神恤民，允荷上天之寵命。在璣衡以齊七政，調玉燭以撫五辰。三白兆今歲之休徵，九垓普及時之厚
translation_en:
Memorial
Draft Memorial Congratulating the Emperor on a Year of Abundant Harvests
By Gao Shida

Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “Splendidly ornate and worthy of admiration.”
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “Appropriate to the form.”
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “A fine memorial.”

We humbly reflect: Heaven inaugurates a glorious age, gathering harmonious qi between heaven and earth; the Emperor holds Heaven’s mandate, bringing successive abundant harvests throughout the nine regions. All creatures revere his all-embracing transforming influence; all living beings seek his benevolent care, which delights in nurturing them. The peoples of the borderlands and the central realm rejoice together; officials and commoners alike celebrate.

This is surely because we have humbly been blessed to encounter Your Majesty, whose undivided virtue reaches Heaven and whose renewed splendor, like Shun’s, accords with the ancient sage emperor. You exalt Confucian learning and honor the Way, greatly extending the excellent designs of the successive sage emperors; you revere the spirits and care for the people, faithfully bearing Heaven’s gracious mandate. Attending to the jade celestial instrument and its sighting tube [?], you bring the seven celestial regulators into alignment; harmonizing the seasons, you bring the five planets into accord. Three auspicious snowfalls foretold this year’s blessings; throughout the nine reaches of the world, there spreads the season’s abundant …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
澤五穀熟而人民育八蜡通而海宇寧無
爾界此疆一視盡禾麻菽麥雖際天極地
爭詫多黍稷稻粱瑞麥中生特挺兩岐之
秀嘉禾異產還呈九穗之祥崇墉比櫛之
非如千倉萬箱之胥積康衢擊壤比屋謳
歌于焉
上供則粢盛之潔足以孝享乎
九廟于焉
國用則儲蓄之隆足以大賚於六師是皆
===
皇上深仁大德之所致以隆我
國家億萬載太平之嘉慶也臣等幸逢
盛世叨列清班考之春秋則特書以見意徵
之雅頌亦迭詠而爲歌況
今日之奇逢尤近古所罕見欲罄形容之妙
慚非博洽之才伏願
以天心而爲心遠紹無窮之大業
以民樂而爲樂丕弘莫大之鴻休地久天長
永
punctuated:
澤。五穀熟而人民育，八蜡通而海宇寧。無爾界此疆，一視盡禾麻菽麥；雖際天極地，爭詫多黍稷稻粱。瑞麥中生，特挺兩岐之秀；嘉禾異產，還呈九穗之祥。崇墉比櫛之非如，千倉萬箱之胥積。康衢擊壤，比屋謳歌。于焉上供，則粢盛之潔足以孝享乎九廟；于焉國用，則儲蓄之隆足以大賚於六師。是皆皇上深仁大德之所致，以隆我國家億萬載太平之嘉慶也。
臣等幸逢盛世，叨列清班。考之春秋，則特書以見意；徵之雅頌，亦迭詠而爲歌。況今日之奇逢，尤近古所罕見。欲罄形容之妙，慚非博洽之才。伏願以天心而爲心，遠紹無窮之大業；以民樂而爲樂，丕弘莫大之鴻休。地久天長，永
translation_en:
…beneficence. The five grains ripen and the people are nourished; the eight year-end agricultural sacrifices are duly performed, and all within the seas is at peace. No distinction is made between your boundary and this frontier: everywhere one looks are grain, hemp, beans, and wheat. Even to the ends of heaven and earth, people marvel at the abundance of millets, rice, and fine grain. Auspicious wheat springs up among the crops, its exceptional stalks bearing twin-branched ears; wondrously growing grain likewise displays the auspicious sign of nine ears. Tall grain-stacks stand close as the teeth of a comb [?], and a thousand granaries and myriad cartloads are filled with the accumulated harvest. On the broad thoroughfares people play at striking the ground, and household after household sings praise. From this abundance, the grain supplied for offerings is pure enough to provide filial sacrifices in the nine ancestral temples; for the needs of the state, the plentiful reserves suffice to bestow lavish rewards upon the six armies. All this has been brought about by Your Majesty’s profound benevolence and great virtue, magnifying the blessings of peace for our dynasty for countless ages.
We, your servants, have the good fortune to encounter this flourishing age and undeservedly occupy the ranks of honored officials. Examining the Spring and Autumn Annals, we find that such events were specially recorded to convey their significance; consulting the Major and Minor Odes and the Hymns, we likewise find them repeatedly celebrated in song. How much more remarkable is today’s extraordinary occurrence, so rarely witnessed in recent antiquity! We wish to exhaust every subtlety of description, yet are ashamed that we lack the requisite breadth of learning and talent. We humbly pray that you take Heaven’s heart as your own heart, carrying forward into the distant future your boundless great enterprise; and that you take the people’s joy as your own joy, greatly extending these unsurpassed blessings. As earth endures and heaven lasts, forever perpetuate…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
皇圖於鞏固日升川至綿
聖壽於無疆臣等下情無任欣躍感戴之至謹
奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
高士達
===
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔大經事實歷陳無遺〕
〔策盡人道者也〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔敷對詳明可錄〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔能道其倫事實詳悉哉〕
〔敷演開日者此也〕
天生烝民有物有則而大經之理寓於人
天佑下民作之君師而大經之理叙於君
此古昔聖帝明王相繼而出必有經世之
punctuated:
皇圖於鞏固，日升川至，綿聖壽於無疆。臣等下情無任欣躍感戴之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
第叁場，策，第一問。
高士達。
同考試官教諭蔡，批〔大經事實歷陳無遺〕〔策盡人道者也〕。
考試官教諭羅，批〔敷對詳明可錄〕。
考試官教諭汪，批〔能道其倫事實詳悉哉〕〔敷演開日者此也〕。
天生烝民，有物有則，而大經之理寓於人；天佑下民，作之君師，而大經之理叙於君。此古昔聖帝明王相繼而出，必有經世之
translation_en:
…may the imperial dominion remain forever secure; like the rising sun and the ever-flowing rivers, may Your Majesty’s sacred longevity extend without limit. We, your servants, cannot contain our joy, gratitude, and devotion. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session: Policy Essay, Question One.
Gao Shida.
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔The historical instances relating to the great constant principles are set forth in succession, omitting none.〕〔This policy essay fully expounds the human Way.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔The response is detailed and clear, and merits selection.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔He can explain their proper relationships; the historical particulars are indeed thoroughly presented.〕〔This is an exposition that “opens the day” [?].〕
Heaven gave birth to the multitude of people: for every thing there is a rule, and the underlying principles of the great constant norms reside in human beings. Heaven aided the people below by establishing rulers and teachers for them, and through the ruler the principles of these great constant norms are set in order. Thus, as the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity arose in succession, they invariably had, for governing the world, …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
典以風化當時垂憲萬世使人由之而不
知化之而莫測也粤自堯舜帝天下而典
謨之書以著湯武王天下而訓誥之書以
成洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝創造洪業條成大誥三編
太宗文皇帝繼志述事御製孝順事實爲善陰
騭二書
宣宗章皇帝嗣纘大統表輯經傳纂爲五倫一
===
書
天施縟藻昭回於雲漢之間
宸翰奎章煒煌於宇宙之內皆欲天下後世是
行是訓曉然知大經之所在甚以善養人
之心誠可以追堯舜而齊湯武者也猗歟
盛哉然道統相繼歷
列聖如一人制作相同閱百世如一日
誥編所載申明五常之條五教育民之訓
三書所載孝子仁人之事君臣父子之道皆
punctuated:
典，以風化當時，垂憲萬世，使人由之而不知，化之而莫測也。粤自堯舜帝天下，而典謨之書以著；湯武王天下，而訓誥之書以成。洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝創造洪業，條成《大誥》三編；太宗文皇帝繼志述事，御製《孝順事實》《爲善陰騭》二書；宣宗章皇帝嗣纘大統，表輯經傳，纂爲《五倫》一書。天施縟藻，昭回於雲漢之間；宸翰奎章，煒煌於宇宙之內。皆欲天下後世是行是訓，曉然知大經之所在，甚以善養人之心，誠可以追堯舜而齊湯武者也。猗歟盛哉！
然道統相繼，歷列聖如一人；制作相同，閱百世如一日。《誥》編所載申明五常之條、五教育民之訓，三書所載孝子仁人之事、君臣父子之道，皆
translation_en:
…canonical writings, with which to transform the customs of their own age and bequeath standards for ten thousand generations, so that people followed them without knowing it and were transformed without fathoming how. From the time when Yao and Shun ruled All under Heaven as emperors, the books of Canons and Counsels became manifest; when Tang and Wu ruled All under Heaven as kings, the books of Instructions and Announcements were completed. We reverently reflect that our dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao founded its great enterprise and set forth the Great Announcements (Da Gao) in three compilations. Emperor Taizong Wen carried forward his predecessor’s intentions and undertakings, imperially composing two books: Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi) and Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Weishan Yinzhi). Emperor Xuanzong Zhang succeeded to the great imperial line, collected material from the classics and their commentaries [?], and compiled it into a single book, the Five Relationships (Wulun). Their heavenly outpourings of rich literary ornament shine amid the Milky Way; their imperial writings, resplendent as the constellation Kui, blaze throughout the universe. All sought to have the people of the world and later generations practice these things and take them as instruction, clearly understanding where the great constant principles reside. Their intent to nurture people through goodness [?] truly enables them to follow Yao and Shun and stand equal to Tang and Wu. Ah, how magnificent!
Yet the succession in the transmission of the Way makes the successive sage emperors seem like a single person; the agreement of their institutions and writings makes a hundred generations seem like a single day. The provisions elucidating the Five Constants and the instructions for educating the people through the Five Teachings recorded in the Announcements, together with the deeds of filial sons and humane men and the ways of ruler and minister, father and son recorded in the three books, all…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
一大經之所在未嘗不相符合也其與典
謨所謂親睦九族愼徽五典之詞訓誥所
謂肇脩人紀重民五敎之語同一大經之
所在未嘗不相表裏也夫大經莫重於人
倫懇請以克盡五倫者爲執事陳之漢高
祖初入秦也謂父老苦於苛虐而約法三
章文帝始即位也慮鰥寡阽於溝壑而議
寬賑貸以君道揆之可謂仁矣張善相知
效君命不畏世充之攻願喪首而不顧瀕
===
昊鄉恪守忠義不從祿山之叛雖斷舌而
不恤以臣道律之可謂忠矣思驪侈之可
懼集家誡書於屛風者房玄齡也知富貴
之靡常以儉約率其子弟者王旦也此愛
而能勞無愧乎父道焉借其妻貸錢以葬
父者董永也與其婦傭身以養母者姜詩
也此貧而能孝無忝乎子職焉常林夫耕
妻饁雖處田野而相敬如賓山濤始微終
貴雖爵十乘而不娶嬪媵德之盛也可見
punctuated: 一大經之所在，未嘗不相符合也。其與典謨所謂親睦九族、愼徽五典之詞，訓誥所謂肇脩人紀、重民五敎之語，同一大經之所在，未嘗不相表裏也。夫大經莫重於人倫，懇請以克盡五倫者爲執事陳之。漢高祖初入秦也，謂父老苦於苛虐，而約法三章；文帝始即位也，慮鰥寡阽於溝壑，而議寬賑貸。以君道揆之，可謂仁矣。張善相知效君命，不畏世充之攻，願喪首而不顧；瀕昊鄉恪守忠義，不從祿山之叛，雖斷舌而不恤。以臣道律之，可謂忠矣。思驪侈之可懼，集家誡書於屛風者，房玄齡也；知富貴之靡常，以儉約率其子弟者，王旦也。此愛而能勞，無愧乎父道焉。借其妻貸錢以葬父者，董永也；與其婦傭身以養母者，姜詩也。此貧而能孝，無忝乎子職焉。常林夫耕妻饁，雖處田野，而相敬如賓；山濤始微終貴，雖爵十乘，而不娶嬪媵。德之盛也，可見。
translation_en:
…the locus of the same great constant principles, never failing to accord with one another. They likewise embody the same great constant principles as the words in the Canons and Counsels concerning “bringing harmony and affection to the nine degrees of kinship” and “carefully making the five teachings illustrious,” and the statements in the Instructions and Announcements concerning “beginning to cultivate human relationships” and “giving weight to the people’s five teachings.” They have never failed to complement one another. Among these great constant principles, nothing is weightier than human relationships. I respectfully beg leave to set before you examples of those who fully discharged their duties within the five relationships.

When Emperor Gaozu of Han first entered Qin, he declared that the elders had suffered under harsh oppression and reduced the laws to three articles. When Emperor Wen first ascended the throne, he feared that widowers and widows stood on the brink of perishing in the ditches, and deliberated on generous relief and loans. Judged by the Way of the ruler, these acts may be called benevolent.

Zhang Shanxiang understood that he should carry out his sovereign’s commands [?]. Unafraid of Shichong’s attack, he was willing to lose his head without regard for himself. Bin Haoxiang [?] steadfastly upheld loyalty and righteousness and refused to join Lushan’s rebellion; even when his tongue was cut out, he showed no concern. Measured by the Way of the minister, these acts may be called loyal.

It was Fang Xuanling who, mindful of the dangers of extravagance [?], gathered family admonitions and wrote them on a screen. It was Wang Dan who, knowing that wealth and eminence are impermanent, led his sons and younger kinsmen by an example of frugality. These men loved their children while making them undertake toil, and were worthy of the Way of the father.

It was Dong Yong who borrowed money through his wife [?] to bury his father. It was Jiang Shi who, together with his wife, hired himself out to support his mother. Poor though they were, they practiced filial devotion and brought no disgrace upon the duties of a son.

Chang Lin tilled the fields while his wife brought him food. Though they lived in the countryside, they treated one another with the respect accorded to guests. Shan Tao began in humble circumstances and eventually attained eminence, yet even with a rank commanding ten carriages, he took no concubines. Here the fullness of their virtue can be seen.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
盧氏泣玄齡之議言入惟剔目以明無貳
李氏歸王凝之遺骨引斧斷臂以示不辱
節之壯也可知他若庾兄弟不惑毋意而
友愛甚篤王覽之與兄王祥也相對終日
而並敦義讓者非揚播之與弟椿津乎待
朋友念甚故舊而同席以食樓護之於呂
公也憫其遺孤而分屋以居者非張裔之
於楊恭乎此皆能篤乎人倫之常大經之
道者也然五倫之道無在而不具故其人
===
之行無往而不合漢高帝爲民而約法三
章即
詔編與民同樂之條也顏杲卿爲君而恪守
忠義即
詔編竭忠成全之旨也董永之償錢葬父盧
氏之剔目示夫柔之
事實所載原平備作聞氏養姑者何異哉山
濤之不娶嬪滕樸護之不忘故舊比之
陰隲所紀叔通娶啞道琮葬友者何殊也
punctuated: 盧氏泣玄齡之議言入，惟剔目以明無貳；李氏歸王凝之遺骨，引斧斷臂以示不辱。節之壯也可知。他若庾兄弟不惑毋意而友愛甚篤，王覽之與兄王祥也；相對終日而並敦義讓者，非揚播之與弟椿、津乎？待朋友，念甚故舊而同席以食，樓護之於呂公也；憫其遺孤而分屋以居者，非張裔之於楊恭乎？此皆能篤乎人倫之常、大經之道者也。然五倫之道，無在而不具，故其人之行，無往而不合。漢高帝爲民而約法三章，即《詔編》與民同樂之條也；顏杲卿爲君而恪守忠義，即《詔編》竭忠成全之旨也。董永之償錢葬父、盧氏之剔目示夫，柔之《事實》所載原平備作、聞氏養姑者何異哉？山濤之不娶嬪滕、樸護之不忘故舊，比之《陰隲》所紀叔通娶啞、道琮葬友者何殊也？
translation_en:
Lady Lu wept on hearing Xuanling's suggestion [?] and gouged out an eye to demonstrate that she would never give her allegiance to another husband. Lady Li brought home Wang Ning's remains and took an axe to sever her arm, demonstrating that she would not suffer dishonor. From these examples one can recognize the strength of their integrity. As for the Yu brothers, who were not swayed by their mother's wishes [?] and were deeply devoted to one another—such was Wang Lan's relationship with his elder brother Wang Xiang. And those who spent whole days together, both cultivating righteousness and deference—were they not Yang Bo and his younger brothers Chun and Jin? In treating friends, Lou Hu cherished his old companion Lord Lü and shared his dining mat with him. And the man who pitied his friend's orphaned children and gave them part of his house to live in—was this not Zhang Yi in his treatment of Yang Gong's family? All these people were steadfast in the enduring norms of human relationships and the Way of the great guiding principles.

Yet the Way of the five relationships is present everywhere in its entirety; thus these people's conduct accorded with it wherever they went. Emperor Gao of Han established a compact of three laws for the people: this corresponds to the provision on sharing enjoyment with the people in the Compilation of Imperial Proclamations (Zhaobian). Yan Gaoqing scrupulously upheld loyalty and righteousness for his ruler: this corresponds to the Compilation's injunction to exhaust one's loyalty and bring matters to fulfillment. How do Dong Yong's repayment of money for his father's burial and Lady Lu's gouging out her eye to demonstrate fidelity to her husband differ from the accounts in Factual Deeds (Shishi) of Yuan Ping undertaking labor [?] and Lady Wen supporting her mother-in-law? [The connecting wording is corrupt.] How do Shan Tao's refusal to take concubines and Pu Hu's [?] remembrance of old friends differ from the accounts in Hidden Virtue (Yinzhi) of Shutong marrying a mute woman and Daozong burying his friend?

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
其大槩之同則其餘可類推矣愚也莊誦
聖製雖已有年而博通之學全未有得惟執事
進而教之
第二問
胡　縻
同考試官訓導張　批〔是策隨問隨荅考擬詳而事實悉具見留心書論他日致用肯不蹈古今之〕
弊歟
同考試官教諭袁　批〔荅歷代名宦人物策最為詳悉且華力光徒文采燁然其尚友千古景仰前〕
修久矣置之優選與論攸歸
===
考試官教諭羅　批〔古人事實條對無遺有見高山仰止之意〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔荅者掛一漏十求其備無遺者惟此非博洽之士能乎〕
賢才有關於世道大矣萃此邦而為名宦
也建功業於當時産此邦而為人物也垂
休光於後世故慕其名不可以不知其人
punctuated:
其大槩之同，則其餘可類推矣。愚也莊誦聖製，雖已有年，而博通之學全未有得，惟執事進而教之。
第二問
胡　縻
同考試官訓導張　批〔是策隨問隨荅，考擬詳而事實悉具，見留心書論。他日致用，肯不蹈古今之〕弊歟？
同考試官教諭袁　批〔荅歷代名宦人物策，最為詳悉，且華力光徒，文采燁然。其尚友千古，景仰前〕修久矣。置之優選，與論攸歸。
考試官教諭羅　批〔古人事實，條對無遺，有見高山仰止之意。〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔荅者掛一漏十，求其備無遺者，惟此。非博洽之士能乎？〕
賢才有關於世道大矣！萃此邦而為名宦也，建功業於當時；産此邦而為人物也，垂休光於後世。故慕其名，不可以不知其人。
translation_en:
…Since their broad outlines agree, the remaining cases can be inferred by analogy. Though I, in my ignorance, have reverently recited the imperial compositions for years, I have gained nothing in the way of comprehensive learning. I ask only that you, honored examiners, guide me onward and instruct me.
Second Question
Hu Mi 胡縻
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: “This policy essay answers each question in turn. Its examination and comparisons are detailed, and the historical facts are all supplied, showing attentive study of writings and discussions. When he puts his learning to use in the future, surely he will avoid [?] the failings of past and present?”
Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “The response to the policy question on distinguished officials and notable figures of successive dynasties is exceptionally detailed and comprehensive. Moreover, its brilliance and force shine forth [?], and its literary expression is radiant. He has long sought fellowship with the worthies of antiquity and revered his virtuous predecessors. Placing him among the superior selections accords with common judgment [?].”
Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: “The deeds of the ancients are addressed point by point, with nothing omitted. One can discern the sentiment expressed in ‘looking up to a lofty mountain.’”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Respondents generally mention one thing while omitting ten. If one seeks a response that is complete and leaves nothing out, this alone qualifies. Could anyone but a man of extensive learning achieve this?”
Worthy and talented men have a profound bearing on the moral condition of the age! Those who gather in this region and become distinguished officials establish achievements in their own time; those born in this region who become notable figures transmit their glorious renown to later generations. Thus, in admiring their reputations, one must know the men themselves…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
求其人爲可以不論其世歟噫尚友千古
景行先哲學者事也執事以山東之名宦
人物詢承學盖欲啓後生小子尚友之心
大哉問也敢不悉心以對乎且以名宦言
有仁惠及民而老幼留於既去之日若劉
寵也以恩信綏盜而政績稱爲天下之首
者李固也水患民憂分導水勢而民賴以
安非吕夷簡而何歲饑民盜請弛鹽禁而
歲豐乃復非王博文而何曾鞏秩滿代去
===
民猶未忍而絶橋以留高源去官十年民
終不忘而立碑以頌德之深也可知吳琚
選人有爭訟輙閉閤自責吏以是不忍於
欺紫禹錫當兵起契冊即内嚴備禦怨由
是尋自引去政之善也可見李師中不貴
刑罰而范仲淹因薦其有王佐之才李載
惟尚寬厚而吕夷簡獨賢其有不苛之政
嘗斷冤獄情無遁矣此趙孟頫之神明所
以稱於郡中焉事至即决才莫及矣此李
punctuated: 求其人，爲可以不論其世歟？噫！尚友千古，景行先哲，學者事也。執事以山東之名宦人物詢承學，盖欲啓後生小子尚友之心。大哉問也！敢不悉心以對乎？且以名宦言，有仁惠及民而老幼留於既去之日，若劉寵也；以恩信綏盜而政績稱爲天下之首者，李固也。水患民憂，分導水勢而民賴以安，非吕夷簡而何？歲饑民盜，請弛鹽禁而歲豐乃復，非王博文而何？曾鞏秩滿代去，民猶未忍而絶橋以留；高源去官十年，民終不忘而立碑以頌：德之深也可知。吳琚選人有爭訟，輙閉閤自責，吏以是不忍於欺；紫禹錫當兵起契冊，即内嚴備禦，怨由是尋自引去：政之善也可見。李師中不貴刑罰，而范仲淹因薦其有王佐之才；李載惟尚寬厚，而吕夷簡獨賢其有不苛之政。嘗斷冤獄，情無遁矣，此趙孟頫之神明所以稱於郡中焉；事至即决，才莫及矣，此李
translation_en:
…In seeking to know these men, can one neglect to consider the age in which they lived [?]? Ah! To take the ancients as friends across the ages and emulate the worthy philosophers of the past is the scholar’s task. You, honored examiners, have questioned us students about Shandong’s celebrated officials and eminent figures, surely wishing to awaken in us younger men the desire to befriend the ancients. How great a question this is! Dare I fail to devote my whole mind to answering it?

To speak first of celebrated officials: Liu Chong extended benevolence and kindness to the people, and young and old sought to detain him when he departed. Li Gu pacified bandits through generosity and trustworthiness, and his achievements in government were acclaimed as foremost in the realm. When floods distressed the people, who but Lü Yijian diverted the waters into separate channels, enabling the people to live in peace? When famine drove the people to banditry, who but Wang Bowen requested that the salt prohibitions be relaxed, restoring them only when harvests were plentiful again?

When Zeng Gong completed his term and departed upon being replaced, the people still could not bear to lose him and broke the bridge to detain him. Ten years after Gao Yuan left office, the people had not forgotten him and erected a stele in his praise. From this one can discern the depth of their beneficence. When litigation arose, Wu Ju would shut his chamber and reproach himself [the wording preceding “litigation” is unclear]. His clerks consequently could not bear to deceive him. When fighting broke out at Qice [?], Zi Yuxi [?] immediately strengthened internal defenses; resentment arose from this, and he soon withdrew from office of his own accord [?]. From this one can see the excellence of their government.

Li Shizhong did not place great value on punishments, and Fan Zhongyan accordingly recommended him as possessing the ability to assist a king. Li Zai prized only generosity and tolerance, and Lü Yijian singled him out for esteem because his administration was free of harshness. In adjudicating cases of wrongful imprisonment, no facts escaped him: this was why Zhao Mengfu’s extraordinary discernment was praised throughout the prefecture. He decided matters as soon as they came before him, and none could match his ability: this was why Li…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
系之姓名所以書於殿柱焉以人物言胷
薪讀誦而儒行見稱於當時者劉智也躬
耕徂徠以易經教授乎後學者石介也李
專之解經謝享與子基同時故時有二蹤
之比崔仲文以才拜官與兄伎同日故世
有兩鳳之稱九歲能文文章獨步于當時
王禹偁之才何高耶八十二登第姓名獨
冠于天下梁顥之志何堅耶王志悟以剛
鷙爲治故人以梟鷹而見呼張詠以剛方
===
爲任故自以乖崖而爲號辯曰謝顥子者
以顏延之文章冠絕與謝靈運齊名也號
曰韓夫子者以韓熙載才氣俊逸與韓昌
黎媲美也羊祜政多遺愛人望碑墮淚因
以墮淚名賈敦頤與弟刺洺人立碑並頌
因以棠棣號圖梁丘賀之形於麒麟閣非
以其小心周密乎繪秦瓊之像於凌煙閣
非以其戰伐有功乎此皆齊魯之名官人
物功業休光著於當時而垂於後世者也
punctuated:
系之姓名所以書於殿柱焉。

以人物言，胷薪讀誦而儒行見稱於當時者，劉智也；躬耕徂徠，以易經教授乎後學者，石介也。李專之解經，謝享與子基同時，故時有二蹤之比；崔仲文以才拜官，與兄伎同日，故世有兩鳳之稱。九歲能文，文章獨步于當時，王禹偁之才何高耶！八十二登第，姓名獨冠于天下，梁顥之志何堅耶！王志悟以剛鷙爲治，故人以梟鷹而見呼；張詠以剛方爲任，故自以乖崖而爲號。辯曰謝顥子者，以顏延之文章冠絕，與謝靈運齊名也；號曰韓夫子者，以韓熙載才氣俊逸，與韓昌黎媲美也。羊祜政多遺愛，人望碑墮淚，因以墮淚名；賈敦頤與弟刺洺，人立碑並頌，因以棠棣號。圖梁丘賀之形於麒麟閣，非以其小心周密乎？繪秦瓊之像於凌煙閣，非以其戰伐有功乎？此皆齊魯之名官人物，功業休光著於當時而垂於後世者也。
translation_en:
…this is why [Li] Xi’s name was inscribed on a pillar in the palace hall.

As for notable men, it was Liu Zhi who read and recited with firewood against his chest [?], and whose Confucian conduct won praise in his day. It was Shi Jie who farmed personally at Culai and taught the Book of Changes to later students. Li Zhuan expounded the classics; Xie Xiang and his son Ji were contemporaries [?], hence the comparison in their day to “two tracks” [?]. Cui Zhongwen received office for his talent on the same day as his elder brother Ji, so people called them the “two phoenixes.” Able to compose at nine, and unrivaled in literary composition in his day—how great was Wang Yucheng’s talent! Passing the examination at eighty-two, and winning a name unequaled throughout the realm—how firm was Liang Hao’s resolve! Wang Zhiwu governed with fierce severity, so people called him an owl or hawk. Zhang Yong took stern uprightness as his responsibility, and therefore styled himself Guaiya, “Contrary Cliff.” The designation “Xie Haozi” [?] was used because Yan Yanzhi’s literary compositions were unsurpassed and he shared equal fame with Xie Lingyun. The designation “Master Han” was used because Han Xizai’s talent and spirit were outstanding and untrammeled, comparable to those of Han Changli [Han Yu]. Yang Hu’s government left much enduring affection; people shed tears when they gazed at his stele, which was consequently named “Shedding Tears.” Jia Dunyi and his younger brother served as prefects of Ming; people erected a stele praising them together, and accordingly called it “Cherry Tree,” an emblem of brotherhood. Was Liangqiu He’s likeness depicted in the Qilin Pavilion not because of his care and thoroughness? Was Qin Qiong’s portrait painted in the Lingyan Pavilion not because of his achievements in warfare? These were all celebrated officials and notable men of Qi and Lu, whose achievements and splendid renown shone in their own time and were handed down to later generations.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
愚也酌幽香而起敬想遺跡而興嗟固未
嘗不以諸名宦人物自期待矣嗚呼抑孰
知有大於此者乎若吾夫子之生爲天地
立心爲生民立命爲往聖繼絶學爲萬世
開太平功業與天地而同久休光與日月
而並明萬世之下孰不欲景仰而師法哉
孟子曰乃所願則學孔子愚亦曰乃所願
則學孔子
第三問
===
同考試官訓導徐　批　〔考證詳而不泛於辭〕
李　□
〔當而不差録之以示行禮者〕
考試官教諭羅　批　〔考禮詳而詞備〕
〔識之也〕
考試官教諭汪　批　〔備考無遺故録之〕
禮本於古而後世之制終有愧於古禮備
於
今而萬世之制皆莫盛於
punctuated:
愚也酌幽香而起敬，想遺跡而興嗟，固未嘗不以諸名宦人物自期待矣。嗚呼！抑孰知有大於此者乎？若吾夫子之生，爲天地立心，爲生民立命，爲往聖繼絶學，爲萬世開太平，功業與天地而同久，休光與日月而並明，萬世之下，孰不欲景仰而師法哉？孟子曰：「乃所願，則學孔子。」愚亦曰：「乃所願，則學孔子。」

第三問

同考試官訓導徐　批　〔考證詳而不泛於辭。〕
李　□
〔當而不差，録之以示行禮者。〕
考試官教諭羅　批　〔考禮詳而詞備。〕
〔識之也。〕
考試官教諭汪　批　〔備考無遺，故録之。〕

禮本於古，而後世之制終有愧於古；禮備於今，而萬世之制皆莫盛於
translation_en:
Savoring their subtle fragrance [?], I am moved to reverence; contemplating the traces they left, I am moved to sigh. Indeed, I have always aspired to emulate these renowned officials and distinguished men. Alas! Yet who recognizes that there is something greater than this? Our Master came into the world to establish a heart for Heaven and Earth, to establish the destiny of the people, to carry forward the severed tradition of learning of the former sages, and to inaugurate peace for ten thousand generations. His achievements endure with Heaven and Earth; his splendid radiance shines alongside the sun and moon. Through ten thousand generations, who would not wish to revere him and take him as a model? Mengzi said: “As for what I wish, it is to emulate Kongzi.” I too say: “As for what I wish, it is to emulate Kongzi.”

Third Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: 〔The evidential research is detailed, without verbosity.〕
Li □ [name incomplete]
〔Appropriate and free from error; recorded here to instruct those who perform the rites.〕
Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: 〔The examination of ritual is detailed, and its exposition comprehensive.〕
〔This records it [?].〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔The investigation is comprehensive and omits nothing; hence its inclusion.〕

Ritual has its roots in antiquity, yet the institutions of later ages ultimately fall short of those of antiquity; ritual has attained completeness in the present, and among the institutions of ten thousand generations none is more flourishing than …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
今甚矣禮之難制也非德則無所本無本則
禮不行非位則無所徵無徵則民弗從德
位兼隆禮制明備此有虞三代之君與我
國朝之
列聖所以皆非漢唐宋之所能及也歟蓋嘗聞
之天高地下萬物散殊而禮制行矣斯禮
也聖人作之明其度數辨其儀文以之而
正朝廷井井乎其不可紊以之而定民心
秩秩乎其不可亂所謂安上治民莫善於
===
禮而君子之所當講也稽之於古有虞命
伯夷以典三禮所謂三禮者祀天神祭地
祇享人鬼是也周官大宗伯以五禮經邦
國所謂五禮者吉凶軍賓嘉是也王制爾
徒脩六禮以節民性所謂六禮者冠婚喪
祭鄉相見是也三禮五禮六禮目雖不同
也然無非一德之是將若夫禮器所載經
禮者經常之禮也如朝覲會同冠婚喪祭
其類有三百之多焉曲禮者委曲之禮也
punctuated:
今。甚矣，禮之難制也！非德則無所本，無本則禮不行；非位則無所徵，無徵則民弗從。德位兼隆，禮制明備，此有虞三代之君與我國朝之列聖所以皆非漢唐宋之所能及也歟！蓋嘗聞之：天高地下，萬物散殊，而禮制行矣。斯禮也，聖人作之，明其度數，辨其儀文，以之而正朝廷，井井乎其不可紊；以之而定民心，秩秩乎其不可亂。所謂安上治民，莫善於禮，而君子之所當講也。

稽之於古，有虞命伯夷以典三禮。所謂三禮者，祀天神、祭地祇、享人鬼是也。《周官》大宗伯以五禮經邦國。所謂五禮者，吉、凶、軍、賓、嘉是也。《王制》爾徒脩六禮以節民性。所謂六禮者，冠、婚、喪、祭、鄉、相見是也。三禮、五禮、六禮，目雖不同也，然無非一德之是將。若夫《禮器》所載，經禮者，經常之禮也，如朝覲、會同、冠婚喪祭，其類有三百之多焉；曲禮者，委曲之禮也。
translation_en:
…the present. How difficult it is to establish rites! Without virtue, they have no foundation; without a foundation, rites cannot be put into practice. Without rank, they have no warrant; without a warrant, the people will not follow them. Virtue and rank alike exalted, and ritual institutions clear and complete: is this not why the rulers of Youyu and the Three Dynasties, together with the successive sage emperors of our own dynasty, are all beyond what the Han, Tang, and Song could attain? I have heard it said: Heaven is high and earth low; the myriad things are distributed in their diversity; and the order of ritual operates among them. The sages created these rites, clarified their measures and prescribed numbers, and distinguished their ceremonial forms. With them they set the court in order, so systematically that it cannot fall into confusion; with them they settle the hearts of the people, so methodically that they cannot fall into disorder. This is what is meant by saying that nothing surpasses rites for securing those above and governing the people. They are therefore something the gentleman ought to study.

Examining antiquity, we find that the ruler of Youyu commanded Bo Yi to take charge of the three rites. These three rites were offerings to the spirits of Heaven, sacrifices to the deities of Earth, and offerings to human spirits. In the Offices of Zhou, the Minister of Rites ordered the states through the five rites. These five rites were the auspicious, mourning, military, guest, and celebratory rites. In the Royal Regulations, the Minister of Education [?; transcribed as 爾徒] cultivated the six rites to regulate the people's dispositions. These six rites were capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, village ceremonies, and formal meetings. Although the categories of the three, five, and six rites differ, all serve to express a single virtue. As for what is recorded in Ritual Vessels, the major rites are the constant, regular rites, such as court audiences, assemblies and meetings, capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice; their categories number as many as three hundred. The detailed rites are rites governing particulars…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
如升降進退俯仰揖遜其類有三千之盛
焉經禮三百曲禮三千條目雖多也然無
非一敬之是敷非若後世之禮徒事乎繁
文末節而已是故炎漢之初叔孫通制綿
蕝之禮而其效僅至於羣臣震恐無敢諠
譁者盖當爭雄角力之餘一旦見夫禮制
之行遽有以銷其暴戾之心收其怠慢之
容故遂至於震懼而不敢肆耳漢高以爲
上得天下不事詩書非必世能仁之主也
===
此魯兩生所以不至而其禮豈能有合於
古歟唐有開元顯慶二禮宋有開寳政
和五禮觀其所制雖曰愈於綿蕝而亦未
見其合於古者豈非其德終有媿於古之
聖人而其禮自不能備自不可行也歟古
之禮信善矣然而有不能行於後世者非
古之禮不可行而行之非其人耳晦庵朱
子之論禮制必以古禮爲據而裁之豈無
見乎哉
punctuated: 如升降進退、俯仰揖遜，其類有三千之盛焉。經禮三百，曲禮三千，條目雖多也，然無非一敬之是敷，非若後世之禮徒事乎繁文末節而已。是故炎漢之初，叔孫通制綿蕝之禮，而其效僅至於羣臣震恐，無敢諠譁者。盖當爭雄角力之餘，一旦見夫禮制之行，遽有以銷其暴戾之心，收其怠慢之容，故遂至於震懼而不敢肆耳。漢高以爲上得天下，不事詩書，非必世能仁之主也。此魯兩生所以不至，而其禮豈能有合於古歟？唐有開元、顯慶二禮，宋有開寳、政和五禮。觀其所制，雖曰愈於綿蕝，而亦未見其合於古者，豈非其德終有媿於古之聖人，而其禮自不能備、自不可行也歟？古之禮信善矣，然而有不能行於後世者，非古之禮不可行，而行之非其人耳。晦庵朱子之論禮制，必以古禮爲據而裁之，豈無見乎哉？
translation_en:
…such as ascending and descending, advancing and withdrawing, bowing and straightening oneself, saluting with clasped hands, and yielding precedence: these amount to as many as three thousand kinds. There are three hundred principal rites and three thousand detailed observances. Although their provisions are numerous, all express the single principle of reverence. They are unlike the rites of later ages, which attend merely to elaborate formalities and minor details.

Thus, at the beginning of the Han dynasty, Shusun Tong devised ceremonies rehearsed with cords and bundles of thatch, yet their effect extended only to making the assembled ministers tremble with fear, so that none dared raise a clamor. Coming just after the struggle for supremacy through force, they suddenly witnessed ritual regulations being put into practice. These checked their violent impulses and restrained their negligent demeanor, so that they became fearful and dared not behave wantonly. Emperor Gao of Han believed that, having gained the empire [on horseback?], he need not attend to the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. He was no ruler capable of achieving humane government within a generation. This is why the two scholars from Lu refused to come. How, then, could his rites accord with those of antiquity?

The Tang had the two ritual codes of the Kaiyuan and Xianqing eras; the Song had the Five Rites of the Kaibao and Zhenghe eras. Examining what they prescribed, we may call them an improvement over the ceremonies rehearsed with cords and bundles of thatch, yet we still do not find them consonant with antiquity. Was this not because the virtue of those rulers ultimately fell short of that of the ancient sages, so that their rites could neither be complete nor be put into practice?

The rites of antiquity were indeed excellent. Nevertheless, where they could not be practiced in later ages, it was not that the ancient rites were impracticable, but simply that those implementing them were not the right people. When Master Zhu, known as Hui’an, discussed ritual institutions, he invariably took the ancient rites as his basis and adapted them accordingly. Surely he had insight in doing so!

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
皇明以禮治天下有
令有
制有職掌孝慈諸書凡君臣父子之大倫朝
覲會同之盛禮冠婚喪祭之大端與凡事
物文為之懿無一不備與有虞三代之諸
禮皆相符合誠萬世不刋之典也而又
敕天下臣民得參用朱子家禮禮制之備
莫備於斯矣天下守之如一國而國不異
政國守之如一家而家不殊俗家守之如
===
一人而人不異行囿斯民於天序天秩之
中納斯民於五禮五典之內比屋可封人
人君子漢唐以下豈足以彷彿萬一而愚
生又惡敢舉一二以見其盛哉
王景連
考試官教諭羅　批〔能本先儒評史守論可取〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔論作史之法有源委有斷制〕
蓋嘗究心於史學者也
第四問
punctuated:
皇明以禮治天下，有《令》，有《制》，有《職掌》《孝慈》諸書。凡君臣父子之大倫、朝覲會同之盛禮、冠婚喪祭之大端，與凡事物文為之懿，無一不備，與有虞三代之諸禮皆相符合，誠萬世不刋之典也。而又敕天下臣民得參用《朱子家禮》，禮制之備，莫備於斯矣。天下守之如一國，而國不異政；國守之如一家，而家不殊俗；家守之如一人，而人不異行。囿斯民於天序天秩之中，納斯民於五禮五典之內，比屋可封，人人君子。漢唐以下，豈足以彷彿萬一？而愚生又惡敢舉一二以見其盛哉！
王景連。
考試官教諭羅　批〔能本先儒評史，守論可取。〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔論作史之法，有源委，有斷制。〕
蓋嘗究心於史學者也。
第四問
translation_en:
Our august Ming governs all under Heaven through ritual. It has the Ordinances, the Regulations, and such books as the Duties of Offices and Filial Piety and Maternal Kindness. These fully provide for the cardinal relationships between ruler and minister and between father and son; the grand rites of court audiences and assemblies; the principal ceremonies of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice; and all the refinements of ritual forms and observances. They accord in every respect with the rites of Shun and the Three Dynasties and are truly canons that shall remain unaltered for ten thousand generations. Furthermore, an imperial command permits subjects throughout the realm to draw also upon Master Zhu’s Family Rituals. No ritual system could be more complete than this. All under Heaven observe it as though they were a single state, so that states do not differ in their governance; each state observes it as though it were a single household, so that households do not differ in their customs; each household observes it as though it were a single person, so that people do not differ in their conduct. It encompasses the people within Heaven’s ordering of relationships and rites and brings them within the Five Rites and the Five Constant Relationships. Every household has people worthy of enfeoffment, and everyone is a gentleman. How could the Han, the Tang, or any subsequent dynasty approximate even a ten-thousandth part of this? And how could I, an ignorant student, presume to convey its grandeur by citing merely one or two examples?
Wang Jinglian.
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “He can ground his assessment of history in the earlier Confucian scholars; the position he maintains is commendable [?].”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “His discussion of the methods of writing history traces their origins and development and offers decisive judgments.”
He has evidently devoted careful thought to the study of history.
Fourth Question.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
作史者本於春秋則是非有定見而予奪
皆合乎天下之公故史者本於春秋則是
非有定論而折衷不謬於聖人之言大哉
春秋之義乎其聖人經世之要乎王者本
之以脩政立事則一代之王法在是也況
作史乎本之以垂訓立教則一代之典章
在是也況故史乎春秋之義其大如此何
以言之聖人之經載乎道聖人之道本諸
心心明則道明道明則凡所以爲經者皆
===
欲以明道也春秋列國中之一史爾孔子
假而脩之以寓一王之法實史外傳心之
要典也茍無聖人之心胷而欲讀其書通
其義難矣況欲擬之以立言乎先儒病學
者不先治經而治史以爲倒學乎無得於
是非予奪之公有以也司馬遷非聖人之
徒也史記一書其能有合於春秋之旨乎
觀其著十二本紀十表八書三十世家七
十列傳凡百三十篇馳騁數千載間勤亦
punctuated:
作史者本於《春秋》，則是非有定見，而予奪皆合乎天下之公；故史者本於《春秋》，則是非有定論，而折衷不謬於聖人之言。大哉，《春秋》之義乎！其聖人經世之要乎！王者本之以脩政立事，則一代之王法在是也，況作史乎？本之以垂訓立教，則一代之典章在是也，況故史乎？《春秋》之義其大如此，何以言之？聖人之經載乎道，聖人之道本諸心。心明則道明，道明則凡所以爲經者，皆欲以明道也。

《春秋》，列國中之一史爾。孔子假而脩之，以寓一王之法，實史外傳心之要典也。茍無聖人之心胷，而欲讀其書、通其義，難矣！況欲擬之以立言乎？先儒病學者不先治經而治史，以爲倒學乎？無得於是非予奪之公，有以也。

司馬遷非聖人之徒也，《史記》一書，其能有合於《春秋》之旨乎？觀其著十二本紀、十表、八書、三十世家、七十列傳，凡百三十篇，馳騁數千載間，勤亦
translation_en:
When those who write history take the Spring and Autumn Annals as their foundation, they have settled judgments of right and wrong, and their praise and blame accord with the impartial judgment of all under Heaven. When those concerned with earlier histories [?] take the Spring and Autumn Annals as their foundation, their conclusions about right and wrong are settled, and their adjudications do not depart from the sage’s words. How great are the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals! Are they not the essentials by which the sage orders the world? If a king takes them as his foundation in reforming government and establishing undertakings, the royal laws of an entire age are embodied in them. How much more, then, for writing history? If he takes them as his foundation in bequeathing instruction and establishing teachings, the institutions of an entire age are embodied in them. How much more, then, for earlier histories [?]? The principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals are so great: how can this be explained? The sage’s classics carry the Way, and the sage’s Way is rooted in his mind. When the mind is clear, the Way is clear; when the Way is clear, everything through which he composes the classics is intended to illuminate the Way.

The Spring and Autumn Annals was merely one history among those of the various states. Kongzi took it up and revised it to embody the laws of a true king; it is, in fact, an essential classic that transmits his mind beyond the historical record itself. Without the sage’s breadth of mind, it is difficult to read his book and comprehend its meaning. How much more difficult to emulate it in establishing teachings through writing! Earlier Confucian scholars deplored students’ studying history before studying the classics: did they not regard this as learning in reverse order? There is a reason why such students fail to grasp impartiality in judging right and wrong and assigning praise and blame.

Sima Qian was no follower of the sage. Could his Records of the Grand Historian accord with the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals? Consider how he composed twelve Basic Annals, ten Tables, eight Treatises, thirty Hereditary Houses, and seventy Biographies—130 chapters in all—ranging freely across several thousand years. His diligence, too, …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
至矣劉向揚雄咸稱其有良史才服其善
叙事理辯而不華質而不俚其文直其事
核不虛美不隱惡謂之實録若有得矣至
其論大道則先黃老而後六經序遊俠則
退處士而進奸雄傳貨殖則崇勢利而羞
貧賤豈能免班固謬於聖人之誚乎所謂
不能合於春秋者此也若夫班固范曄陳
壽之徒相繼而作則又不過依倣遷法而
爲之非遷比也遷且不及况望其過之而
===
有得於春秋之旨哉迨宋歐陽脩作五代
史其立例始寓春秋之意至其爲論每篇
必以嗚呼發之蓋以爲亂世之書而致嘆
也至於叙述則文簡而能暢事增而不贅
觀其篇名曰家人傳則帝王正家之義見
矣曰梁臣傳唐臣傳則忠臣不事二君之
義昭矣曰死節傳死事傳則人臣之伏節
死義者傳矣曰一行傳非以著士之高尚
者乎曰唐六臣傳非以明臣之背附者乎
punctuated:
至矣。劉向、揚雄咸稱其有良史才，服其善叙事理，辯而不華，質而不俚，其文直，其事核，不虛美，不隱惡，謂之實録，若有得矣。至其論大道，則先黃老而後六經；序遊俠，則退處士而進奸雄；傳貨殖，則崇勢利而羞貧賤。豈能免班固謬於聖人之誚乎？所謂不能合於春秋者，此也。若夫班固、范曄、陳壽之徒，相繼而作，則又不過依倣遷法而爲之，非遷比也。遷且不及，况望其過之而有得於春秋之旨哉？

迨宋歐陽脩作五代史，其立例始寓春秋之意。至其爲論，每篇必以嗚呼發之，蓋以爲亂世之書而致嘆也。至於叙述，則文簡而能暢，事增而不贅。觀其篇名，曰家人傳，則帝王正家之義見矣；曰梁臣傳、唐臣傳，則忠臣不事二君之義昭矣；曰死節傳、死事傳，則人臣之伏節死義者傳矣；曰一行傳，非以著士之高尚者乎？曰唐六臣傳，非以明臣之背附者乎？
translation_en:
…was indeed utmost. Liu Xiang and Yang Xiong both praised him as possessing the talent of a fine historian. They admired his skill in narrating events and their underlying principles: eloquent without ornament, plain without vulgarity. His writing was straightforward and his facts verified; he neither bestowed unfounded praise nor concealed evil. They called it a truthful record, suggesting that he had attained something of the Way. Yet in discussing the Great Way, he placed the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi before the Six Classics; in recounting the wandering knights, he disparaged scholars in retirement and exalted unscrupulous men of power; and in writing the biographies of those who amassed wealth, he esteemed power and profit and treated poverty and low status as shameful. How could he escape Ban Gu’s criticism that he departed from the sage’s teachings? This is what is meant by his failure to accord with the Spring and Autumn Annals. As for Ban Gu, Fan Ye, Chen Shou, and their like, who wrote in succession, they did no more than imitate Sima Qian’s methods and were no match for him. Since they could not even equal Qian, how could one expect them to surpass him and grasp the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals?

Only when Ouyang Xiu of the Song composed the History of the Five Dynasties did the principles of historical composition begin to embody the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals. In his appraisals, he invariably opened each piece with “Alas!” This was presumably because he regarded his work as a record of an age of disorder and therefore voiced his lament. As for his narration, its language is concise yet fluent, and its account of events fuller without becoming prolix. Consider the titles of its chapters: “Biographies of Family Members” reveals the principle that emperors and kings must put their households in order. “Biographies of Ministers of Liang” and “Biographies of Ministers of Tang” make clear the principle that loyal ministers do not serve two rulers. “Biographies of Those Who Died for Their Integrity” and “Biographies of Those Who Died in Service” transmit accounts of ministers who remained steadfast in their integrity and died for righteousness. Is “Biographies of Men Distinguished by a Single Virtue” not intended to manifest the lofty character of scholars? Is “Biographies of Six Ministers of Tang” not intended to expose ministers’ abandonment of one allegiance for another?

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
曰雖傳則歷世累朝之臣無操守者也宜
脩之言曰吾用春秋之法師其義不襲其
文論者稱其紀述之功不在遷下非以遷
與脩等也紀例精密非遷所及則稱之者
意也觀者不以文害辭可也其後紫陽朱
夫子出作爲通鑑綱目表歲以首年而因
年以著統大書以提要而分註以備言歲
周於上而天道明矣統正於下而人道定
矣大綱既舉而鑒戒昭矣衆目畢張而幾
===
微著矣至其大義所在則尊正統即春秋
大一統之義也於中宗每歲書帝所在即
春秋書公在乾侯之義也至於隨事褒貶
若黜曹魏以正僞尊昭烈以明統楊雄仕
於漢而曰莽大夫陶潛卒於宋而曰晉徵
士誅奸諛於既死發潛德之幽光詞嚴義
正炳如日星何莫非春秋之義乎噫以諸
子言之遷之博學洽聞固非班輩所能及
而脩之義例精密又非遷所能及矣然而
punctuated: 曰雖傳，則歷世累朝之臣無操守者也。宜脩之言曰：「吾用春秋之法，師其義，不襲其文。」論者稱其紀述之功不在遷下，非以遷與脩等也；紀例精密，非遷所及，則稱之者意也。觀者不以文害辭可也。其後紫陽朱夫子出，作爲通鑑綱目，表歲以首年，而因年以著統；大書以提要，而分註以備言。歲周於上，而天道明矣；統正於下，而人道定矣；大綱既舉，而鑒戒昭矣；衆目畢張，而幾微著矣。至其大義所在，則尊正統，即春秋大一統之義也；於中宗每歲書帝所在，即春秋書公在乾侯之義也。至於隨事褒貶，若黜曹魏以正僞，尊昭烈以明統，楊雄仕於漢而曰莽大夫，陶潛卒於宋而曰晉徵士，誅奸諛於既死，發潛德之幽光，詞嚴義正，炳如日星，何莫非春秋之義乎？噫！以諸子言之，遷之博學洽聞，固非班輩所能及，而脩之義例精密，又非遷所能及矣。然而，
translation_en:
…As for the section called “Miscellaneous Biographies” [?], it concerns ministers who served successive reigns and dynasties without maintaining their integrity. It was fitting that Ouyang Xiu should say: “I employ the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, taking its principles as my guide without copying its wording.” When critics praise his achievement in historical narration as no less than Sima Qian’s, they do not mean that Qian and Xiu are equal in every respect. Their meaning is that the precision of Xiu’s historiographical conventions surpasses what Qian attained. Readers should simply avoid letting individual words obscure the meaning of the statement.

Afterward, Master Zhu of Ziyang appeared and composed the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror. He placed calendrical designations at the head of each year’s entry and used the sequence of years to indicate legitimate succession. He wrote the essentials prominently as an outline and supplied separate annotations to give the full account. With the years set out completely above, the Way of Heaven became clear; with legitimate succession correctly established below, the human order became settled. Once the main outline was raised, historical lessons and warnings became manifest; once all the detailed entries were displayed, subtle beginnings became apparent.

As for its great principles, its honoring of legitimate succession embodies the Spring and Autumn Annals’ principle of honoring unified rule. Its recording of the emperor’s whereabouts in each year under Zhongzong embodies the principle behind the Annals’ recording that the duke was at Ganhou. As for its assigning praise and blame according to events, it demotes Cao Wei to rectify claims to legitimacy and expose usurpation, and honors Zhaolie to clarify legitimate succession. Although Yang Xiong served under the Han, it calls him a grand master of Wang Mang; although Tao Qian died under the Song, it calls him a scholar summoned to office under the Jin. It condemns treacherous flatterers after their deaths and brings forth the hidden radiance of unrecognized virtue. Its language is stern and its principles correct, shining like the sun and stars. Which of these does not embody the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals?

Ah! Speaking of these several writers, Qian’s broad learning and extensive knowledge were certainly beyond the reach of Ban Gu and his like; yet the precision of Xiu’s interpretive principles and historiographical conventions was likewise beyond Qian’s reach. Nevertheless…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
求其上足以承春秋之墜緒下可以爲萬
世之昭鑒者會綱目具何以哉學孔子者
先學朱子可也管見如斯未知是否惟執
事其進教之
第五問
徐□德
同考試官訓導蕭　批　〔時務一策關□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□措置有方者辟此作窮之所養即達之所施也故錄□□〕
同考試官教諭姜　批　〔策問時務欲觀其□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
===
同考試官教諭楊　批　〔策有斷制非識時務□□□□□□□□□□□□□□致用之才此篇對酌得宜舉而措之無難矣〕
考試官教諭羅　批　〔以得人爲說最是不能允宜高薦〕
考試官教諭汪　批　〔五策俱可觀惟時務一篇□□置允當不謂之俊傑可乎〕
治天下之道存乎法舉天下之法存乎人
法者道之寓非法則道不能以自見人者
法之具非人則法不能以自行故治天下
punctuated:
求其上足以承春秋之墜緒，下可以爲萬世之昭鑒者，會綱目具何以哉？學孔子者，先學朱子可也。管見如斯，未知是否，惟執事其進教之。

第五問
徐□德
同考試官訓導蕭　批　〔時務一策，關□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□措置有方者，辟此作，窮之所養，即達之所施也，故錄□□〕
同考試官教諭姜　批　〔策問時務，欲觀其□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
同考試官教諭楊　批　〔策有斷制，非識時務□□□□□□□□□□□□□□致用之才。此篇對酌得宜，舉而措之無難矣。〕
考試官教諭羅　批　〔以得人爲說，最是不能，允宜高薦。〕
考試官教諭汪　批　〔五策俱可觀，惟時務一篇□□置允當，不謂之俊傑可乎？〕

治天下之道存乎法，舉天下之法存乎人。法者，道之寓，非法則道不能以自見；人者，法之具，非人則法不能以自行。故治天下
translation_en:
…if we seek a work sufficient, looking backward, to carry on the fallen legacy of the Spring and Autumn Annals and, looking forward, to serve as a clear mirror for all generations, is it the Outline and Details (Gangmu) alone, and why?
