Is this not the heart of ease, uprightness, kindness, and goodness entering the realm of the spiritual? Ah! Such is the power of music to transform the human heart. Is this not why music must never leave one's person, even for a moment? In general, both the heart within and the person without require the learner's devoted effort; neither may be neglected. Thus the gentlemen of antiquity fully employed music to govern the heart, making all within harmonious, and fully employed ritual to govern their persons, making all without accord with proper order. Thereby they could move people and influence things; extending this throughout the realm presented no difficulty.

Second Session
Discourse
The Preeminent Master of the Way and Virtue for All Ages
Xu Chongde

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Assistant Instructor: “With restraint and emphasis, rises and falls, this is a fine composition. What doubt can there be about recommending it for a high place?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The argument is precise and thorough, and the textual evidence clear. Moreover, its prose technique and organization are splendid to behold: reading it makes one tremble as though our Master stood before us. To find a scholar such as you among hundreds and thousands—who would not treasure him?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: “The diction has an antique gravity, and the writing is mature and vigorous. He must be a man of learning. He deserves a place among the foremost selections; why should he not be recommended first?”

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭羅　批　〔筆力高古議論的當〕
〔場中之魁楚者也〕
考試官教諭汪　批　〔作者詞浮無擬是篇推明〕
〔道德宗主鑿鑿乎其實也且文勢滔滔豈稗筆所能及耶〕
論曰平水土以奠民萬世之功也然而不
能救人心之陷溺躬稼穡以粒民萬世之
功也然而不能保人心之淪亡患可有也
人心不可溺也食可去也人心不可亡也
然則萬世之功其歸之孔子乎孔子刪述
===
六經以爲萬世道德之宗主所以救人心
之陷溺者在是所以保人心之淪亡者在
是所以參天地贊化育而立人極於千萬
世者在是孔子之功萬世之功也使世無
孔子則六經不備六經不備則道德蔑聞
天下後世之人將貿貿焉如聾如瞶戴天
行日而莫之聞見也雖安居於水土之上
飽食於稼穡之餘靈於物而實不異於物
矣如人心何世道何有若曰自生民以來
punctuated:
考試官教諭羅批：〔筆力高古，議論的當。〕〔場中之魁楚者也。〕

考試官教諭汪批：〔作者詞浮無擬，是篇推明〕〔道德宗主，鑿鑿乎其實也。且文勢滔滔，豈稗筆所能及耶？〕

論曰：平水土以奠民，萬世之功也，然而不能救人心之陷溺；躬稼穡以粒民，萬世之功也，然而不能保人心之淪亡。患可有也，人心不可溺也；食可去也，人心不可亡也。然則萬世之功，其歸之孔子乎？孔子刪述六經，以爲萬世道德之宗主，所以救人心之陷溺者在是，所以保人心之淪亡者在是，所以參天地、贊化育而立人極於千萬世者在是。孔子之功，萬世之功也。使世無孔子，則六經不備；六經不備，則道德蔑聞。天下後世之人，將貿貿焉，如聾如瞶，戴天行日，而莫之聞見也。雖安居於水土之上，飽食於稼穡之餘，靈於物而實不異於物矣。如人心何？世道何？有若曰：「自生民以來
translation_en:
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔The writing has an elevated, antique vigor, and the arguments are sound.〕〔This is one of the outstanding pieces in the examination.〕

Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔The author’s language is floating and beyond comparison [?]. This piece elucidates〕〔the supreme authority in the Way and virtue, establishing its substance with compelling clarity. Moreover, the prose flows in a mighty torrent: how could an inferior writer match it?〕

The discourse says: Bringing the waters and land into order so that the people might live securely was an achievement for all ages; yet it could not rescue human hearts from engulfment. Personally undertaking sowing and reaping to feed the people with grain was an achievement for all ages; yet it could not preserve human hearts from ruin. Calamities may occur, but human hearts must not be engulfed; food may be dispensed with, but human hearts must not be lost. Should not the achievement for all ages, then, be attributed to Kongzi? Kongzi edited and transmitted the Six Classics, becoming the supreme authority in the Way and virtue for all ages. Herein lies the means of rescuing human hearts from engulfment; herein lies the means of preserving human hearts from ruin; herein lies the means of forming a triad with Heaven and Earth, assisting their transforming and nurturing work, and establishing the ultimate human standard for countless generations. Kongzi’s achievement is an achievement for all ages. Had there been no Kongzi in the world, the Six Classics would not have been complete; had the Six Classics not been complete, the Way and virtue would scarcely have been heard of. The people of the world in later generations would have remained bewildered, as though deaf and blind, living beneath Heaven and walking in daylight, yet hearing and seeing nothing. Though dwelling securely upon the land amid the waters and eating their fill from abundant harvests, they would, despite possessing greater spiritual intelligence than other creatures, in truth be no different from them. What would become of human hearts? What would become of the moral order of the world? You Ruo said: “Since humankind first came into being …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
來者有盛於孔子也信乎窮天地亘古今一
人而已矣果爾李氏之論如此或者聞而
疑焉曰道德之天古今賢愚所同也行之
而爲道有之而爲德萬古此天地則萬古
此人心萬古此人心則萬古此道德也孔
子何以獨爲萬世之宗主乎意不然允執
厥中堯傳舜也惟精惟一舜授禹也堯舜
禹相傳一道而爲當時道德之宗主世不
能皆堯舜禹也歷四百載而始傳之湯建
中于民則湯所以爲有商一代之宗主也
世不能皆湯也歷六百載而始傳之文武
周公懿恭建極思兼三王則文武周公所
以爲有周一代之宗主也世不能皆文武
周公陵夷而至於春秋之時無傳焉春秋
之時何時也諸侯放恣人欲橫流道德或
幾乎熄矣斯時也誰其宗主乎孔子有德
無位不得宗主乎道德於天下將託之書
而傳也則易更三古混於八索矣詩書煩
punctuated: 來者有盛於孔子也。」信乎！窮天地，亘古今，一人而已矣。果爾，李氏之論如此。或者聞而疑焉，曰：「道德之天，古今賢愚所同也。行之而爲道，有之而爲德。萬古此天地，則萬古此人心；萬古此人心，則萬古此道德也。孔子何以獨爲萬世之宗主乎？」意不然。允執厥中，堯傳舜也；惟精惟一，舜授禹也。堯舜禹相傳一道，而爲當時道德之宗主，世不能皆堯舜禹也。歷四百載而始傳之湯，建中于民，則湯所以爲有商一代之宗主也，世不能皆湯也。歷六百載而始傳之文武周公，懿恭建極，思兼三王，則文武周公所以爲有周一代之宗主也，世不能皆文武周公。陵夷而至於春秋之時，無傳焉。春秋之時，何時也？諸侯放恣，人欲橫流，道德或幾乎熄矣。斯時也，誰其宗主乎？孔子有德無位，不得宗主乎道德於天下。將託之書而傳也，則《易》更三古，混於八索矣；《詩》《書》煩
translation_en:
…those who came surpassed Confucius [?].” How true! Throughout heaven and earth, across antiquity and the present, there has been but this one man. Indeed, such is Master Li’s argument. Someone who heard it raised a doubt, saying: “The Heaven of the Way and virtue [?] is shared by the worthy and the foolish, past and present. Practised, it is the Way; possessed within oneself, it is virtue. Throughout all ages, heaven and earth remain the same, and so does the human heart; throughout all ages, the human heart remains the same, and so do the Way and virtue. Why should Confucius alone be their supreme master for all generations?”

I think otherwise. “Sincerely hold fast to the mean” was what Yao transmitted to Shun; “Be discerning and single-minded” was what Shun imparted to Yu. Yao, Shun, and Yu transmitted one Way to one another and were the supreme masters of the Way and virtue in their own times. Yet not everyone in the world could be a Yao, Shun, or Yu. Only after four hundred years was it transmitted to Tang. His establishment of the mean among the people made Tang the supreme master of the Shang dynasty; yet not everyone could be a Tang. Only after six hundred years was it transmitted to Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou. Through admirable reverence, establishing the highest standard, and aspiring to unite the achievements of the Three Kings, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou became the supreme masters of the Zhou dynasty; yet not everyone could be a Wen, Wu, or Duke of Zhou. Decline continued until the Spring and Autumn period, when the transmission ceased.

What sort of age was the Spring and Autumn period? The feudal lords acted without restraint, human desires ran rampant, and the Way and virtue were nearly extinguished. Who could be their supreme master at such a time? Confucius possessed virtue but held no position, and so could not preside over the Way and virtue throughout the world. He would entrust them to writings for transmission, but the Book of Changes, having passed through the three periods of antiquity, had become mingled with the Eight Cords; the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents were encumbered…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
紀禮樂散亡而皆莫之正矣於是乎有一定
焉乃刪詩書定禮樂贊周易脩春秋堯舜
禹湯文武周公之道既壞而復完既墜而
復續凡天地之所以高厚日月之所以照
臨山川之所以峙流草木之所以蕃育仁
義禮智之所以為性惻隱羞惡辭讓是非
之所以為情父子君臣夫婦兄弟朋友之
所以為倫理物之為物人之為人君子之
所以為君子聖賢之所以為聖賢何莫不
===
備於斯而萬世道德于焉不宗主於堯舜
禹湯文武周公而宗主於六經矣孔子所
以為萬世計者不其至乎自是一變而縱
橫再變而楊墨春秋下而戰國矣縱橫楊
墨能變孔子之六經乎孟子生而闡六經
之道德於子思之門人於是正人心息邪
說距詖行十主乎孔子戰國之人得不陷
於夷狄禽獸者非孔子之功誰之功也坑
焚於秦彼自坑焚耳從生之口拔執得而
punctuated: 紀，禮樂散亡，而皆莫之正矣。於是乎有一定焉，乃刪詩書，定禮樂，贊周易，脩春秋。堯舜禹湯文武周公之道，既壞而復完，既墜而復續。凡天地之所以高厚，日月之所以照臨，山川之所以峙流，草木之所以蕃育，仁義禮智之所以為性，惻隱羞惡辭讓是非之所以為情，父子君臣夫婦兄弟朋友之所以為倫理，物之為物，人之為人，君子之所以為君子，聖賢之所以為聖賢，何莫不備於斯？而萬世道德，于焉不宗主於堯舜禹湯文武周公，而宗主於六經矣。孔子所以為萬世計者，不其至乎？自是一變而縱橫，再變而楊墨，春秋下而戰國矣。縱橫楊墨，能變孔子之六經乎？孟子生而闡六經之道德於子思之門人，於是正人心，息邪說，距詖行，十主乎孔子。戰國之人得不陷於夷狄禽獸者，非孔子之功，誰之功也？坑焚於秦，彼自坑焚耳。從生之口，拔執得而
translation_en:
…in their records; rites and music had become scattered and lost, and no one had put any of these things right. Then a definitive settlement was made: Confucius edited the Odes and Documents, established rites and music, elucidated the Changes of Zhou, and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals. The Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou, once damaged, was made whole again; once fallen into abeyance, it was continued anew. Why Heaven is high and Earth substantial; why the sun and moon shine upon the world; why mountains stand and rivers flow; why plants flourish; why benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom constitute human nature; why compassion, shame and aversion to wrongdoing, deference, and the sense of right and wrong constitute its feelings; why the relationships between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger brother, and friends constitute the ethical order; what makes things things and human beings human; what makes exemplary men exemplary and sages and worthies sagely and worthy—what among these is not fully contained here? Thus, for all subsequent ages, the authoritative source of the Way and virtue became the Six Classics, rather than Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou. Was not Confucius’s provision for all future ages consummate?

Thereafter, one transformation brought the advocates of vertical and horizontal alliances, and another brought the teachings of Yang and Mo; the Spring and Autumn period gave way to the Warring States. Could the advocates of alliances or the teachings of Yang and Mo alter Confucius’s Six Classics? Mengzi arose and elucidated the Way and virtue of the Six Classics among the disciples of Zisi. He thereby rectified people’s hearts, silenced pernicious doctrines, opposed biased conduct, and took Confucius as his master [?]. That the people of the Warring States avoided sinking to the condition of barbarians and beasts—if this was not Confucius’s achievement, whose was it?

As for the burying of scholars and burning of books under the Qin, those responsible merely carried out their own burying and burning. What came from the mouth of Cong Sheng [possibly Fu Sheng; the following wording is garbled]—who could [?] …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
坑焚之黄老於漢彼自黄老耳董子之明
經孰得而黄老之所以爲秦漢道德之宗
主者孔子也不有孔子則伏生董子何所
傳秦漢之人何所聞而宗主之乎下是而
晉宋教斯佛矣晉宋而隋唐佛斯盛矣人
之去夷狄也其幾何哉昌黎韓子聞道德
於孟子之後原道一篇拳拳乎仁義之說
佛骨一表汲汲乎正邪之辯非有得於六
經之道德能如是耶然則以道德宗主乎
===
南北之間而啓唐者孔子也去是而梁唐
壞且亂矣梁唐而漢周壞亂極矣人之去
禽獸也其幾何哉有宋諸子倡道德於千
載之下濂溪周子繼孟子不傳之緒而兩
程得之兩程夫子發前聖未發之藴而朱
子足之非本原於六經之旨遽能如是耶
然則以道德宗主乎千古之時而啓宋者
孔子也宋之有金腥我中原甚矣無足道
也然猶能於我夫子關其起居則孔子之
punctuated: 坑焚之？黄老於漢，彼自黄老耳，董子之明經，孰得而黄老之？所以爲秦漢道德之宗主者，孔子也。不有孔子，則伏生、董子何所傳，秦漢之人何所聞而宗主之乎？下是而晉宋，教斯佛矣；晉宋而隋唐，佛斯盛矣。人之去夷狄也，其幾何哉？昌黎韓子聞道德於孟子之後，《原道》一篇，拳拳乎仁義之說；《佛骨》一表，汲汲乎正邪之辯。非有得於六經之道德，能如是耶？然則以道德宗主乎南北之間而啓唐者，孔子也。去是而梁唐，壞且亂矣；梁唐而漢周，壞亂極矣。人之去禽獸也，其幾何哉？有宋諸子倡道德於千載之下，濂溪周子繼孟子不傳之緒，而兩程得之；兩程夫子發前聖未發之藴，而朱子足之。非本原於六經之旨，遽能如是耶？然則以道德宗主乎千古之時而啓宋者，孔子也。宋之有金，腥我中原甚矣，無足道也。然猶能於我夫子關其起居，則孔子之
translation_en:
…bury and burn it? As for the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi under the Han, those who followed them did so on their own account. Who could turn Master Dong’s elucidation of the Classics into those teachings? It was Confucius who served as the supreme authority for the Way and virtue under the Qin and Han. Without Confucius, what would Fu Sheng and Master Dong have transmitted? What would the people of Qin and Han have heard and taken as their supreme authority?

After this came the Jin and Song, when teaching turned to Buddhism; from the Jin and Song to the Sui and Tang, Buddhism flourished. How little separated people from the barbarians! Master Han of Changli learned of the Way and virtue after Mencius. His essay “An Inquiry into the Way” earnestly expounded benevolence and righteousness; his memorial “On the Buddha’s Bone” urgently distinguished the orthodox from the heterodox. Could he have done so without grasping the Way and virtue of the Six Classics? Thus it was Confucius who, through the Way and virtue, served as the supreme authority amid the Northern and Southern dynasties and prepared the way for the Tang.

After this came the Liang and Tang, with decay and disorder; from the Liang and Tang to the Han and Zhou, decay and disorder reached their height. How little separated people from birds and beasts! The masters of the Song championed the Way and virtue a thousand years later. Master Zhou of Lianxi continued the line of transmission that had lapsed after Mencius, and the two Cheng brothers received it. The two Masters Cheng brought to light profound meanings that earlier sages had not disclosed, and Master Zhu completed their work. Could they have achieved this so readily without grounding themselves in the purport of the Six Classics? Thus it was Confucius who, through the Way and virtue, served as the supreme authority throughout the ages and prepared the way for the Song.

The Jin, which arose during the Song, grievously befouled our Central Plain; they scarcely merit discussion. Yet they could still show concern for our Master’s daily observances [?], so Confucius’s…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
道德行乎夷狄矣元以繼宋污我衣冠甚
矣何足道哉然猶能用許魯齋教其族類
則孔子之道德變乎夷狄矣孔子刪述六
經以爲萬世道德之宗主詎不信哉雖然
孔子不可尚已自其刪述之後言之則發
明道德者孰有過於有宋諸君子而宋之
諸君子孰有備於朱子者哉惜乎宋不幸而
誤以僞學見沮求其能躬行於上推行於
下者不可得也孰若我
===
朝
太祖高皇帝主之於先
列聖相傳繼之於後六經之道行之在上六經
之說明之在下上下一心古今一道孔子
固萬世道德之宗主而我
列聖與
今日
聖天子又孔子道德之宗主也愚何幸親逢其
盛
punctuated: 道德行乎夷狄矣。元以繼宋，污我衣冠甚矣，何足道哉！然猶能用許魯齋教其族類，則孔子之道德變乎夷狄矣。孔子刪述六經，以爲萬世道德之宗主，詎不信哉！雖然，孔子不可尚已。自其刪述之後言之，則發明道德者，孰有過於有宋諸君子？而宋之諸君子，孰有備於朱子者哉！惜乎宋不幸而誤以僞學見沮，求其能躬行於上、推行於下者，不可得也。孰若我朝太祖高皇帝主之於先，列聖相傳繼之於後，六經之道行之在上，六經之說明之在下，上下一心，古今一道！孔子固萬世道德之宗主，而我列聖與今日聖天子，又孔子道德之宗主也。愚何幸親逢其盛！
translation_en:
…the Way and virtue thus prevailed among the barbarians. The Yuan succeeded the Song and gravely defiled our caps and robes—the emblems of our civilization. How could they merit mention? Yet they could still employ Xu Luzhai to teach their own people; thus Confucius’s Way and virtue transformed the barbarians. Confucius edited and transmitted the Six Classics, becoming the authoritative master of the Way and virtue for all ages. Can this truly be doubted?

Even so, Confucius cannot be surpassed. Speaking of the period after his editing and transmission of the classics, who elucidated the Way and virtue more fully than the gentlemen of the Song? And among those gentlemen, who was more comprehensive than Master Zhu? Alas, in the Song their learning was unfortunately and mistakenly obstructed as “spurious learning.” One could find no one able personally to practice it at the highest level and extend its practice to those below.

How could this compare with our dynasty? Emperor Taizu Gao first upheld it, and the succession of sage emperors carried it forward thereafter. The Way of the Six Classics is practiced above, and their teachings are elucidated below. Above and below share one mind; antiquity and the present follow one Way. Confucius is indeed the authoritative master of the Way and virtue for all ages, while our sage emperors and the reigning sage Son of Heaven are themselves the chief upholders of Confucius’s Way and virtue. How fortunate I, humble as I am, am to witness this flourishing age in person!

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
表
擬
賀大有年表　高士達
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔騈儷可觀〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔得體〕
考試官教諭江　批〔表佳〕
伏以
天開景運蓬和氣於兩間
帝握乾符豐綏於九有萬類戴含宏之化羣
===
生圖樂育之仁夷夏騰歡臣民胥慶盖
伏遇
○○○○
一德格天
重華協帝隆儒重道大恢
列聖之良圖敬神恤民允荷
上天之寵命在璣衡以齊七政調玉燭以撫五
辰三白兆今歲之休徵九垓普及時之厚
punctuated:
表

擬賀大有年表。高士達。
同考試官教諭蔡，批〔騈儷可觀〕。
考試官教諭羅，批〔得體〕。
考試官教諭江，批〔表佳〕。

伏以，天開景運，蓬和氣於兩間；帝握乾符，豐綏於九有。萬類戴含宏之化，羣生圖樂育之仁。夷夏騰歡，臣民胥慶。盖伏遇○○○○，一德格天，重華協帝。隆儒重道，大恢列聖之良圖；敬神恤民，允荷上天之寵命。在璣衡以齊七政，調玉燭以撫五辰。三白兆今歲之休徵，九垓普及時之厚
translation_en:
Memorial

Draft Memorial Congratulating the Emperor on a Year of Abundant Harvests, by Gao Shida.
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔The parallel phrasing is worthy of appreciation.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔Appropriate to the genre.〕
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: 〔A fine memorial.〕

We humbly observe: Heaven inaugurates a glorious age, with harmonious qi flourishing [?] between Heaven and Earth; the Emperor holds Heaven’s token of authority, bringing abundance and peace to the nine regions. All beings revere his all-embracing transformation; the multitude look to his benevolence, which delights in nurturing them. The peoples beyond and within the realm rejoice; ministers and commoners alike celebrate.

For we have humbly encountered ○○○○ [four circles in the text]: your single-minded virtue reaches Heaven, and your renewed splendor accords with the Divine Sovereign. You exalt Confucian learning and honor the Way, greatly extending the excellent designs of the sage emperors of your line. You reverence the spirits and care for the people, worthily receiving High Heaven’s gracious mandate. You attend to the celestial instruments to bring the seven celestial governors into harmony, and regulate the precious torch of seasonal concord to bring order to the five celestial bodies. Three falls of snow have foretold this year’s auspicious fortune; throughout the nine reaches spread the timely and bountiful …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
澤五穀熟而人民育八蜡通而海宇寧無
爾界此疆一視盡禾麻菽麥雖際天極地
爭誇多黍稷稻粱瑞麥中生特挺兩岐之
秀嘉禾異產還呈九穗之祥崇墉比櫛之
弗如千倉萬箱之胥積康衢擊壤比屋謳
歌于焉
上供則粢盛之潔足以孝享乎
九廟于焉
國用則儲蓄之隆足以大賚於六師是皆
===
皇上深仁大德之所致以隆我
國家億萬載太平之嘉慶也臣等幸逢
盛世叨列清班考之春秋則特書以見意徵
之雅頌亦迭詠而爲歌況
今日之奇逢尤近古所罕見欲罄形容之妙
慚非博洽之才伏願
以天心而爲心遠紹無窮之大業
以民樂而爲樂丕弘莫大之鴻休地久天長
永
punctuated:
澤。五穀熟而人民育，八蜡通而海宇寧。無爾界此疆，一視盡禾麻菽麥；雖際天極地，爭誇多黍稷稻粱。瑞麥中生，特挺兩岐之秀；嘉禾異產，還呈九穗之祥。崇墉比櫛之弗如，千倉萬箱之胥積。康衢擊壤，比屋謳歌。于焉上供，則粢盛之潔足以孝享乎九廟；于焉國用，則儲蓄之隆足以大賚於六師。是皆皇上深仁大德之所致，以隆我國家億萬載太平之嘉慶也。
臣等幸逢盛世，叨列清班。考之春秋，則特書以見意；徵之雅頌，亦迭詠而爲歌。況今日之奇逢，尤近古所罕見。欲罄形容之妙，慚非博洽之才。伏願以天心而爲心，遠紹無窮之大業；以民樂而爲樂，丕弘莫大之鴻休。地久天長，永
translation_en:
…beneficence. The five grains ripen and the people are nourished; the eight year-end agricultural sacrifices are duly performed, and all within the seas is at peace. With no distinction between your boundary and this frontier, everywhere alike is filled with grain, hemp, beans, and wheat. Even to the ends of heaven and earth, all vie in praising their abundant millets, rice, and fine grain. Auspicious wheat springs up amid the fields, its paired ears standing out in special beauty; wondrous stalks of grain appear, displaying the auspicious sign of nine ears. Even lofty walls arrayed like comb teeth cannot compare with the piled harvest; a thousand granaries and ten thousand carts are filled with it. On the broad thoroughfares people play at striking the earth; household after household sings in praise. From this bounty, offerings are supplied to the throne: pure sacrificial grain suffices for filial offerings in the nine ancestral temples. From it, too, the needs of the state are met: ample reserves suffice for generous rewards to the six armies. All this has been brought about by Your Majesty’s profound benevolence and great virtue, magnifying for our state the blessed joy of peace for countless ages.
We, your servants, are fortunate to encounter this flourishing age and undeservedly occupy the ranks of distinguished officials. Examining the Spring and Autumn Annals, we find that such events were specially recorded to convey their significance; consulting the Major and Minor Odes and the Hymns, we likewise find them repeatedly celebrated in song. How much more does this apply to today’s extraordinary occurrence, seldom witnessed even in recent antiquity! We wish to exhaust the subtleties of description, yet are ashamed that we lack the talent of broad learning. We humbly wish that you take Heaven’s heart as your own heart, carrying forward into the distant future your boundless great undertaking; that you take the people’s joy as your own joy, vastly extending your unsurpassed blessings. As earth endures and heaven lasts, forever…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
皇圖於鞏固日升川至綿
聖壽於無疆臣等下情無任欣躍感戴之至謹
奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
高士達
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔大經事實歷陳無遺〕
考試官教諭羅　批〔敷對詳明可錄〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔能道九倫事實詳悉〕
===
〔深盡人道者也〕
〔敷演閘目者也〕
天生烝民有物有則而大經之理寓於人
天佑下民作之君師而大經之理叙於君
此古昔聖帝明王相繼而出必有經世之
punctuated:
皇圖於鞏固，日升川至，綿聖壽於無疆。臣等下情無任欣躍感戴之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第叁場，策，第一問。
高士達。
同考試官教諭蔡批〔大經事實歷陳無遺〕
考試官教諭羅批〔敷對詳明可錄〕
考試官教諭汪批〔能道九倫事實詳悉〕
〔深盡人道者也〕
〔敷演閘目者也〕

天生烝民，有物有則，而大經之理寓於人；天佑下民，作之君師，而大經之理叙於君。此古昔聖帝明王相繼而出，必有經世之
translation_en:
…the imperial realm in enduring stability; as the sun rises and rivers flow, may Your Majesty’s sacred longevity extend without limit. We, your servants, cannot contain our joy and grateful devotion. We respectfully present this memorial of congratulations for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session: Policy Essay, First Question.
Gao Shida.
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: comment 〔The historical particulars concerning the great norms are set out successively, with nothing omitted.〕
Examiner Luo, Instructor: comment 〔The response is detailed and clear, worthy of selection.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor: comment 〔He can explain the historical particulars of the nine human relationships thoroughly and in detail.〕
〔He probes deeply and fully into the human Way.〕
〔He elaborates the headings [?].〕

Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people; for every thing there is a rule, and the principles of the great norms reside in human beings. Heaven protects the people below and establishes rulers and teachers for them, and the principles of the great norms are set in order by the ruler. This is why, when the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity arose in succession, they invariably had, for ordering the world, …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
三皇以興化當時垂憲萬世使人由之而不
詰經術之而莫測也粤自堯舜帝天下而典
謨垂謨之書以著湯武王天下而訓誥之書以
成洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝創造洪業條成大誥三編
太宗文皇帝繼志述事御製孝順事實爲善陰
隲二書
宣宗章皇帝嗣承大統采輯經傳纂爲五倫一
===
書
天藻睿藻昭回於雲漢之間
宸翰奎章煒煌於宇宙之内皆欲天下後世是
行是訓曉然知大經之所在其以善養人
之心誠可以追堯舜而齊湯武者也猗歟
盛哉然道統相繼歷
列聖如一人制作相同閱百世如一日
誥編所載申明五常之條五教育民之訓
三書所載孝子仁人之事君臣父子之道皆
punctuated:
三皇，以興化當時，垂憲萬世，使人由之而不詰，經術之而莫測也。粤自堯舜帝天下，而典謨垂謨之書以著；湯武王天下，而訓誥之書以成。洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝創造洪業，條成《大誥》三編；太宗文皇帝繼志述事，御製《孝順事實》《爲善陰隲》二書；宣宗章皇帝嗣承大統，采輯經傳，纂爲《五倫》一書。
天藻睿藻昭回於雲漢之間，宸翰奎章煒煌於宇宙之内，皆欲天下後世是行是訓，曉然知大經之所在。其以善養人之心，誠可以追堯舜而齊湯武者也。猗歟，盛哉！然道統相繼，歷列聖如一人；制作相同，閱百世如一日。《誥》編所載，申明五常之條、五教育民之訓；三書所載，孝子仁人之事、君臣父子之道，皆
translation_en:
…the Three Sovereigns [?], to promote moral transformation in their own time and bequeath standards for myriad generations, causing people to follow them without questioning, while their ordering of affairs remained beyond fathoming [?]. From the time when Yao and Shun ruled All under Heaven as emperors, writings of canons and counsels transmitting their plans [?] became manifest; when Tang and Wu ruled All under Heaven as kings, writings of instructions and announcements were completed. We reverently reflect that our dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao established his great undertaking and systematically compiled the three parts of the Great Announcements (Da Gao). Emperor Taizong Wen carried forward his predecessor’s intentions and undertakings, imperially composing two books: Facts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi) and Doing Good and Hidden Virtue (Weishan Yinzhi). Emperor Xuanzong Zhang succeeded to the imperial line, gathered material from the classics and their commentaries, and compiled it into a single book, the Five Relationships (Wulun).
Their heavenly compositions and sagely writings shine amid the Milky Way; their imperial calligraphy and resplendent compositions blaze throughout the universe. All aim to have people throughout All under Heaven and in later generations follow these practices and teachings, clearly understanding where the great constant principles reside. Their desire to nurture people through goodness truly enables them to follow in the footsteps of Yao and Shun and stand equal to Tang and Wu. Ah, how magnificent! The succession in the transmission of the Way passes through the sage emperors as though they were one person; their institutions and compositions accord, remaining the same through a hundred generations as through a single day. What the volumes of the Announcements contain—the provisions elucidating the Five Constant Virtues and the instructions for educating the people through the Five Teachings—and what the three books contain—the deeds of filial sons and benevolent men, and the ways governing ruler and minister, father and son—all…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
一大經之所在未嘗不相符合也其與典
謨所謂親睦九族慎徽五典之詞訓誥所
謂肇脩人紀重民五教之語同一大經之
所在未嘗不相表裏也夫大經莫重於人
倫愚請以克盡五倫者爲執事陳之漢高
祖初入秦也謂父老苦於苛虐而約法三
章文帝始即位也慮鰥寡阽於溝壑而議
寬賑貸以君道揆之可謂仁矣張善相知
效君命不畏世充之攻願喪首而不願叛
===
杲卿恪守忠義不從祿山之叛雖斷舌而
不恤以臣道律之可謂忠矣思驕侈之可
懼集家誡書於屏風者房玄齡也知富貴
之靡常以儉約率其子弟者王旦也此愛
而能勞無愧乎父道焉借其妻貸錢以葬
父者董永也與其婦傭身以養母者姜詩
也此貧而能孝無忝乎子職焉當林夫耕
妻饁雖處田野而相敬如賓山濤始微終
貴雖爵十乘而不娶嬪媵德之盛也可見
punctuated:
一大經之所在，未嘗不相符合也。其與典謨所謂親睦九族、慎徽五典之詞，訓誥所謂肇脩人紀、重民五教之語，同一大經之所在，未嘗不相表裏也。夫大經莫重於人倫，愚請以克盡五倫者爲執事陳之。

漢高祖初入秦也，謂父老苦於苛虐，而約法三章；文帝始即位也，慮鰥寡阽於溝壑，而議寬賑貸。以君道揆之，可謂仁矣。張善相知效君命，不畏世充之攻，願喪首而不願叛；杲卿恪守忠義，不從祿山之叛，雖斷舌而不恤。以臣道律之，可謂忠矣。思驕侈之可懼，集家誡書於屏風者，房玄齡也；知富貴之靡常，以儉約率其子弟者，王旦也。此愛而能勞，無愧乎父道焉。借其妻貸錢以葬父者，董永也；與其婦傭身以養母者，姜詩也。此貧而能孝，無忝乎子職焉。當林夫耕妻饁，雖處田野而相敬如賓；山濤始微終貴，雖爵十乘而不娶嬪媵。德之盛也，可見。
translation_en:
…lie in the same great constant, and have never failed to accord with one another. They likewise embody the same great constant as the phrases in the Canons and Counsels about bringing the nine degrees of kinship into affectionate harmony and carefully promoting the five cardinal duties, and the words in the Instructions and Announcements about first setting human relationships in order and giving weight to the five teachings for the people. They have never failed to complement one another. Within this great constant, nothing is more important than human relationships. I humbly ask leave to set before you examples of those who fully discharged the duties of the five relationships.

When Gaozu of Han first entered Qin, he declared that its elders had suffered under harsh and oppressive rule, and reduced the laws to three articles. When Emperor Wen first ascended the throne, he feared that widowers and widows were on the brink of perishing in the ditches, and considered measures of leniency, relief, and loans. Judged by the way of the ruler, these deeds may be called benevolent. Zhang Shanxiang understood his duty to carry out his sovereign’s commands: he did not fear Shichong’s attack and preferred to lose his head rather than rebel. Gaoqing steadfastly upheld loyalty and righteousness and refused to join Lushan’s rebellion; even having his tongue cut out did not deter him. Judged by the way of the minister, these deeds may be called loyal.

It was Fang Xuanling who, reflecting on the dangers of arrogance and extravagance, compiled family admonitions and inscribed them on a screen. It was Wang Dan who, knowing that wealth and rank were impermanent, led his sons and younger kinsmen by an example of frugality. Loving them while also making them exert themselves, these men were worthy of the way of the father. It was Dong Yong who borrowed money through his wife [?] to bury his father. It was Jiang Shi who, together with his wife, hired himself out to support his mother. Remaining filial despite poverty, these men did no dishonor to the duties of a son.

In the case of Dang Lin [?], the husband plowed and the wife brought food to the fields; although they lived in the countryside, they treated each other with the respect accorded to guests. Shan Tao began in humble circumstances and eventually attained high rank; although his rank entitled him to ten carriages, he took no secondary wives or concubines. The fullness of their virtue can be seen in this.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
盧氏泣玄齡之誘言入帷剔目以明無貳
李氏歸王凝之遺骨引斧斷臂以示不辱
節之壯也可知他若處兄弟不惑毋意而
友愛甚篤王覽之與兄王祥也相對終日
而並敦義讓者非楊播之與弟椿津乎待
朋友念其故舊而同席以食樓護之於呂
公也憫其遺孤而分屋以居者非張裔之
於楊恭乎此皆能篤乎人倫之常大經也
道者也然五倫之道無在而不具故其人
===
之行無往而不合漢高帝爲民而約法三
章即
誥編與民同樂之條也顏杲卿爲君而恪守
忠義即
誥編竭忠成全之旨也董永之貸錢葬父盧
氏之剔目示夫恭之
事實所載原平傭作聞氏養姑者何異哉山
濤之不娶嬪媵樓護之不忘故舊比之
陰騭所紀叔道娶啞道琮葬友者何殊與
punctuated: 盧氏泣玄齡之誘言，入帷剔目以明無貳；李氏歸王凝之遺骨，引斧斷臂以示不辱。節之壯也可知。他若處兄弟，不惑毋意而友愛甚篤，王覽之與兄王祥也；相對終日而並敦義讓者，非楊播之與弟椿、津乎？待朋友，念其故舊而同席以食，樓護之於呂公也；憫其遺孤而分屋以居者，非張裔之於楊恭乎？此皆能篤乎人倫之常，大經也，道者也。然五倫之道，無在而不具，故其人之行，無往而不合。漢高帝爲民而約法三章，即《誥編》與民同樂之條也；顏杲卿爲君而恪守忠義，即《誥編》竭忠成全之旨也。董永之貸錢葬父，盧氏之剔目示夫，恭之《事實》所載原平傭作、聞氏養姑者，何異哉？山濤之不娶嬪媵，樓護之不忘故舊，比之《陰騭》所紀叔道娶啞、道琮葬友者，何殊與？
translation_en:
Lady Lu wept at Xuanling’s words intended to test her, went behind the curtains, and gouged out an eye to demonstrate her unwavering fidelity. Lady Li brought home Wang Ning’s remains and, taking up an axe, cut off her arm to show that she would not suffer dishonor. The strength of their chastity can thus be understood. As for relations between brothers: Wang Lan maintained the deepest fraternal affection for his elder brother Wang Xiang, undeterred by his mother’s intentions [?]. And were those who spent entire days together, both cultivating righteousness and deference, not Yang Bo and his younger brothers Chun and Jin? As for the treatment of friends: Lou Hu remembered his old friendship with Lü Gong and shared his mat with him at meals. And was it not Zhang Yi who, pitying the orphan left by Yang Gong, set aside part of his house for the child to live in? All these people devoted themselves to the enduring norms of human relationships—the great guiding principles, the Way itself. Yet the Way of the five relationships is fully present everywhere; thus, wherever these people acted, their conduct accorded with it.

Emperor Gao of Han reduced the laws to three articles for the people: this corresponds to the provision on sharing enjoyment with the people in the Collected Admonitions (Gaobian). Yan Gaoqing steadfastly upheld loyalty and righteousness for his ruler: this corresponds to the import of exhausting one’s loyalty and bringing matters to completion in the Collected Admonitions. Dong Yong borrowed money to bury his father, and Lady Lu gouged out an eye as a demonstration to her husband. How do these differ from [?] Yuan Ping’s working for hire and Lady Wen’s supporting her mother-in-law, as recorded in Accounts of Actual Deeds (Shishi)? Shan Tao took no concubines, and Lou Hu did not forget his old friends. Compared with Shudao’s marrying a mute woman and Daocong’s burying a friend, as recorded in Hidden Recompense (Yinzhi), how are these different?

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
其大槩之同則其餘可類推矣愚也並誦
聖製雖已有年而愽通之學全未有得惟執事
進而敎之
第二問　　　　　　　　　　胡璉
同考試官訓導張　批　是策隨問隨荅考
〔據詳而事實燦然見留心乎載籍他日致用肯不晤古人之〕
同考試官敎諭袁　批　荅歷代名宦人物策
〔最爲詳悉且華力光健文采煒然其尚友千古景仰前〕
〔芳歟〕
===
考試官敎諭羅　批　古人事實條對無遺覽
〔修文矣眞之優選爲異論攸歸〕
〔高山仰止之意〕
考試官敎諭汪　批　荅者掛一漏十求其悉對
〔無遺者惟此非愽洽之士能乎〕
賢才有關於世道大矣萃此邦而爲名宦
也建功業於當時産此邦而爲人物也垂
休光於後世故慕其名不可以不知其人
punctuated:
其大槩之同，則其餘可類推矣。愚也並誦聖製，雖已有年，而愽通之學全未有得，惟執事進而敎之。
第二問，胡璉。
同考試官訓導張批：是策隨問隨荅，考〔據詳而事實燦然，見留心乎載籍，他日致用，肯不晤古人之〕
同考試官敎諭袁批：荅歷代名宦人物策，〔最爲詳悉，且華力光健，文采煒然，其尚友千古，景仰前〕〔芳歟！〕
考試官敎諭羅批：古人事實，條對無遺，覽〔修文矣，眞之優選，爲異論攸歸〕〔高山仰止之意。〕
考試官敎諭汪批：荅者掛一漏十，求其悉對〔無遺者，惟此。非愽洽之士，能乎？〕
賢才有關於世道大矣！萃此邦而爲名宦也，建功業於當時；産此邦而爲人物也，垂休光於後世。故慕其名，不可以不知其人，
translation_en:
…Since their general purport is the same, the remaining instances may be inferred by analogy. Though I, in my ignorance, have recited both imperial compositions for years, I have attained nothing at all in comprehensive learning. I ask only that you guide me forward and instruct me.
Second policy question. Hu Lian 胡璉.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: This policy essay answers each question in turn. 〔Its supporting evidence is detailed, and the historical facts stand out clearly, showing attentive study of the written records. When putting this learning into practice in the future, would he fail to comprehend the ancients’ …〕[?]
Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: This policy essay on celebrated officials and notable figures of successive dynasties 〔is exceptionally detailed and thorough. Its brilliance and vigor are radiant and robust [?], and its literary accomplishment shines forth. Surely he takes the worthies of all ages as his friends and reveres the exemplary〕〔virtue of his predecessors!〕
Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: The deeds of the ancients are answered point by point, with nothing omitted. On reading it, 〔the writing is cultivated indeed; truly an outstanding selection, a convergence of exceptional judgments [?]〕〔—the sentiment of looking up to a lofty mountain.〕[?]
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Respondents mention one thing and omit ten. If one seeks an answer that covers everything 〔without omission, this alone qualifies. Could anyone but a man of wide and thorough learning accomplish this?〕
The bearing of worthy and talented men upon the moral condition of the age is great indeed! Those who gather in this province and become celebrated officials establish achievements in their own time; those born in this province who become notable figures transmit their glorious renown to later generations. Thus, in admiring their reputations, one must know the men themselves …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
求其人焉可以不論其世歟噫尚友千古
景行先哲學者事也執事以山東之名宦
人物詢承學蓋欲啓後生小子尚友之心
大哉問也敢不悉心以對乎且以名宦言
有仁惠及民而老幼留於既去之日者劉
寵也以恩信綏盜而政績稱為天下之首
者李固也水患民憂分導水勢而民賴以
安非吕夷簡而何歲饑民盜請弛鹽禁而
歲豐乃復非王博文而何曾肇秩滿代去
===
民猶未忍而絕橋以留髙源去官十年民
終不忘而立碑以頌德之深也可知矣祖
進入有爭訟輙閉閤自責吏以是不忍於
欺榮禹錫當兵起契冊即內嚴備禦寇由
是尋自引去政之善也可見李師中不貴
刑罰而范仲淹因薦其有王佐之才李載
惟尚寬厚而吕夷簡獨賢其有不苛之政
嘗斷寃獄情無遁矣此趙孟頫之神明所
以稱於郡中焉事至即決才莫及矣此李
punctuated: 求其人，焉可以不論其世歟？噫！尚友千古，景行先哲，學者事也。執事以山東之名宦人物詢承學，蓋欲啓後生小子尚友之心。大哉問也！敢不悉心以對乎？且以名宦言，有仁惠及民而老幼留於既去之日者，劉寵也；以恩信綏盜而政績稱為天下之首者，李固也。水患民憂，分導水勢而民賴以安，非吕夷簡而何？歲饑民盜，請弛鹽禁而歲豐乃復，非王博文而何？曾肇秩滿代去，民猶未忍而絕橋以留；髙源去官十年，民終不忘而立碑以頌，德之深也可知矣。祖進入有爭訟輙閉閤自責，吏以是不忍於欺；榮禹錫當兵起契冊，即內嚴備禦，寇由是尋自引去，政之善也可見。李師中不貴刑罰，而范仲淹因薦其有王佐之才；李載惟尚寬厚，而吕夷簡獨賢其有不苛之政。嘗斷寃獄，情無遁矣，此趙孟頫之神明所以稱於郡中焉；事至即決，才莫及矣，此李
translation_en:
…Seeking to know these men, how could one fail to consider the age in which they lived? Ah! To befriend the worthy across the ages and emulate the eminent philosophers of the past is the scholar’s undertaking. You, sir, have questioned us students about Shandong’s distinguished officials and notable figures, surely wishing to awaken in us younger students the desire for such fellowship with the worthy. Great indeed is your question! Dare I answer without giving it my fullest attention?

To speak first of distinguished officials: it was Liu Chong whose benevolence benefited the people, so that old and young sought to detain him on the day of his departure. It was Li Gu who pacified bandits through kindness and trustworthiness, and whose achievements in government were acclaimed as foremost in the realm. When floods distressed the people, who but Lü Yijian diverted the waters into separate channels, securing the people’s safety? When famine drove the people to banditry, who but Wang Bowen requested relaxation of the salt prohibitions, restoring them only when harvests were plentiful? When Zeng Zhao completed his term and was replaced, the people still could not bear his departure and broke the bridge to keep him there. Ten years after Gao Yuan left office, the people had never forgotten him and erected a stele in his praise. From this we can appreciate the depth of their virtue.

Whenever disputes arose, Zu Jinru [?] would shut his chamber doors and reproach himself; his clerks therefore could not bring themselves to deceive him. When fighting arose at Qice [?], Rong Yuxi immediately made rigorous defensive preparations within, and the marauders soon withdrew of their own accord. The excellence of their administration is evident. Li Shizhong placed little value on punishments, and Fan Zhongyan accordingly recommended him as possessing the talent to assist a king. Li Zai esteemed only leniency and generosity, and Lü Yijian singled him out for praise because his administration was free of harshness. In adjudicating cases of wrongful imprisonment, he allowed no facts to escape detection: this was why Zhao Mengfu’s extraordinary discernment was praised throughout the prefecture. Matters were decided as soon as they came before him, and none could equal his ability: this was why Li…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
爲之姓名所以書於殿柱焉以人物言買
嵩讀誦而儒行見稱於當時者劉智也躬
耕徂徠以易經教授乎後學者石介也李
陳之解組謝事與子基同時故時有二疏
之比崔仲文以才拜官與兄俊同日故世
有兩鳳之稱九歲能文文章獨步于當時
王禹偁之才何高耶八十二登第姓名獨
冠于天下梁顥之志何堅耶王志愷以剛
鷙爲治故人以皂鵰而見呼張詠以剛方
===
爲任故自以乖崖而爲號稱曰謝顏子者
以顏延之文章冠絕與謝靈運齊名也號
曰韓夫子者以韓熙載才氣俊逸與韓昌
黎媲美也羊祜政多遺愛人望碑墮淚因
以墮淚名賈敦頤與弟敦實刺洛人立碑並頌
因以棠棣號圖梁丘賀之形於麒麟閣非
以其小心周密乎繪秦瓊之像於凌煙閣
非以其戰伐有功乎此皆齊魯之名宦人
物功業休光著於當時而垂於後世者也
punctuated: 爲之姓名所以書於殿柱焉。以人物言，買嵩讀誦而儒行見稱於當時者，劉智也；躬耕徂徠，以易經教授乎後學者，石介也。李陳之解組謝事，與子基同時，故時有二疏之比；崔仲文以才拜官，與兄俊同日，故世有兩鳳之稱。九歲能文，文章獨步于當時，王禹偁之才何高耶！八十二登第，姓名獨冠于天下，梁顥之志何堅耶！王志愷以剛鷙爲治，故人以皂鵰而見呼；張詠以剛方爲任，故自以乖崖而爲號。稱曰謝顏子者，以顏延之文章冠絕，與謝靈運齊名也；號曰韓夫子者，以韓熙載才氣俊逸，與韓昌黎媲美也。羊祜政多遺愛，人望碑墮淚，因以墮淚名；賈敦頤與弟敦實刺洛，人立碑並頌，因以棠棣號。圖梁丘賀之形於麒麟閣，非以其小心周密乎？繪秦瓊之像於凌煙閣，非以其戰伐有功乎？此皆齊魯之名宦人物，功業休光著於當時而垂於後世者也。
translation_en:
…was why Wei's [?] name was inscribed on a palace pillar. As for notable figures: it was Liu Zhi who read and recited texts—the phrase 買嵩 is unclear [?]—and whose Confucian conduct won praise in his day; it was Shi Jie who farmed at Culai and taught the Classic of Changes to younger students. Li Chen [?] laid aside his seal cord and retired from office at the same time as his son Ji, so contemporaries compared them to the Two Shus. Cui Zhongwen received office for his talent on the same day as his elder brother Jun, so people called them the Two Phoenixes. Able to compose prose at nine, and unrivaled in literary composition in his day—how lofty was Wang Yucheng's talent! Passing the examination at eighty-two, and achieving a name unequaled throughout the realm—how steadfast was Liang Hao's resolve! Wang Zhikai [?] governed with fierce severity, so people called him the Black Eagle. Zhang Yong made firmness and integrity his charge, and therefore styled himself Guaiya, “Contrary Cliff.” The designation “Masters Xie and Yan” [?] arose because Yan Yanzhi's literary compositions were outstanding and his fame equaled that of Xie Lingyun. The title “Master Han” arose because Han Xizai's talent and spirit were exceptional and untrammeled, rivaling Han Changli.

Yang Hu's administration left many affectionate memories; people shed tears on seeing his commemorative stele, which consequently became known as the Stele of Falling Tears. Jia Dunyi and his younger brother Dunshi served as prefects at Luo; people erected a stele praising them together, and accordingly called it the Tangdi, “Cherry Tree,” Stele. Was Liangqiu He's portrait displayed in the Qilin Pavilion not because he was cautious and meticulous? Was Qin Qiong's likeness painted in the Lingyan Pavilion not because he had won merit in warfare? These were all renowned officials and notable figures of Qi and Lu, whose achievements and glorious distinction shone in their own time and were handed down to later generations.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
愚也酌幽香而起敬想遺跡而興嗟固未
嘗不以諸名宦人物自期待矣嗚呼抑孰
知有大於此者乎若吾夫子之生為天地
立心為生民立命為往聖繼絕學為萬世
開太平功業與天地而同久休光與日月
而並明萬世之下孰不欲景仰而師法哉
孟子曰乃所願則學孔子愚亦曰乃所願
則學孔子
第三問
李簡
===
同考試官訓導徐　批〔考覈詳而不泛折衷當而不差歸之以宗行禮者〕
識上也
考試官教諭羅　批〔答禮論最為詳備〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔此卷無遺故錄之〕
禮本於古而後世之制終有愧於古禮備
於
今而萬世之制皆莫盛於
punctuated:
愚也酌幽香而起敬，想遺跡而興嗟，固未嘗不以諸名宦人物自期待矣。嗚呼！抑孰知有大於此者乎？若吾夫子之生，為天地立心，為生民立命，為往聖繼絕學，為萬世開太平，功業與天地而同久，休光與日月而並明，萬世之下，孰不欲景仰而師法哉？孟子曰：「乃所願，則學孔子。」愚亦曰：「乃所願，則學孔子。」

第三問
李簡

同考試官訓導徐　批〔考覈詳而不泛，折衷當而不差，歸之以宗行禮者〕識上也。
考試官教諭羅　批〔答禮論最為詳備。〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔此卷無遺，故錄之。〕

禮本於古，而後世之制終有愧於古；禮備於今，而萬世之制皆莫盛於
translation_en:
…As I, your unworthy servant, imbibe their subtle fragrance, reverence arises; as I contemplate the traces they left, I sigh in admiration. Indeed, I have always aspired to measure myself against these renowned officials and figures. Alas! Yet who realizes that there is something greater than this? Our Master, in his lifetime, established a heart for Heaven and Earth, established a destiny for the people, carried on the interrupted learning of the former sages, and opened an age of peace for all generations. His achievements endure as long as Heaven and Earth; his splendid radiance shines alongside the sun and moon. Through ten thousand generations, who would not wish to look up to him and take him as a model? Mengzi said, “As for what I wish, it is to emulate Kongzi.” I too say, “As for what I wish, it is to emulate Kongzi.”

Third Question
Li Jian

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: 〔The investigation is detailed without being diffuse; the judgments are balanced and appropriate, without error. It concludes by honoring those who put ritual into practice [?].〕 His discernment is of the highest order.
Comment by Examiner Luo, Instructor: 〔The discussion of ritual in this answer is exceptionally detailed and comprehensive.〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔This paper leaves nothing out; hence it has been selected for inclusion.〕

Ritual has its roots in antiquity, yet the institutions of later ages ultimately fall short of those of antiquity. Ritual is fully realized in the present, and the institutions of all ages have never been more splendid than those of…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
今甚矣禮之難制也非德則無所本無本則
禮不行非位則無所徵無徵則民弗從德
位兼隆禮制明備此有虞三代之君與我
國朝之
列聖所以皆非漢唐宋之所能及也歟盖嘗聞
之天高地下萬物散殊而禮制行矣斯禮
也聖人作之明其度數辨其儀文以之而
正朝廷井井乎其不可紊以之而定民心
秩秩乎其不可亂所謂安上治民莫善於
===
禮而君子之所當講也稽之於古有虞命
伯夷以典三禮所謂三禮者祀天神祭地
祇享人鬼是也周官大宗伯以五禮經邦
國所謂五禮者吉凶軍賓嘉是也王制司
徒脩六禮以節民性所謂六禮者冠婚喪
祭鄉相見是也三禮五禮六禮目雖不同
也然無非一德之是將若夫禮器所載經
禮者經常之禮也如朝覲會同冠婚喪祭
其類有三百之多焉曲禮者委曲之禮也
punctuated:
今。甚矣，禮之難制也！非德則無所本，無本則禮不行；非位則無所徵，無徵則民弗從。德位兼隆，禮制明備，此有虞三代之君與我國朝之列聖所以皆非漢唐宋之所能及也歟！盖嘗聞之：天高地下，萬物散殊，而禮制行矣。斯禮也，聖人作之，明其度數，辨其儀文，以之而正朝廷，井井乎其不可紊；以之而定民心，秩秩乎其不可亂。所謂安上治民，莫善於禮，而君子之所當講也。

稽之於古，有虞命伯夷以典三禮，所謂三禮者，祀天神、祭地祇、享人鬼是也。《周官》大宗伯以五禮經邦國，所謂五禮者，吉、凶、軍、賓、嘉是也。《王制》司徒脩六禮以節民性，所謂六禮者，冠、婚、喪、祭、鄉、相見是也。三禮、五禮、六禮，目雖不同也，然無非一德之是將。若夫《禮器》所載，經禮者，經常之禮也，如朝覲、會同、冠、婚、喪、祭，其類有三百之多焉。曲禮者，委曲之禮也。
translation_en:
…the present. How very difficult it is to establish rites! Without virtue, they have no foundation; without a foundation, rites cannot be put into practice. Without rank, they have no authoritative attestation; without such attestation, the people will not follow them. When virtue and rank are both exalted, the institutions of ritual are clear and complete. Is this not why the rulers of Youyu and the Three Dynasties, together with the successive sage emperors of our dynasty, are all beyond anything the Han, Tang, and Song could attain? I have heard it said: Heaven is high and earth is low; the myriad things are dispersed and differentiated, and the institutions of ritual operate among them. These rites were created by the sages, who clarified their measures and prescriptions and distinguished their ceremonial forms. Through them they set the court in proper order, so methodically that it could not fall into confusion; through them they settled the people's hearts, so systematically that they could not fall into disorder. This is what is meant by saying that nothing surpasses ritual in securing those above and governing the people. It is therefore something the gentleman ought to study.

Examining antiquity, we find that the ruler of Youyu commanded Bo Yi to oversee the three rites. These were the offerings to celestial spirits, the sacrifices to terrestrial spirits, and the offerings to human spirits. In the Offices of Zhou, the Minister of Rites orders the states through the five rites: auspicious rites, mourning rites, military rites, rites for guests, and celebratory rites. In “Royal Regulations,” the Minister of Education cultivates the six rites to regulate the people's dispositions: capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, village ceremonies, and formal meetings. Although the categories of the three, five, and six rites differ, all alike serve to advance a single virtue. As for what is recorded in “Ritual Vessels,” the fundamental rites are the regular and enduring rites, such as court audiences, assemblies and meetings, capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice. Their categories number as many as three hundred. The detailed rites are rites governing particulars…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
如升降進退俯仰揖遜其類有三千之盛
焉經禮三百曲禮三千條目雖多也然無
非一敬之是敷非若後世之禮徒事乎繁
文末節而已是故炎漢之初叔孫通制綿
蕝之禮而其效僅至於羣臣震恐無敢諠
譁者蓋當爭雄角力之餘一旦見大禮制
之行遽有以銷其暴戾之心收其怠慢之
容故遂至於震懼而不敢肆耳漢高以爲
上得天下不事詩書非必世能仁之主也
===
比肩而生所以不至而其禮豈能有合於
古歟唐有開元顯慶二禮宋有開寶及政
和五禮觀其所制雖曰愈於綿蕝而亦未
見其合於古者豈非其德終有歉於古也
聖人而其禮自不能備自不可行也歟古
之禮信善矣然而有不能行於後世者非
古之禮不可行而行之非其人耳晦庵朱
子之論禮制必以古禮爲據而裁之豈無
見乎哉
punctuated: 如升降進退、俯仰揖遜，其類有三千之盛焉。經禮三百，曲禮三千，條目雖多也，然無非一敬之是敷，非若後世之禮徒事乎繁文末節而已。是故炎漢之初，叔孫通制綿蕝之禮，而其效僅至於羣臣震恐，無敢諠譁者。蓋當爭雄角力之餘，一旦見大禮制之行，遽有以銷其暴戾之心，收其怠慢之容，故遂至於震懼而不敢肆耳。漢高以爲上得天下，不事詩書，非必世能仁之主也。比肩而生，所以不至，而其禮豈能有合於古歟？唐有開元、顯慶二禮，宋有開寶及政和五禮，觀其所制，雖曰愈於綿蕝，而亦未見其合於古者，豈非其德終有歉於古也聖人，而其禮自不能備、自不可行也歟？古之禮信善矣，然而有不能行於後世者，非古之禮不可行，而行之非其人耳。晦庵朱子之論禮制，必以古禮爲據而裁之，豈無見乎哉！
translation_en:
…such as ascending and descending, advancing and withdrawing, bowing and straightening, saluting with clasped hands and yielding precedence: these comprise fully three thousand forms. There are three hundred fundamental rites and three thousand detailed observances. Although their provisions are numerous, all serve to express a single reverence. They are unlike the rites of later ages, which concern themselves merely with elaborate formalities and petty details.

Thus, at the beginning of the Han dynasty, Shusun Tong devised ceremonies rehearsed with ropes and bundles of grass as markers. Yet their effect extended only to making the assembled ministers tremble with fear, so that none dared make a commotion. For, after their struggles for supremacy and contests of strength, they suddenly witnessed the performance of grand ceremonial institutions. These immediately subdued their violent dispositions and restrained their negligent bearing, so that they became fearful and dared not behave without restraint. Gaozu of Han believed that he had won the empire as ruler [?] and did not concern himself with the Odes and the Documents. He was not a sovereign capable of bringing about benevolent government within a generation. “Born shoulder to shoulder, and therefore did not attain it” [?]: how could his rites have accorded with antiquity?

The Tang had the two ritual codes of the Kaiyuan and Xianqing eras, and the Song had those of the Kaibao era and the Five Rites of the Zhenghe Era. Examining what they established, one may say that these surpassed the ceremonies marked out with ropes and grass bundles, yet one still finds no agreement with antiquity. Was this not because their virtue ultimately fell short of that of the sages of antiquity [?], so that their rites could neither be complete nor be put into practice?

The rites of antiquity were indeed excellent. Where they could not be carried out in later ages, this was not because ancient rites were impracticable, but because those carrying them out were not the right people. When Master Zhu, known as Hui’an, discussed ritual institutions, he invariably took ancient rites as his basis and adapted them accordingly. Surely he had insight in doing so!

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
皇明以禮治天下有
令有
制有職掌孝慈諸書凡君臣父子之大倫朝
覲會同之盛禮冠婚喪祭之大端與凡事
物文爲之懿無一不備與有虞三代之諸
禮皆相符合誠萬世不刊之典也而又
勑天下臣民得恭用朱子家禮禮制之備
莫備於斯矣天下守之如一國而國不異
政國守之如一家而家不殊俗家守之如
一人而人不異行囿斯民於天序天秩之
中納斯民於五禮五典之内比屋可封人
人君子漢唐以下豈足以彷彿萬一而愚
生又惡敢舉一二以見其盛哉
===
第四問
王景運
考試官教諭羅　批〔能不泥先儒評史當論可取〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔論作史之法有源委有斷制〕
蓋嘗究心於史學者也
punctuated:
皇明以禮治天下，有《令》，有《制》，有《職掌》《孝慈》諸書。凡君臣父子之大倫，朝覲會同之盛禮，冠婚喪祭之大端，與凡事物文爲之懿，無一不備，與有虞三代之諸禮皆相符合，誠萬世不刊之典也。而又勑天下臣民得恭用朱子《家禮》，禮制之備，莫備於斯矣。天下守之如一國，而國不異政；國守之如一家，而家不殊俗；家守之如一人，而人不異行。囿斯民於天序天秩之中，納斯民於五禮五典之内，比屋可封，人人君子。漢唐以下，豈足以彷彿萬一？而愚生又惡敢舉一二以見其盛哉？

第四問
王景運
考試官教諭羅　批〔能不泥先儒，評史當，論可取。〕
考試官教諭汪　批〔論作史之法，有源委，有斷制。〕

蓋嘗究心於史學者也。
translation_en:
Our august Ming dynasty governs all under Heaven through ritual. It has its Ordinances, its Regulations, and such books as Official Responsibilities and Filial Piety and Compassion. Nothing is lacking: the cardinal relationships between ruler and minister and between father and son; the grand ceremonies of court audiences and assemblies; the principal rites of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice; and all the refinements of ceremonial forms and conduct. These accord with the rites of Shun and the Three Dynasties and are truly immutable standards for all ages. Moreover, an imperial command permits subjects throughout the realm respectfully to follow Master Zhu’s Family Rituals. No system of ritual could be more complete.

All under Heaven observe these rites as though they were a single state, with no differences in government among states; each state observes them as though it were a single family, with no differences in custom among families; each family observes them as though it were a single person, with no differences in conduct among individuals. Thus the people are encompassed within Heaven’s ordering of relationships and ranks and brought within the five rites and five constant duties. Every household has people worthy of enfeoffment, and everyone is a gentleman. How could the Han, Tang, or subsequent dynasties bear even the faintest resemblance to this? And how could I, a humble student, presume to convey its magnificence by citing merely one or two examples?

Fourth Question
Wang Jingyun
Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔He avoids being bound by earlier Confucian scholars. His assessments of histories are sound, and his argument is worthy of acceptance.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔His discussion of the methods of writing history traces their origins and development and offers decisive judgments.〕

I have indeed devoted thought to the study of history.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
作史者本於春秋則是非有定見而予奪
皆合乎天下之公作史者本於聖人之言大哉
非有定論而折衷不謬於聖人之言大哉
春秋之義乎其聖人經世之要乎王者本
之以脩政立事則一代之王法在是也況
作史乎本之以垂訓立教則一代之典章
在是也況作史乎春秋之義其大如此何
以言之聖人之經載乎道聖人之道本諸
心心明則道明道明則凡所以為經者皆
===
欲以明道也春秋列國中之一史爾孔子
假而脩之以寓一王之法實史外傳心之
要典也苟無聖人之心胷而欲讀其書通
其義難矣況欲擬之以立言乎先儒病學
者不先治經而治史以為倒學卒無得於
是非予奪之公有以也司馬遷非聖人之
徒也史記一書其能有合於春秋之旨乎
觀其著十二本紀十表八書三十世家七
十列傳凡百三十篇馳騁數千載間勤亦
punctuated: 作史者本於《春秋》，則是非有定見，而予奪皆合乎天下之公。作史者本於聖人之言，大哉！非有定論，而折衷不謬於聖人之言。大哉，《春秋》之義乎！其聖人經世之要乎！王者本之以脩政立事，則一代之王法在是也，況作史乎？本之以垂訓立教，則一代之典章在是也，況作史乎？《春秋》之義，其大如此，何以言之？聖人之經載乎道，聖人之道本諸心。心明則道明，道明則凡所以為經者，皆欲以明道也。《春秋》，列國中之一史爾。孔子假而脩之，以寓一王之法，實史外傳心之要典也。苟無聖人之心胷，而欲讀其書、通其義，難矣，況欲擬之以立言乎？先儒病學者不先治經而治史，以為倒學，卒無得於是非予奪之公，有以也。司馬遷非聖人之徒也，《史記》一書，其能有合於《春秋》之旨乎？觀其著十二本紀、十表、八書、三十世家、七十列傳，凡百三十篇，馳騁數千載間，勤亦
translation_en:
When historians take the Spring and Autumn Annals as their foundation, they have settled views of right and wrong, and their praise and blame accord entirely with the impartial judgment of all under Heaven. Historians take the sage’s words as their foundation—how great! Without settled judgments, their adjudications nevertheless do not depart from the sage’s words [?]. How great are the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals! Are they not the essentials by which the sage orders the world? When a king takes them as his foundation for improving government and establishing affairs, the royal laws of an entire age are contained therein. How much more, then, should historians do so? When he takes them as his foundation for bequeathing instruction and establishing moral teaching, the institutions of an entire age are contained therein. How much more, then, should historians do so?

On what grounds can we say that the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals are so great? The sage’s classics convey the Way, and the sage’s Way is rooted in his mind. When the mind is illuminated, the Way is illuminated; when the Way is illuminated, everything through which the classics are constituted serves to illuminate the Way. The Spring and Autumn Annals was merely the history of one among the various states. Confucius took it and revised it to embody the laws of a true king. It is, in fact, an essential canon that goes beyond history to transmit the sage’s mind. Without the sage’s breadth of mind, it is difficult to read his book and comprehend its principles. How much more difficult to emulate it in establishing one’s own teachings!

Earlier Confucian scholars criticized students who studied history before studying the classics, considering this learning in reverse order. Such students ultimately failed to grasp impartiality in judging right and wrong and assigning praise and blame: there was good reason for this criticism. Sima Qian was not a follower of the sage. Could his Records of the Historian accord with the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals? Consider his twelve Basic Annals, ten Tables, eight Treatises, thirty Hereditary Houses, and seventy Biographies: 130 chapters in all, ranging across several thousand years. His diligence, too, …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
至矣劉向揚雄咸稱其有良史才服其善
叙事理辯而不華質而不俚其文直其事
核不虛美不隱惡謂之實錄若有得矣至
其論大道則先黃老而後六經序遊俠則
退處士而進奸雄傳貨殖則崇勢利而羞
貧賤豈能免班固謬於聖人之誚乎所謂
不能合於春秋者此也若夫班固范曄陳
壽之徒相繼而作則又不過依倣遷法而
爲之非遷比也遷且不及況望其過之而
===
有得於春秋之旨哉迨宋歐陽脩作五代
史其立例始寓春秋之意至其爲論每篇
必以嗚呼發之蓋以爲亂世之書而致嘆
也至於叙述則文簡而能暢事增而不贅
觀其篇名曰家人傳則帝王正家之義見
矣曰梁臣傳唐臣傳則忠臣不事二君之
義昭矣曰死節傳死事傳則人臣之伏節
死義者傳矣曰一行傳非以著士之高尚
者乎曰唐六臣傳非以明臣之背附者乎
punctuated:
至矣！劉向、揚雄咸稱其有良史才，服其善叙事理，辯而不華，質而不俚，其文直，其事核，不虛美，不隱惡，謂之實錄，若有得矣。至其論大道，則先黃老而後六經；序遊俠，則退處士而進奸雄；傳貨殖，則崇勢利而羞貧賤。豈能免班固謬於聖人之誚乎？所謂不能合於春秋者，此也。若夫班固、范曄、陳壽之徒，相繼而作，則又不過依倣遷法而爲之，非遷比也。遷且不及，況望其過之而有得於春秋之旨哉？
迨宋歐陽脩作五代史，其立例始寓春秋之意。至其爲論，每篇必以嗚呼發之，蓋以爲亂世之書而致嘆也。至於叙述，則文簡而能暢，事增而不贅。觀其篇名曰家人傳，則帝王正家之義見矣；曰梁臣傳、唐臣傳，則忠臣不事二君之義昭矣；曰死節傳、死事傳，則人臣之伏節死義者傳矣；曰一行傳，非以著士之高尚者乎？曰唐六臣傳，非以明臣之背附者乎？
translation_en:
…was indeed utmost! Liu Xiang and Yang Xiong both praised his talent as a fine historian and admired his skill in narrating events and their underlying principles: eloquent without ornament, plain without vulgarity, direct in his writing and accurate in his facts, neither praising without foundation nor concealing wrongdoing. They called it a true record, and he seems to have attained something of the ideal. Yet when discussing the Great Way, he gives precedence to the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi over the Six Classics; when recounting the deeds of wandering knights, he disparages reclusive scholars and exalts unscrupulous men of power; and when writing the biographies of those who accumulated wealth, he esteems power and profit and treats poverty and low station as shameful. How could he escape Ban Gu’s reproach that he departed from the teachings of the Sage? This is what is meant by his failure to accord with the Spring and Autumn Annals. As for Ban Gu, Fan Ye, Chen Shou, and their like, who wrote in succession, they merely followed Sima Qian’s methods and were no match for him. If they could not even equal Qian, how could one expect them to surpass him and grasp the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals?
Only when Ouyang Xiu of the Song wrote the History of the Five Dynasties did the principles of historical composition begin to embody the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals. In his appraisals, he invariably opens each piece with “Alas!” This is surely because he regarded it as a book about an age of disorder and thus gave voice to lamentation. As for the narrative, its language is concise yet lucid; it includes more events without becoming prolix. Consider its chapter titles: “Biographies of Family Members” reveals the principle that emperors and kings must put their households in order; “Biographies of the Ministers of Liang” and “Biographies of the Ministers of Tang” make plain the principle that a loyal minister does not serve two rulers; “Biographies of Those Who Died for Their Integrity” and “Biographies of Those Who Died in Service” transmit the deeds of ministers who remained steadfast in their integrity and died for righteousness. Is “Biographies of Men Distinguished by a Single Virtue” not intended to make manifest the lofty character of scholars? Is “Biographies of the Six Ministers of Tang” not intended to expose ministers’ abandonment of one allegiance and attachment to another?

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
而雜傳則歷世累朝之臣無操守者也宜
脩之言曰吾用春秋之法師其義不襲其
文論者稱其紀述之功不在遷下非以遷
與脩等也紀例精密非遷所及則稱之本
意也觀者不以文害辭可也其後紫陽朱
夫子出作爲通鑑綱目表歲以首年而因
年以著統大書以提要而分註以備言歲
周於上而天道明矣統正於下而人道定
矣大綱既舉而鑒戒昭矣衆目畢張而幾
===
微著矣至其大義所在則尊正統即春秋
大一統之義也於中宗每歲書帝所在即
春秋書公在乾侯之義也至於隨事褒貶
若黜曹魏以正僞尊昭烈以明統楊雄仕
於漢而曰莽大夫陶潛卒於宋而曰晉徵
士誅奸諛於既死發潛德之幽光詞嚴義
正炳如日星何莫非春秋之義乎噫以諸
子言之遷之博學洽聞固非班輩所能及
而脩之義例精密又非遷所能及矣然而
punctuated: 而雜傳則歷世累朝之臣無操守者也。宜脩之言曰：「吾用春秋之法，師其義，不襲其文。」論者稱其紀述之功不在遷下，非以遷與脩等也；紀例精密，非遷所及，則稱之本意也。觀者不以文害辭可也。其後紫陽朱夫子出，作爲《通鑑綱目》，表歲以首年，而因年以著統；大書以提要，而分註以備言。歲周於上，而天道明矣；統正於下，而人道定矣；大綱既舉，而鑒戒昭矣；衆目畢張，而幾微著矣。至其大義所在，則尊正統，即《春秋》大一統之義也；於中宗每歲書帝所在，即《春秋》書公在乾侯之義也。至於隨事褒貶，若黜曹魏以正僞，尊昭烈以明統，楊雄仕於漢而曰莽大夫，陶潛卒於宋而曰晉徵士，誅奸諛於既死，發潛德之幽光，詞嚴義正，炳如日星，何莫非《春秋》之義乎？噫！以諸子言之，遷之博學洽聞，固非班輩所能及；而脩之義例精密，又非遷所能及矣。然而
translation_en:
…As for the Miscellaneous Biographies, these concern ministers of successive ages and dynasties who lacked moral integrity. Fittingly, Ouyang Xiu said: “I employ the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, taking its principles as my model without imitating its wording.” When critics praise his achievement in historical narration as no less than Sima Qian’s, they do not mean that Qian and Xiu are equal in every respect. Their praise truly means that the precision of his historiographical conventions surpasses what Qian achieved. Readers should not let individual words obscure the meaning of the statement.

Afterward, Master Zhu Xi of Ziyang appeared and composed the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian gangmu). He marked the passage of time by placing the year first, and through the dating made the legitimate succession manifest. He set out the essentials in large characters and supplied the full account in subsidiary annotations. With the years fully set out above, the Way of Heaven became clear; with the legitimate succession correctly established below, the human order became settled. Once the main outline was raised, its lessons and warnings became plain; once all the detailed entries were displayed, subtle incipient developments became apparent.

As for its overarching principles, its honoring of the legitimate succession embodies the Spring and Autumn Annals’ principle of exalting unified rule. Its recording of Emperor Zhongzong’s whereabouts each year embodies the same principle as the Annals’ recording that the duke was at Ganhou. As for assigning praise and blame according to events: it demotes Cao Wei to rectify claims to legitimacy, and honors Emperor Zhaolie to clarify the legitimate succession. Although Yang Xiong served under the Han, it calls him “Grand Master under Wang Mang”; although Tao Qian died under the Song, it calls him “Summoned Scholar of the Jin.” It condemns treacherous flatterers after their deaths and brings the hidden radiance of unrecognized virtue to light. Its language is stern and its judgments just, shining like the sun and stars. Which of these does not embody the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals?

Ah! Among these writers, Qian’s breadth of learning and extensive knowledge were certainly beyond the reach of Ban Gu and his peers; yet the precision of Xiu’s principles and conventions was likewise beyond Qian’s reach. Nevertheless…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
不可以無法而天下之法在得人而爲之
孔子曰文武之政布在方策其人存則其
政舉此之謂也方今
朝廷清明俊乂在官法皆盡善何有於弊也
執事發策顧以救弊之方下詢承學得非
謂諸生皆窮經學古之人致用有日所當
講明者固不可以不豫耶敢請復其萬一
財用重事也周官有司會主理財之職大
學以生財爲絜矩之本財用之重於古也
===
尚矣理之可無法乎今租稅之入猶昔也
非有所盈縮也而國用或有不足者豈生
齒日繁兵甲日盛仰給於
朝廷者衆歟然京師之稱百萬之號自古然
矣孰得而少之哉惟綜理得人如李濬臣
之爲度支張方平之爲三司腹茲有以起
仁儉之實必撿會有以節財用之虛耗則
不必加賦於什一之外而國用常舒無不
足矣賦役重務也漢宣帝有政平訟理之
punctuated:
不可以無法，而天下之法在得人而爲之。孔子曰：「文武之政，布在方策。其人存，則其政舉。」此之謂也。方今朝廷清明，俊乂在官，法皆盡善，何有於弊也？執事發策，顧以救弊之方下詢承學，得非謂諸生皆窮經學古之人，致用有日，所當講明者固不可以不豫耶？敢請復其萬一。
財用，重事也。周官有司會主理財之職，大學以生財爲絜矩之本，財用之重於古也尚矣。理之可無法乎？今租稅之入猶昔也，非有所盈縮也，而國用或有不足者，豈生齒日繁，兵甲日盛，仰給於朝廷者衆歟？然京師之稱百萬之號，自古然矣，孰得而少之哉？惟綜理得人，如李濬臣之爲度支、張方平之爲三司，腹茲有以起仁儉之實，必撿會有以節財用之虛耗，則不必加賦於什一之外，而國用常舒，無不足矣。
賦役，重務也。漢宣帝有政平訟理之
translation_en:
…cannot do without proper methods; yet putting the methods of the realm into practice depends on finding the right people. Confucius said: “The government of Kings Wen and Wu is set forth on wooden tablets and bamboo slips. When the right people are present, their government is carried out.” This is what those words mean. Today the court is enlightened, outstanding men hold office, and all institutions are entirely sound. What abuses could there be? Yet you, gentlemen, have set a policy question and condescended to ask us students about ways to remedy abuses. Might this be because you consider us students people who thoroughly study the classics and learn from antiquity, and who will one day put our learning to use, so that we must prepare in advance by clarifying what we ought to understand? I venture to offer a reply on even a small part of the matter.
Public finance is a weighty concern. The Offices of Zhou provides for a Grand Accountant charged with managing finances, while the Great Learning makes the production of wealth the foundation of the principle of the measuring square. The importance attached to public finance in antiquity thus has a long history. Can it be managed without proper methods? Today tax receipts remain as they were in the past, neither increasing nor decreasing. Yet state funds sometimes prove insufficient. Could this be because the population grows daily, the armed forces expand daily, and many depend upon the court for their support? But the capital has been spoken of as numbering a million since ancient times. Who could reduce that number? What matters is finding the right people to oversee and manage affairs, such as Li Junchen serving as Director of the Bureau of Revenue and Zhang Fangping serving as Commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions. They could thereby bring benevolence and frugality into actual practice [?], and through scrutiny of accounts [?] curb wasteful expenditure. There would then be no need to levy taxes beyond the tithe, and state finances would always be ample, never deficient.
Taxation and labor service are weighty responsibilities. Emperor Xuan of Han had words concerning equitable administration and the proper adjudication of lawsuits …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
唐太宗有爲朕養民之言賦役之□□
民也大矣今貧富之則有等也非有所□
隆也而民或至於逋負者豈軍國有□□
方多故賦斂於百姓者過數然□□之□
力役之用從古然矣孰得而已之□惟守
令得人如朱邑之守桐鄉黃霸之在穎
城驗田賦以定科差而人心悅均賦役有
如衡平而歌謠作則不必變法於九等之
外而民力自舒無逋負矣盜非不治也而
===
尚未能息攘奪之風盜非善之者無□□
之者非法乎道不拾遺自不爲盜也如是
者本之教養卓茂嘗以之矣貴不大遺不
敢盜也如是者得之嚴明虞詡乃所長焉
使教養威嚴兼備不廢則里閈之間安有
桴鼓之警哉荒非不救也而卒不能禦水
旱之災庸非積之者乎預救之者無術乎
義倉之政所以備荒也如是者可以行於
平日文公嘗舉之矣勸借之方所以救荒
punctuated:
唐太宗有爲朕養民之言，賦役之□□民也大矣。今貧富之則有等也，非有所□隆也，而民或至於逋負者，豈軍國有□□方多故，賦斂於百姓者過數？然□□之□，力役之用，從古然矣，孰得而已之□？惟守令得人，如朱邑之守桐鄉、黃霸之在穎城，驗田賦以定科差，而人心悅；均賦役有如衡平，而歌謠作。則不必變法於九等之外，而民力自舒，無逋負矣。
盜非不治也，而尚未能息攘奪之風。盜非善之者無□□之者非法乎？道不拾遺，自不爲盜也，如是者本之教養，卓茂嘗以之矣。貴不大遺，不敢盜也，如是者得之嚴明，虞詡乃所長焉。使教養威嚴兼備不廢，則里閈之間安有桴鼓之警哉？
荒非不救也，而卒不能禦水旱之災，庸非積之者乎，預救之者無術乎？義倉之政，所以備荒也，如是者可以行於平日，文公嘗舉之矣。勸借之方，所以救荒
translation_en:
…Emperor Taizong of the Tang spoke of “nurturing the people on my behalf.” The effect of taxation and labor service upon the people is great [partly illegible]. At present, the standards governing rich and poor have their gradations; there is no [illegible] increase [?]. Yet some people fall into arrears. Is this because military and state affairs face [illegible] troubles, and levies upon the common people exceed the prescribed amounts? Yet [illegible] and the employment of compulsory labor have existed since antiquity. Who could abolish them? Only by securing suitable prefects and magistrates—as when Zhu Yi administered Tongxiang and Huang Ba served in Yingcheng—can assessments of fields and taxes determine the allocation of obligations and win the people’s approval. When taxation and labor service are apportioned as evenly as a balanced scale, songs of praise arise. Then, without changing the established system of nine grades, the people’s resources will naturally be eased, and there will be no arrears.
It is not that banditry goes unpunished, yet the practice of plunder and seizure has still not been checked. Is this not because those who deal with banditry lack [illegible], and those who handle it fail to follow proper methods [?]? When no one picks up property lost on the road, people naturally refrain from theft. Such conduct is rooted in instruction and nurture; Zhuo Mao once employed this approach. “Valuing no great loss” [?]: people dare not steal. Such a result comes from strictness and clarity, in which Yu Xu excelled. If instruction and nurture were maintained together with authority and severity, how could the alarm drums sound in the villages?
It is not that famine goes unrelieved, yet in the end the disasters of flood and drought cannot be warded off. Is this not a matter of those who accumulate reserves [?], or of those responsible for advance relief lacking effective methods? The system of charitable granaries provides against famine. Such a measure can be implemented in ordinary times; Duke Wen once put it into practice. The method of encouraging loans serves to relieve famine…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
也如是者不可廢於臨時范文正蓋嘗用
焉使預儲時措兩盡無遺則道路之間安
有流殍之見哉孟子曰經正則庶民興庶
民興斯無邪慝矣歐陽子曰脩其本以勝
之此古今闢異端之定論也學校者正經
脩本之地也我
朝之作興於斯至矣使奉行於下者皆能以
道為心以身為教如文翁如安定則學校
於是乎興而一邑一郡皆化於正矣鄉邑
===
化之天下同焉異端有不息乎孔子曰吾
觀於鄉而知王道之易易也呂氏曰鄉飲
行而天下之化行矣此古今談鄉飲之大
義也是舉也王者道化之本也我
朝之崇重於斯至矣使奉宣於下者皆能以
德為重以敬為禮如黃霸如劉彝則鄉飲
於是乎嚴而鄉邑之間尊德尚齒矣鄉邑
化之天下同焉澆頑有不革乎吁道非常
資法而立法未嘗遠人也有人則
punctuated: 也。如是者，不可廢於臨時，范文正蓋嘗用焉。使預儲時措，兩盡無遺，則道路之間安有流殍之見哉？孟子曰：「經正則庶民興，庶民興斯無邪慝矣。」歐陽子曰：「脩其本以勝之。」此古今闢異端之定論也。學校者，正經脩本之地也。我朝之作興於斯至矣。使奉行於下者皆能以道為心，以身為教，如文翁，如安定，則學校於是乎興，而一邑一郡皆化於正矣。鄉邑化之，天下同焉，異端有不息乎？孔子曰：「吾觀於鄉，而知王道之易易也。」呂氏曰：「鄉飲行，而天下之化行矣。」此古今談鄉飲之大義也。是舉也，王者道化之本也。我朝之崇重於斯至矣。使奉宣於下者皆能以德為重，以敬為禮，如黃霸，如劉彝，則鄉飲於是乎嚴，而鄉邑之間尊德尚齒矣。鄉邑化之，天下同焉，澆頑有不革乎？吁！道非常資法而立，法未嘗遠人也。有人則
translation_en:
…Such measures must not be neglected when the need arises; Fan Wenzheng indeed once employed them. If advance stockpiling and timely measures were both fully carried out, with nothing omitted, how could refugees and the bodies of the starved be seen along the roads?

Mengzi said: “When the guiding principles are correct, the common people rise to goodness; when the common people rise to goodness, there is no depravity.” Master Ouyang said: “Cultivate the root in order to overcome it.” These are the settled judgments, ancient and modern, on rejecting heterodox teachings. Schools are places for correcting guiding principles and cultivating the root. Our dynasty has done the utmost to promote them. If those charged with carrying this out locally could all take the Way to heart and teach through their own conduct, like Wen Weng and Anding [Hu Yuan], schools would flourish, and every county and prefecture would be transformed toward rectitude. Once villages and towns were transformed, all under Heaven would follow. How could heterodox teachings fail to cease?

Kongzi said: “I observe the village ceremony and thereby understand how very easy the Kingly Way is to practice.” Master Lü said: “When the village drinking ceremony is practiced, moral transformation proceeds throughout all under Heaven.” These are statements, ancient and modern, of the great significance of the village drinking ceremony. This observance is the foundation of a true king’s transformation of the people through the Way. Our dynasty has shown it the utmost esteem. If those charged with promulgating it locally could all give weight to virtue and make reverence the essence of ritual, like Huang Ba and Liu Yi, the village drinking ceremony would be conducted with solemnity, and people in villages and towns would honor virtue and respect age. Once villages and towns were transformed, all under Heaven would follow. How could frivolity and obstinacy fail to be reformed?

Ah! The Way does not always depend on laws for its establishment, but laws have never been independent of people. If there are the right people, then…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
行法有關於道而人有重於法也如是哉
故王者以人事天則得天三光全而寒暑
時大臣以人事君則忠君百官正而萬民
理人乎人乎其天地之心國家之本氣化
之原不可一日而無者乎愚生請以是爲
終篇復惟執事其採擇之
punctuated: 行。法有關於道，而人有重於法也，如是哉！故王者以人事天，則得天，三光全而寒暑時；大臣以人事君，則忠君，百官正而萬民理。人乎！人乎！其天地之心、國家之本、氣化之原，不可一日而無者乎！愚生請以是爲終篇，復惟執事其採擇之。
translation_en: …are put into effect. Laws bear upon the Way, yet worthy men carry greater weight than laws: such indeed is the case! Thus, when a king employs worthy men in serving Heaven, he gains Heaven’s favor: the three luminaries—the sun, moon, and stars—remain whole, and cold and heat arrive in their proper seasons. When a great minister employs worthy men in serving his ruler, he fulfills his loyalty to the ruler: the hundred officials are upright, and the myriad people are well governed. Worthy men! Worthy men! Are they not the heart of Heaven and Earth, the foundation of the state, and the source of the transformations of vital force, indispensable for even a single day? This humble student begs to conclude his essay with these words, and once more asks that you, honored examiners, select whatever in them merits acceptance.

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試録後序
山東古齊魯名邦走
京師才數千舍餘衣被
皇明詩書仁義之澤百年於茲如
金既冶如泥既鈞成周之風
宛然目前固宜夫士多學古
而志在澤物有聲於時者相
===
後先也玄錫恒竊願遊歷其
間拜孔子之堂躡岱宗之顛
從今之君子而問學焉久矣
成化癸卯秋適山東大比巡
按監察御史宋經暨藩臬重
臣預聘四方之儒以司文衡
而濫及於玄錫不遠數千里
punctuated:
山東鄉試録後序

山東，古齊魯名邦，走京師才數千舍餘，衣被皇明詩書仁義之澤百年於茲。如金既冶，如泥既鈞，成周之風宛然目前。固宜夫士多學古而志在澤物，有聲於時者相後先也。

玄錫恒竊願遊歷其間，拜孔子之堂，躡岱宗之顛，從今之君子而問學焉，久矣。成化癸卯秋，適山東大比，巡按監察御史宋經暨藩臬重臣預聘四方之儒以司文衡，而濫及於玄錫，不遠數千里
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

Shandong, the renowned land of ancient Qi and Lu, lies only a little over several thousand travel stages [?] from the capital. For a hundred years now, it has enjoyed the beneficent influence of the August Ming: the teachings of the Odes and Documents, benevolence and righteousness. Like metal already smelted and clay already shaped on the potter’s wheel, it displays before our very eyes the customs of the perfected Zhou order. It is fitting indeed that many of its scholars study antiquity and aspire to benefit others, and that men renowned in their own time emerge one after another.

I, Xuanxi, have long cherished the wish to travel there, pay homage in the hall of Confucius, ascend the summit of Daizong, and seek learning from the gentlemen of the present day. In the autumn of the guimao year of Chenghua [1483], Shandong was holding its triennial Provincial Examination. Investigating Censor Song Jing, serving as regional inspector, together with the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, engaged scholars from all quarters in advance to judge the examination writings. Their invitation undeservedly extended even to me, Xuanxi, undeterred by a distance of several thousand li …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
致僅饒陽玄錫既拜使者之
辱欣然就傳至則聞小試甚
嚴且公而就比者尚千二百
有奇心復偉之既而連得其
所爲文閱焉就其中而拔其
尤者則雅者深如精者粟如
浩乎有氣之作人也蔚乎有
===
來之粲目也鏗乎金聲之擲
地也健且著焉如萬馬之奔
而辯駁也博且約焉如萬水
之折而必東也文章之盛曠
萬古而僅一見也玄錫傾心
於往素者固已不待歷其閾
覿其人而其所以學所以蘊
punctuated: 致僅饒陽。玄錫既拜使者之辱，欣然就傳。至則聞小試甚嚴且公，而就比者尚千二百有奇，心復偉之。既而連得其所爲文閱焉，就其中而拔其尤者，則雅者深如，精者粟如，浩乎有氣之作人也，蔚乎有來之粲目也，鏗乎金聲之擲地也。健且著焉，如萬馬之奔而辯駁也；博且約焉，如萬水之折而必東也。文章之盛，曠萬古而僅一見也。玄錫傾心於往素者，固已不待歷其閾、覿其人，而其所以學、所以蘊
translation_en:
…reaching Raoyang [?]. I, Xuanxi, respectfully acknowledged the honor of the envoy’s visit and gladly took the post carriage. Upon arriving, I learned that the preliminary examination had been most rigorous and impartial, yet those presenting themselves for the Provincial Examination still numbered over twelve hundred. I was again greatly impressed. Soon afterward, I received their compositions in succession and read them, selecting the outstanding pieces from among them. The elegant ones were profound; the refined ones were like grains of millet [?]. Their expansive vigor stirred the spirit; their luxuriant richness dazzled the eyes [?]; their ringing tones were like metal striking the ground. Vigorous and lucid, they resembled ten thousand horses galloping, with arguments contending [?]; broad in learning yet concise, they resembled ten thousand streams that, however winding their courses, inevitably flow eastward. Such a flourishing of literary composition is scarcely seen once in all the ages.
What I, Xuanxi, had long yearned for could thus be attained without crossing their thresholds or meeting them in person: that by which they learned and that which they stored within…

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
蓄一旦而盡得之顧非願邪
雖然玄錫之所見者文也夫
者道之器而行則器之實也
文與行固不可偏廢孔子曰
文莫吾猶人也躬行君子則
吾未之有得諸士子其尚躬
行君子之道而務於有得哉
===
山東故多君子不可以屈指
數若王文正公曾三試名皆
第一或者戲其喫着不盡曾
曰平生志不在溫飽旣其貴
也如其言乾興初正色立朝
淸嚴可憚時倚重焉卒之屛
謂除恭成仁祖太平之治若
punctuated:
蓄，一旦而盡得之，顧非願邪？雖然，玄錫之所見者文也。夫者，道之器，而行則器之實也。文與行固不可偏廢。孔子曰：「文莫吾猶人也，躬行君子，則吾未之有得。」諸士子其尚躬行君子之道，而務於有得哉！

山東故多君子，不可以屈指數。若王文正公曾，三試名皆第一。或者戲其喫着不盡，曾曰：「平生志不在溫飽。」旣其貴也，如其言。乾興初，正色立朝，淸嚴可憚，時倚重焉。卒之屛謂除恭，成仁祖太平之治。若
translation_en:
…what they have stored within themselves—to grasp it all in a single day: is this not what I have wished for? Nevertheless, what I, Xuanxi, have seen is their writing. Now, [writing?] is the vessel of the Way, while conduct is the substance within that vessel. Neither writing nor conduct may be neglected. Confucius said: “In literary learning, perhaps I am like other men; but as for personally practicing the conduct of a gentleman, I have not yet attained it.” May you candidates personally practice the Way of the gentleman and strive to attain it!

Shandong has long had more gentlemen than one could count on one’s fingers. Take Wang Zeng, posthumously honored as Duke Wenzheng: he ranked first in all three examinations. Someone once teased him that he would never exhaust his supply of food and clothing. Zeng replied: “My lifelong ambition is not merely to be warm and well fed.” Once he attained high office, he lived up to his words. At the beginning of the Qianxing reign period, he stood at court with an upright demeanor; his integrity and sternness inspired awe, and great reliance was placed upon him. Ultimately, by ousting Wei and removing Gong [apparently Ding Wei and Lei Yungong; transcription doubtful], he helped bring about the peaceful rule of Emperor Renzong. Someone like …

title: 成化十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
曾庶乎學孔子而躬行者也
之諸士子生長是邦其志曾之
志而允迪之哉若或以科目
爲登進之階惟利有官序而
已他日備位百司薦列台鼎
勢可奪焉利可襲焉威可怵
焉使行與言戾終與始違非
===
玄錫所以望於諸士子也幸
相與勉旃
江西饒州府德興縣儒學敎
諭羅玄錫謹序
punctuated:
曾庶乎學孔子而躬行者也。之諸士子，生長是邦，其志曾之志而允迪之哉！若或以科目爲登進之階，惟利有官序而已，他日備位百司，薦列台鼎，勢可奪焉，利可襲焉，威可怵焉，使行與言戾，終與始違，非玄錫所以望於諸士子也。幸相與勉旃！
江西饒州府德興縣儒學敎諭羅玄錫謹序。
translation_en:
…Zeng may be considered one who studied Confucius and personally put his teachings into practice. You students [?], born and raised in this land, should surely embrace Zeng’s aspirations and faithfully follow them! If, however, you regard the examinations as a ladder to advancement, seeking only the advantage of official rank [?], then someday, when you occupy posts in the various offices and rise to the ranks of the highest ministers, power may deflect your resolve, profit may assail you, and threats may intimidate you, making your conduct contradict your words and your end depart from your beginning. This is not what I, Xuanxi, hope for you students. May you encourage one another in this endeavor!
Preface respectfully written by Luo Xuanxi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Dexing County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.
